This is the fourth in a series of Imagine Bestiary Expansions.  The Imagine Bestiary: Mysteries of the Planes leaves 
the natural universe and explores the inner planes, along with their struggles, influences, and exploration leading to 
greater dangers and rewards.  
This volume expands play for the Game Master and player alike.

===== PAGE 6 =====
iv
his is the fourth bestiary for the Imagine Role Playing system. It takes the players into new realms: the 
inner planes. These planes are found closest to the natural universe and are not controlled directly by 
deities. Raging with conflict yet ripe for exploration, the inner planes are a diverse new playground, 
from the Veil of Dreams where exists anything that can be imagined, to the otherworldly demiplanes 
of Phase and Shadow that brush against the natural universe. 
War is always brewing in the planes, whether it is slow and covert between eternal entities of tremendous power, 
or a series of cataclysms, shattering the planar boundaries, and reshaping the multiverse. 
The planes are home to all manner of beings, each with their own agenda and ultimate goals—from the 
elemental primes vying for control to the Queen of Illusion and King of Nightmare battling in the Veil of 
Dreams. Unlike in the natural universe, where good and evil are the strongest indicators of ideology, order 
and chaos vie for control in the inner planes. Order is ever working toward a triumphant perfection of balance 
in the multiverse, while chaos seeks to bring that perfection down and reshape it as the individual sees fit. 
When visiting inner planes, characters must choose well their actions, for consequences are far reaching and 
long lasting. By freeing a group of Djinn, one may ultimately change the power structure within the Plane of 
Air, allowing the Chaotic Air Elementals (magic) to gain ascendency and deposing the Order Air Elementals 
(divinity), thus placing a Chaos Air Prime where once an Order Air Prime ruled. 
But not all is so dire. Although the elemental planes are engaged in constant conflict, they are balanced in such 
a way as to be navigable for the properly protected planes traveler. The Planes of Fire, Water, Earth, and Air bear 
a wonder of wyrds (elemental animals) and whylls (elemental plants), as well as elementals of various strengths 
and sizes. Outward from these planes it only gets weirder and wilder. The Veil of Dreams is as malleable as 
a dream itself and has been shaped by true dreamers all over the multiverse. The Plane of the Lost has been 
collecting leftovers and the forgotten since time began. The Fae live in their World Tree sphere, from murky 
islands amidst dark seas at the tree’s roots all the way up to high, leafy branches where warmth from the outer 
sphere fills all with light and life. And down in the cubic plane of Rockholm, Giants and Dwarves struggle 
against eye-terrors, lava worms, and even more astounding monsters. 
Not only can this bestiary be a guide for well-stocked, high title characters, but also for those playing lower title 
scenarios and campaigns. Perhaps lesser planar beings and effects begin to alter the natural world near a planar 
portal. Perhaps wyrds and whylls have been spotted, and travelers are threatened by lesser planar creatures who 
have emerged from that portal. Is this sudden planar opening accidental? Some chance of fate? Or, is it deliberate 
and the lesser beings merely scouts preparing for a deadlier planar invasion force to come? The inner planes can 
add to any adventure at any title. This and more await you as you unravel the Mystery of the Planes.

Heredity  
There are times when the specific attributes of a character’ parents are known. At the discretion of the GM, some 
of the character’s starting attributes can be based on their parent’s attributes or place in society as shown below. 
The rest are determined by environment and rolled or determined as normal.

===== PAGE 8 =====
2
New Races
Many of the races found herein represent ancestors of existing races or planar alternatives. The introduction of these races 
into any setting is completely dependent on the GM’s discretion. While everything is ultimately up to the GM, it is especially 
important here as unrestricted access to these new races can be unbalancing if not used properly. There are times when 
a Djinn, Ifrit, or other planar racial being finds their way into the natural universe, but if this becomes commonplace, 
it can border on the ridiculous in particular settings. However, if the setting is the planes themselves, this can be wildly 
appropriate. 
Included among these new races is the final addition of anthropomorphic animal types (also known as Wild Ones) and 
goblinkin (Geebra, Red Goblins, and Ice Trolls). These are designed to fit right in with existing races and may appear much 
more frequently in a particular GM’s world. A race like Geebra might be very common, whereas Ice Trolls may be found 
only in isolated areas. Wild Ones, along with new Elves and Dwarves, will vary widely from world to world; some settings 
may be heavily populated by these, whereas in others, they barely exist.  
This set of new races, whether ancestral, planar, or expansions, are presented to complete the palette of races from which 
a GM may paint a unique setting. Imagine has a plethora of races available for players and GMs alike. Maybe these races 
inhabit your high fantasy hodge-podge or nexus world. Maybe your setting is a focused one, where elemental races battle 
goblinkin. Or, perhaps your setting is composed entirely of Wild Ones battling for dominance. 
Rather than specifying which race is which type (ancestral, planar, or expansion), it is left to the GM to decide how each 
race fits into their campaign setting. Perhaps in your setting Dao and Ifrit are the ancestors of Dwarves and Djinn, Marid 
the ancestors of Elves, Silver/Shadow Elves unknown or yet to emerge from Elves, and Iron/Stone Dwarves yet to evolve 
from Dwarves. Maybe Crystori are a more advanced form of Planar or vice versa.
Paint your world as you see fit with the now complete spectrum of Imagine fantasy races, and may players always find 
something new and exciting to try.

Brachara
These crab-like beings live in or near the sea. Besides their three pairs of legs, they have two sets of arms—one with claws 
and the other with normal hands, allowing them to use weapons and tools like other humanoids. Brachara tend to scurry 
when moving and can be somewhat slower than other races. They are fierce when challenged, bristling easily and taking 
offense. Though difficult to make friends, they are fiercely loyal to friends and family and are known to face sacrifice well, 
even venturing off on quests of discovery when faced with challenges for which they have no answers. Brachara are a 
surprising race and many underestimate them, only to later discover their tenacity and strength of will.

Grethen
These Fae folk are creatures of grayish green muck and clay. Their hairless skin glistens with a dull sheen, and their large 
eyes are eerie and off-putting. Magically, they are beings of bog, mud, and muck infused with elements of water and earth—
with a touch of the Plane of Shadow. The tales of their origin differ greatly; some say they were made as servitors of ancient 
elves, likely Shadow Elves. Others claim that the Grethen arose spontaneously from a magical accident or from an ancient 
bog infused with magical waters. Today, they are a self-sustaining race, reproducing by budding asexually to produce a small 
form that lies in a magical or sacred muck pond until arising from it a month later. Full-grown Grethen are small in stature, 
similar to Midfolk. They are short lived for Fae, surviving no more than 120 years. Then tend to be Neutral to Neutral Evil.

Gryphara
A proud and aloof people, the Gryphara are an odd mix: a griffin humanoid bearing an eagle’s head, shoulders, and wings, 
with a separate pair of arms that extend from the same shoulders but end in talons. Feathers cover their upper half and in 
a line down their trunk to their mid-torso, but the rest of their bodies are a mix of lion-humanoid, including a lion’s tail 
and raking claws. Although their feathery wings are large and majestic, they can only fly with aid of magic. As a people, 
Gryphara tend to be reclusive; nevertheless, they prove to be fierce friends to their friends of allied races. Gryphara prefer to 
live in towers, cliffs, or at the very least hill homes where they can catch flight easily. Individuals tend to be Neutral to Good 
in alignment.

Hippotara
These Wild Ones are hippopotamus humanoids. They are large beings of approximately Ogre size. They can 
be gruff,  unfriendly and quick to anger.  They do get along with Loxodara and Kerasara, having close ties with 
these larger Wild Ones races. Hippotara are stubborn and hard to control. Their size and thick hide make them 
extremely dangerous opponents. They tend towards Neutrality but individuals of all alignments exist.

Jumara
These giraffe-like Wild Ones are generally a nomadic people, few settling anywhere for long. They inhabit 
grasslands where they love to run. They are also strict herbivores and especially adore sweet fruits and tender 
nuts. Though often on friendly terms with both Cervara and Equara (with whom they share many of their 
temperaments), they have a distinct dislike of Chetahl. Jumara are known for story collecting and trading. They 
are excellent listeners and ferociously faithful, once they overcome their initial distrust. As a race they tend to be 
Neutral to Good alignment.

Kerasara
The Kerasara are Wild Ones who greatly resemble rhinoceroses. As large as Ogres (and a bit smarter), they generally keep 
away from other races and are considered rare in most settings. Though they have some contact with Equara, Cervara, and 
Jumara, they are mistrustful of most other races, even other Wild Ones. Kerasara are stubborn to a fault and easily angered. 
Their imposing horns and thick hide make them extremely dangerous opponents. Unfortunately, their poor eyesight 
reduces their depth perception, which prevents most from wielding missile weapons. They tend to be Neutral as a people.

Lissara
The Lissara are sometimes mistaken for small Saurians or large S’retts, but if one looks carefully, one will notice a less 
pronounced snout and lack of tearing teeth. Lissara do, however, boast a wicked set of claws and are at home in both water 
and on land. True amphibians, Lissara can even regrow lost limbs. Their webbed hands and feet allow them to be excellent 
swimmers. They are a mysterious people, often reclusive, both as a race and as individuals. They can be of any alignment but 
tend towards Neutral.

Loxodara
The Loxodara are a strong and wise people resembling elephantine humanoids. Though slow to anger, they make 
dangerous opponents once riled. These Wild Ones are well regarded by most other Wild Ones, as well as quite a 
few other races. Loxodara make excellent allies and thoughtful companions, and are sometimes the caretakers of 
lost lore or special places. 
They tend to have a hierarchal society and follow leaders almost reverently, making them somewhat more easily 
controlled, though they can be strong-willed in many situations. As a race they tend to be Good, and many 
individuals have either Moral or Order tendencies.

These otter-like Wild Ones are a mirthful and generally happy race. They tend towards playfulness and

Mellivara
Mellivara are tough and hearty like the badgers they resemble. Since they are dwarven in size and frame, it is easy to mistake 
them as furry dwarves from a distance. Nevertheless, the Mellivara are their own people, fiercely individual. They are slow to 
form bonds, but when they do, they are firm and as unyielding as themselves. They are without fear of any kind and cannot 
be made to feel it, even with magical means. The Mellivara survive in many climes and conditions and are as likely to settle 
among other Wild Ones as living as reclusive nomads. Having no specific preference on style of home, some Mellivara even 
dwell in caves. Mellivara are especially resistant to poisons and, to a lesser degree, diseases and being controlled. They tend 
to be Neutral but can be of any alignment.

Nymph
Throughout ancient mythology, Nymphs are found as part of the rich storytelling traditions of many cultures. Among the 
Greeks, they were considered spirits, bound to specific places in nature, such as rivers, springs, groves, forests, and cool 
grottoes. The reality is that these beautiful creatures typically prefer secluded locales and live in small bands with one another. 
It is in these places that they revel in their freedom from “civilized” societies. However, when a lone traveler wanders into their 
dominion, Nymph are generally curious. Stories tell of travelers who wander too closely to these secluded individuals and then 
become infatuated with them. It is said that should a wanderer stumble upon a Nymph, they will lose all sense and be driven 
mad with obsession over these enchanting beings. The truth is not necessarily far from this myth. Since Nymphs cannot breed 
with each other, they must find their potential mates outside of their communities, sometimes targeting travelers. Typically—
but not always—their offspring are pure Nymphs. Once their offspring is born, the traveler is allowed to return to his former 
life, as most Nymphs prefer seclusion. However, others become obsessed over particular individuals and endeavor to subjugate 
them entirely. Some notable members of the Nymph race are the Nereids and Circe as told in Homer’s Odyssey.

Susara
The strong and stubborn Susara are Wild Ones arisen from boars. They are known for their excellent hearing 
and sense of smell. Though they have strong familial and tribal bonds, they lack the manners and bearing of 
other Wild Ones. The Susara’s culture would be barbaric if they did not trade heavily with others. Their large 
tusks allow them to do serious damage at close range or when charging, and their fur is course and their noses 
flattened into a snout. Though they are known for being fair trackers, their fearlessness is well renown. Susara are 
generally of Neutral alignment.

Testudara
These shelled humanoids resembling tortoises emerged from the muck and kept to themselves for so long 
enough that their origins are a mystery, even to themselves, since few records were kept from their earliest 
years. The Testudara’s slowness and generally poor flexibility have led them to linger at the outskirts of the rest 
of the world’s societies. Though Testudara are tough and resilient, they prefer to avoid most conflicts, and as 
such have become taciturn and often times dour. They are warm to their friends and family and are known for 
their reliability and trustworthiness. Most Testudara are Neutral Good in alignment and tend toward passivity, 
although individuals of all alignments exist.

Ursara
The Ursara are humanoid bear-like beings. Unlike the yeti and sasquatch, which only have the fur of bears, these 
beings have the snouts, claws, and size of bears, and in fact are often confused for bears. The Ursara are amazing 
warriors, known for being aggressive and fearless in battle. They also build strong friendships and take care of 
family and friends. Though massive, the Ursara can be stealthy hunters. They are omnivores and eat just about 
anything. Most Ursara are Neutral Good, but those of all alignments can be found.

Wildling
These Fae appear to be bundled wood and twig bound so tightly that no gap can be seen, and with hair and coverings made 
of leaf and flower. Wildlings are magical beings of plant infused with the elements of fire, air, and the Phase Plane. There 
are many conflicting tales of their origins. Some contend that they were created by ancient Elves, perhaps the Silver Elves 
themselves, and others that an Elven mage infused his own life spirit into them. Some even claim that Wildlings arose from 
a magical accident or from an ancient sylvan forest. Despite the legends, everyone agrees that Wildlings are now a full-
fledged race unto themselves. They have two distinct sexes and reproduce by entwining for a week or more to produce a 
bud. This bud separates from the entwined parents and spends its first month in sacred or magical soil until it wakes up. It 
then pulls its roots from the soil and slowly grows as it ages. Wildlings tend to be Neutral to Neutral Good in alignment.

Wolfen
While Grahl are dog-based wild ones, their Wolfen cousins are more wolf-like and much larger. Compared to other Wild 
Ones, Wolfen are much more feral and dangerous. Being fairly barbaric, they generally live in packs or tight-knit family 
groups in modest communities. Though some Wolfen are nomadic, most have laid claim to specific territory that they 
fiercely guard. Because Wolfen packs generally do not form relationships with other packs, they have been unable to group 
together to form a civilization. In fact, Wolfen are so territorial, they consider any outsider (even other Wolfen) who trespass 
into their territory interlopers and will deal with them aggressively. In rare circumstances, when great conflict arises that 
threatens all clans, a great leader will arise who is respected by all and leads them through the conflict. Wolfen occasionally 
trade with other Wild One races (especially Grahl) but are suspicious of civilized peoples, who often confuse them for 
lycanthropes. Wolfen tend to be Neutral as a race with individuals of both Good and Evil alignments.

New Diseases
These new diseases represent plagues and planar 
influence in the earthly realm. Since they all have a 
magical component, anyone affected by these diseases 
will be detectable as magical.
The Fading (Magical)
Type: Blood and skin
Agent: Blood to skin contact
Incubation Period: 1d4 days
Effects
Mild (01-20%): 3d4 days. Fever, 1 level of fatigue, skin 
becomes slightly translucent (-1 Appearance). There 
is a 5% chance per minute (or 10 seconds in combat) 
that whenever something is touched or grasped, the 
hand or contact area will phase and pass through the 
object, phasing back in after 10 seconds (avoiding solid 
objects).
Serious (21-60%): 2d4 weeks. High fever, 1-2(+1) levels 
of fatigue, skin becomes completely translucent (-2 
Appearance) revealing musculature underneath. There 

===== PAGE 61 =====
55
is a 25% chance per minute (or 10 seconds in combat) 
that whenever something is touched or grasped, the 
hand or contact area will phase and pass through the 
object, phasing back in after 10 seconds (avoiding solid 
objects). Once per 6 hours there is a 5% chance the 
being will phase out completely and be trapped in the 
phase plane, unable to return until the disease passes 
or until unphased by magical or divine means. 
Terminal (61-100%): 4d4 weeks. Very high fever, 
1d4+1 levels of fatigue, skin and muscle fiber become 
completely translucent (-4 Appearance) revealing 
internal organs and bones. There is a 50% chance 
per minute (or 10 seconds in combat) that whenever 
something is touched or grasped, the hand or contact 
area will phase and pass through the object, phasing 
back in after 10 seconds (avoiding solid objects). Once 
per 6 hours there is a 5% cumulative chance the being 
will phase out completely and be trapped in the phase 
plane, unable to return even when the disease passes. 
Even if unphased by magical or divine means, the 
being’s entire body remains translucent, and the phase 
plane becomes the being’s home plane.

Incubation Period: 1d4 days
Effects

Night Terror (Magical)
Type: Skin, brain, and nervous system
Agent: Physical contact with a carrier while the carrier 
is dreaming or mental contact with the carrier at any 
time 
Incubation Period: 1-3 days
Effects
Mild (01-20%): 3d4 days. Tossing and turning while

Ravening Haunt in the Plane of Dreams.

Planar Abilities and Disabilities
In places where connections to the inner planes is strong their influences can affect abilities and disabilities beings are exposed 
to. Though all normal ability rules apply, each ability or disability allows a fortune roll (GM discretion). If fail it becomes a 
planar ability/disability. If neither success nor fail it is unchanged. A success equals choice of normal ability/disability or planar. 
The choice of which planar focus can be determined randomly on the Planar Ability/Disability Focus Table or selected by the 
GM.  The GM may determine that the planar influence of a particular plane in certain areas is overpowering and use only that 
planar ability/disability table replacing all added abilities and disabilities, racial or otherwise with the planar ones. 
Ability/Disability Conversion Table
Fortune Roll
Ability/Disability changes
Fail
Normal ability or disability is replaced with a planar ability or disability.
Neither succeed nor fail
Unchanged: Normal ability or disability applies.
Succeed
Choice of normal ability or disability or planar ability or disability.

===== PAGE 69 =====
63
Transcendence 
This is an alternate to Divine Ascension, which is deity advancement beyond 15th Title. 
A player’s character should not under most circumstances advance beyond 15th Title. However, if someone wishes to 
advance, they may choose from two paths. The first path is Divine Ascension, whose requirements and effects are outlined 
in the Master’s Manual, must be sponsored by greater beings and is only available with the support of the worship of lesser 
beings. The second path, however, is Transcendence, which is outlined below. Transcendence advancement effects, listed by 
Title, are identical to those listed in the Master’s Manual, except where noted below.
•	 Enlightened (Title 16-20)
	» Have at least 3 powers
	» Have the ability to plane shift
	» Be permanently mentally linked to a minimum of 1 other being
	» Be immortal through any of a number of methods, magical or otherwise
•	 Ascendant (Title 21-25)
	» Have at least 5 powers
	» Be permanently mentally linked to a minimum of 4 other beings
	» Select a perfecting path: an area of intellectual, personal, or spiritual enlightenment that allows the Ascendant 
the ability to improve both oneself and those to whom the being is linked and with whom the being works (can 
include but is not limited to life, light, oblivion, ending, freedom, truth, love, knowledge, power, perfection, magical 
knowledge, interconnectedness, and unity)
	» Select a plane or part of a plane other than the earthly plane as home (where the being will be banished to)
•	 Prime (Title 26-29)
	» Have at least 7 powers
	» Be permanently mentally linked to a minimum of 100 other beings
	» Be a multi-planar recognized leader or prime in 1 area of intellectual, personal, or spiritual enlightenment
•	 Transcended (Title 30)
	» Have at least 9 internal powers
	» Be permanently mentally linked to a minimum of 1,000 other beings
	» Be the sole multiverse leader in 1 area of intellectual, personal, or spiritual enlightenment
	» Discard the need for a body, even though the Transcended may use one from time to time when interacting with lesser 
beings
	» Make one final choice:
1.	Choice One: Leave-taking. The Transcended transcends completely and breaks all mental and spiritual linkage to 
other beings, leaving behind the entire multiverse (perhaps creating another or rising above or out existence itself).
2.	Choice Two: Total Union. The Transcended becomes a caretaker of the existing multiverse, above it and 
beyond worship. Thereafter, the being intervenes in the area or areas of their intellectual, personal, or spiritual 
enlightenment and is connected to all other beings who pursue the same, either directly through listening of 
thoughts and feelings, or universally, simply by knowing the multiverse’s needs before they occur.

78
Expanded Kinetics
The skills below are expanded from their Player’s Guide forms 
to allow more usage for the kineticist and other practitioners 
of Kinetics Knowledge. Here the original usage and various 
additional uses have been supplied to allow the practitioners of 
Kinetics Knowledge to fulfill a more core role and to match the 
new kinetics skills found in this volume. These new usages apply 
only to practitioners of Kinetics Knowledge; characters with these 
updated skills who do not have Kinetics Knowledge are limited to 
the usages found in the Player's Guide.
CRYOKINESIS
Attributes: Intelligence, Aura		
Rating: 14
Start Bonus: 2d6%		
	
Time: 10 Seconds
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill represents the ability to control and use cold 
temperatures in various ways. 
General Usage: The user concentrates on the desired effect 
and mentally wills it to happen. Unlike spells, the amount of 
Aura needed to create an effect is constant. The Aura from the 
practitioner’s Aura Pool is drained and returns at the user’s Aura 
Regeneration Rate. Note: Class Title in these usages always refers 
to the Class Title of the practitioner, even when the verbiage seems 
to indicate otherwise.  Effect range is 10 ft. per Class Title unless 
otherwise specified.
Chill (10 Aura; +20% modifier, 2 seconds): Reduces air temperature 
by 5 degrees per Class Title in a 10 ft. radius per Class Title, 
centered on the caster.
Cold Blast (18 Aura; -20% modifier, 5 seconds): Creates a cone 5 ft. 
long per Class Title and 2 ft. in diameter per Class Title. All those 
caught within the area of the blast take 1d4 damage per Class Title 
to exposed areas. Exposure consists of an area that has less than 5 
points of armor protection.
Fog Bank (12 Aura; +10% modifier, 5 seconds): Reduces air 
temperature to 5 degrees below the current dew point producing 
fog in a 10 ft. radius per Class Title.  This skill will fail in areas with 
insufficient humidity.  Lasts for 10 minutes per Class Title.
Freeze (14 Aura; no modifier, 2 second): Freezes up to 2’x 2’x 2’ of 
liquid per Class Title. 
Frost (12 Aura; +10% modifier, 5 seconds):  Causes one being or 
object to suddenly drop in temperature; 1d4 damage per Class Title 
in one area and all areas surrounding it. 
Frostbite (20 Aura; -30% modifier, 5 seconds): Fast freezes an area 
causing all affected targets to make a Magic Resistance or suffer a 
level of fatigue per two practitioner titles.  This skill is 20% easier to 
use in areas of dense fog.
Frost Weapon (18 Aura; -20% modifier, 10 seconds): Can be made 
to coat a melee weapon in a frost effect causing 1d4 damage per 
2 Class Titles used in the skill. A warm, inner layer is created on 
the weapon so the weapon itself is unharmed. Magic Resistance 
applies to any targets struck. Those who make their resistance take 
no damage.  The effect lasts 1 target strike per Class Title or 10 
minutes per Class Title, whichever comes first.
Ice Patch (16 Aura; -10% modifier, 5 seconds): Condenses ambient 
humidity in the air to create an ice slick beneath the feet of a 
victim.  The target may make a Magic Resistance to prevent the 
effect.  The target must make an Agility save when moving, or once 
per 10 seconds when attacking, or the target slips and falls on the 
ice. 1d6+1 seconds must be spent to stand and this requires an 
additional Agility save to do so, unless the target moves off the ice 
patch. Insufficient humidity will cause this skill to fail at the game 
master’s discretion.
Ice Trap (15 Aura; -5% modifier, 10 minutes): Creates an area 
which can be no bigger than 5 ft. x 5 ft. per Class Title. This usage 
takes 10 minutes. This area is a set trap that when touched by 
another Aura field will be triggered, causing sprays of freezing 
cold coming up/out from the area trapped. It causes 1d4 magical 
cold damage per Practitioner Title to 1d4 areas struck if a Magic 
Resistance fails, half damage is taken if a Magic Resistance 
succeeds, and no damage is taken if a Magic Resistance succeeds 
by half or less. The trap can only be triggered once. The frost sprays 
can be narrowed or channeled by nozzles, slits, holes, etc. by setting 
the trap below or behind the channeling method. This can cause 
the area affected to narrow to target a specific height or location. 
The Ice Trap will last for 1 hour per Class Title once set. Alternately 
1/10th of a Will Force can be spent to make the trap permanent, 
resetting every 10 seconds once triggered. 
Produce Ice (16 Aura; -10% modifier, 5 seconds): Condenses 
ambient humidity in the air to create up to 1’x 1’x 1’ of ice per Class 
Title in any shape he desires.  If the humidity is too low, a source 
of water must be present.  Range is touch.  Lasts 1 target strike 
per Class Title and lasts no more than 10 minutes per Class Title, 
whichever comes soonest. 
Shelter (20 Aura; -30% modifier, 10 minutes): Creates a shelter 
large enough to house 1 person per Class Title out of ice.  This 
shelter will last for 8 hours before it will begin to melt. Range is 
touch.
Specialization Ability, Storm of Cold (20 Aura; -30% modifier, 10 
seconds): Creates a whirlwind of sleet, ice and snow which has a 
fixed height of 10 ft. and a radius of 2 ft. per Class Title.
The storm causes all who are caught within its radius to suffer the 
following effects:
•	 Make a Magic Resistance or take 1d4 damage per 2 Class Titles 
per 10 seconds to all exposed areas (a body area protected by 
less than five points of armor is considered exposed.) Characters 
wearing metal armor on hands, feet, or head take an additional 
one point of damage per 10 seconds to those areas.
•	 Make a Magic Resistance or be blinded.
•	 Make an Agility save every 10 seconds. A failure indicates the 
being has lost his footing and has fallen to the ground.
•	 Make a Strength save to combat normally. An unsuccessful save 
results in a penalty of -4 to hit and half damage to attacks and 
-20% to all combat skills.
•	 Missile weapons fired within a Storm of Cold always miss their 
target.
•	 Missile weapons fired into the storm have an equal chance of 
striking any being within the area of effect.
Mastery Ability, Mantle of Ice (20 Aura; -30% modifier, 5 seconds): 
Envelops the user’s Aura in ice. In this form the practitioner is 
immune to cold as the spell Endure Cold. Anything entering the 
caster’s Aura while this spell is in effect will take 1d4 points of 
damage per Class Title. This spell also grants Force Armor at 3 
points per Class Title.
Special Use: The practitioner can make a skill roll when forced to 

===== PAGE 85 =====
79
suffer the effects of a cold-based attack or effect. If the skill roll is 
successful, the practitioner gets a +20% to Magic Resistance for 
that attack and any damage from the attack is reduced by -1 per 
die. 
Notes: Beings immune to cold are unaffected by this skill.  All 
other beings must make a Magic Resistance.  If a Magic Resistance 
is made by 1/2 or more, then no damage is applied. If a Magic 
Resistance is made by less than 1/2, then 1/2 damage is dealt. If a 
Magic Resistance is failed, then full damage is applied.
Critical Failure: Skill user is unable to use Cryokinesis for one 
minute and must make a Will Force save or suffer mental fatigue. 
Critical Success: 1/2 Aura requirements.
Repeat Usage: Further usage in a period of one minute requires a 
Will Force save to avoid mental fatigue.
Repeat Failures: Treat three failures in a minute’s time as a critical 
failure.
ELECTROKINESIS
Attributes: Intelligence, Aura		
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: 10 Seconds
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill represents the ability to magically

Regeneration Rate. Note: Class Title in these usages always refers

Ball (18 Aura; no modifier, 10 seconds):  Creates a ball of electricity

areas.  Any area that is protected by less than 5 points of non-metal 
armor protection is considered exposed.  Targets are afforded a 
Magic Resistance to avoid damage.
Bolt (14 Aura; +20% modifier, 5 seconds): Creates a bolt of 
electricity that travels 10 ft. per Class Title in a straight line.  Any 
being struck will take 1d8 damage per Class Title to a random 
area and all areas surrounding it.  The target is afforded a Magic 
Resistance to avoid damage.
Electric Trap (15 Aura; +15% modifier, 10 minutes): Creates an

Shock (12 Aura; +30% modifier, 2 seconds): Sends an electrical

convulse. This has the effect of forcing the target to make a Magic 
Resistance or let go of anything they are holding.  The target must 
be within 15 ft. + 5 ft. per class title.
Static Shield (12 Aura; +30% modifier, 5 second): Causes the

a super insulator, granting immunity to electrical effects.  The

any kinesis per Class Title. Duration is 15 minutes + 5 minutes per

Spark (10 Aura; +40% modifier, 2 seconds): Creates an electrical

Lightning Sphere (20 Aura; -10% modifier, 10 seconds): The

TELEKINESIS
Attributes: Aura, Will Force	 	
Rating: 15
Start Bonus: 2d6%		
	
Time: 5 Seconds
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: The capacity to move objects through magic and 
mental will.
General Usage: The practitioner focuses on any visible object 
weighing up to one pound per Will Force point of the practitioner. 
A skill roll is made to determine if the object can be moved. 
If the skill roll is attained, the object begins moving under the 
control of the skill user. Multiple objects can be controlled, each 
requiring a cumulative +2 rating modifier (-10% bonus) to the skill 
roll.  Failure of any skill roll attempt indicates that all previously 
controlled objects are no longer under control. The object moves at 
a rate of up to 1 ft. per second, per Will Force point. Each minute 
of control drains one Aura temporarily from the skill user (returns 
at the practitioner’s Aura Regeneration Rate; one per hour for 
non-spellcasters). Note: Class Title in these usages always refers to 
the Class Title of the practitioner, even when the verbiage seems 
to indicate otherwise.  Effect range is 10 ft. per Class Title unless 
otherwise specified.
Notes: If line of sight is lost on the object, then the telekinetic link 
is broken and the object plummets. General telekinesis does not 
affect living matter nor possessions held or worn on a living being.
Special Use: If the practitioner has the skill Kinetics Knowledge, 
they have access to several additional effects through Telekinesis.  
The user concentrates on the desired effect and mentally wills it to 
happen.  Unlike casting spells, the amount of Aura needed to create 
an effect is constant.  The Aura is drained from the practitioner’s 
Aura Pool and returns at the user’s Aura Regeneration Rate.  These 
effects may target a being if so specified, though an unwilling 
target is afforded a Magic Resistance.  As a practitioner increases 
in Kinetic ability, they may control multiple objects without 
additional skill rolls.  Also, the weight limit on the General Usage 
changes as follows for those with Kinetics Knowledge, Lore, and 
Mastery:

Break Fall (12 Aura; +15% modifier, 1 second): Allows the 
practitioner to cushion their own fall from any height landing on 
the ground without injury.
Catch (12 Aura; +15% modifier, 1 second): Allows the practitioner 
to catch an object or objects weighing a total of up to 100 lb. per 
Class Title, stops the momentum of the object and allows it to drop 
to the ground.
Deflect (6 Aura; +45%, 5 seconds): Creates a movable invisible 
shield of telekinetic force that can be used to deflect up to 1 
object or projectile per Class Title of the practitioner weighing 
no more than 5 lb. per Class Title.  The shield will dissipate when 
the maximum number of deflections have occurred.  Only one 
projectile can be affected per second, and the practitioner must 
concentrate to keep this effect active. This effect last 10 seconds per 
Practitioner Title.
Flight (12 Aura, +15% modifier, 10 seconds): The practitioner can 
fly in any direction at 3 ft. per Intelligence point per second. The 
practitioner does not need to maintain concentration while flying, 
but still must make Intelligence saves to change directions or make 
any difficult moves. This effect lasts 30 minutes per Class Title. 
Lift (15 Aura, no modifier), 5 seconds: Lifts a being or object and 
suspends it in midair, holding it helpless for a time.  The target 
is considered to be under the effects of the spell Levitate except 
the practitioner and not the person held controls any up or down 
motion. The object or being will remain lifted for 10 seconds per 
Practitioner Title.  At the end of the lift, gravity reasserts its hold 
on the object or being.  The target is afforded a Magic Resistance to 
negate this effect.
Repulsor Trap (15 Aura; no modifier, 10 minutes): Creates an 
area which can be no bigger than 5 ft. x 5 ft. per Class Title. 
This usage takes 10 minutes. This area is a set trap that when 
touched by another Aura field will be triggered, causing a brief 
but powerful repulsion coming up/out from the area trapped. 
It causes an Agility save at -5% per Practitioner Title to avoid 
falling down and a Strength save at -5% per Practitioner Title to 
resist being pushed. The direction pushed is away from the trap 
1d6 feet per Practitioner Title. If the being fails their Agility Save, 
they do not get a Strength Save to avoid being repulsed. The trap 
can only be triggered once. The repulsion can be narrowed or 
channeled by nozzles, slits, holes, etc. by setting the trap below or 
behind the channeling method. This can cause the area affected to 
narrow to target a specific height or location and will now cause 
1d4+1 magical repulsion damage per Class Title in areas struck. 
The Repulsor Trap will last for 1 hour per Class Title once set. 
Alternately 1/10th of a Will Force can be spent to make the trap 
permanent, resetting every 10 seconds once triggered. 
Reflect (16 Aura, -5% modifier, 5 seconds): This effect causes 

===== PAGE 88 =====
82
all missile weapons and missile spells that are targeted at the 
spellcaster to be reflected to the point of origin. The missile or spell 
will hit a random location.  This will reflect any number of spells 
and missiles at any time and takes no concentration on the part of 
the caster once the effect is in place. Missile spells are spells which 
contain “displacement” as one of their types and are cast at the

Slow Fall (8 Aura, +35% modifier, 1 second): Reduces falling

Throw (10 Aura; +25%, 5 seconds): Causes a stationary object

and Strength are applied as though the object had been thrown.  
Should an object used in this manner be affected by Reflection, it is 
propelled back to its origin rather than the practitioner.
Specialization Ability, Telekinetic Storm (18 Aura; -15% modifier,

an area no larger than 10 ft. x 10 ft. x 10 ft. per Practitioner Title 
to be caught up in a swirling telekinetic vortex.  The vortex itself 
is a cylinder with a 10 ft. diameter that extends 15 ft. high.  The

Telekinetic Storm take 1d10 per Class Title to 4d4 randomly 
determined body areas from the swirling debris. GM discretion for

Mastery Ability, Repulsion Shroud (10 Aura, +25% modifier, 5

around themselves, making them immune to telekinetic and 
repulsion effects as the spell Endure Repulsion. Also providing

strikes the barrier requires the opponent to make a Strength save

Class Title away from the barrier.) Missile weapons are caught in

Title.
Critical Success: 1/2 Aura requirements.
Critical Failure: Skill user is unable to use Telekinesis for 1 minute 
and must make a Will Force save or suffer mental fatigue.
Repeat Failure: Treat 3 repeat failures as a Critical Failure.
Traps
Detect, Remove, and Set Wilderness and Urban Traps
In Imagine Role Playing, rangers, rogues, and others who set 
traps have always been encouraged to be creative by describing 
the trap they wish to make and allowing the GM to set its chance 
and difficulty. With the following new descriptions of various 
traps, both the player and GM alike now have a ready reference of 
well-known and often-used traps to choose from. Each has a type, 
difficulty, time to set, means of detection, components necessary 
for creation, manner of triggering, and removal method. Traps fall 
into two categories (wilderness or urban), along with two subtypes 
(mundane or magical). This reference is merely a guide, and many 
more traps can be created by combining elements of these existing 
traps or devising entirely new ones. 
Wilderness (Mundane Traps) 
These are physical traps created with material naturally found 
in the environment or with limited additional resources. It is 
relatively easy to create traps in certain areas like forests and 
scrubland, while proving more difficult in areas such as deserts and 
tundra. 
Hanging Snares
Description: A weight suspended above the snared target falls 
down, pulling both the snare and the target upwards into the 
height. 
This is an easy-to-make trap with few components, most of which 
can readily be found in most forests or scrublands. A Foraging/
Forestry or Survival skill roll is required to find all but the rope 
while in these environments. Sinew can be harvested with 
Butchering from most medium or large animals, and cord can be 
made with Leather Working from most pelts.
Low Hanging Snare
Construction Time: 10 Minutes
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +20%	
Remove: +20% 
Required: 
10’ of thin rope, twine, cord, or sinew (snare)
1 small tree or large object at least 6’ off the ground (height)
1 100 lb. rock or log (weight)
1 small rigid Y stick (trigger)
Bait as desired (increases likelihood of game but not of the trap 
working)
Triggered By: Taking the bait or hitting the snare
Effect: Half Agility save to avoid the snare, otherwise the target is 
lifted off the ground and considered prone
Special Conditions: This snare only lifts up targets who weigh 
less than 50 lb. In this case, there is a 60% chance the target will 
be snared upside-down, which may have a detrimental long-term 
effect.
Special Effect: Beings caught in the snare who weigh between 50 
and 200 lb. must make an Agility save or fall prone. Any attempt 
to untie the snare and stand back up takes 1d6+4 seconds and 
requires a successful Strength save. This trap has no effect on 
targets over 200 lb.

===== PAGE 89 =====
83
Detection: Spotting either the snare, the rope tied to the weight, 
the rope over the height, or the Y-stick trigger
Removal: The rope is carefully untied from the weighted material 
and lowered to the ground. Failure is as Effect or Special Effect, 
depending on the weight of whoever is removing the trap. 
Modifiers: Cover Tracks can help disguise both the snare and the 
weight, removing the +20% detection chance. Furthermore, the 
end of the snare can be replaced by a net to catch multiple targets, 
depending on the size of the net. 
Regular Hanging Snare
Construction Time: 20 Minutes
Set: +10% 	
Detect: +20%	
Remove: +10% 
Required: 
20’ of thin rope, twine, cord, or sinew (snare)
1 small tree or large object at least 12’ off the ground (height)
1 200 lb. rock or log (weight)
1 small rigid Y stick (trigger)
Bait as desired (increased likelihood of game but not of the trap 
working)
Triggered By: Taking the bait or hitting the snare
Effect: Half Agility save to avoid the snare, otherwise the target is 
lifted off the ground and considered prone
Special Conditions: This snare only lifts up targets who weigh 
less than 200 lb. In this case, there is a 60% chance the target will 
be snared upside-down, which may have a detrimental long-term 
effect.
Special Effect: Beings caught in the snare who weigh between 200 
and 400 lb. must make an Agility save at -10% or fall prone. Any 
attempt to untie the snare and stand back up takes 1d6+4 seconds 
and requires a successful Strength save at -10%. This trap has no 
effect on targets over 400 lb.
Detection: Spotting either the snare, the rope tied to the weight, 
the rope over the height, or the Y-stick trigger
Removal: The rope is carefully untied from the weighted material 
and lowered to the ground. Failure is as Effect or Special Effect, 
depending on the weight of whoever is removing the trap.

High Hanging Snare
Construction Time: 30 Minutes
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +20%	
Remove: +0% 
Required: 
36’ of thin rope, twine, cord, or sinew (snare)
1 tree or large object at least 18’ off the ground (height)
1 400 lb. rock or log (weight)
1 small rigid Y stick (trigger)
Bait as desired (increased likelihood of game but not of the trap 
working)
Triggered By: Taking the bait or hitting the snare
Effect: Half Agility save to avoid the snare, otherwise the target is

Special Conditions: This snare only lifts up targets who weigh

Special Effect: Beings caught in the snare who weigh between 400

Removal: The rope is carefully untied from the weighted material

depending on the weight of whoever is removing the trap. 
Modifiers: Cover Tracks can help disguise both the snare and the 
weight, removing the +20% detection chance. Furthermore, the 
end of the snare can be replaced by a net to catch multiple targets, 
depending on the size of the net. 
Spring Snares
Description: Pulling away the trigger releases a spring attached 
to a snare, which constricts the body area touched. The target is 
then flung into the air against the ground on the far side of the 
spring. This is an easy-to-make trap with few components, most 
of which can readily be found in most forests or scrublands. A 
Foraging/Forestry or Survival skill roll is required to find all but 
the rope while in these environments. Sinew can be harvested with 
Butchering from most medium or large animals, and cord can be 
made with Leather Working from most pelts. 
Small Twig Snare
Construction Time: 5 Minutes
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +20%	
Remove: +20% 
Required: 
3’ of thin rope, twine, cord, or sinew (snare)
1 flexible stick or sapling 2-3’ long (spring)
1 small rigid Y stick (trigger)
Bait as desired (increased likelihood of game but not of the trap 
working)
Triggered By: Taking the bait or hitting the snare
Effect: Half Agility save to avoid the snare, otherwise the snare 
constricts a random body area and whips the target into the air 
and against the ground on the far side of the spring. This results in 
1d4+1 damage to both the area constricted and 1d3 other random 
body areas.
Special Conditions: This snare only lifts and slams targets who 
weigh less than 20 lb.
Special Effect: Beings caught in the snare who weigh between 20 
and 200 lb. must make an Agility save or be struck by the spring 
material and either take 1d4+1 damage to a random area or have a 
limb caught in the snare. In the latter case, the target must make a 
second Agility save or fall prone and spend 1d6+4 seconds untying 

===== PAGE 90 =====
84
the snare and standing back up. This trap has no effect on beings 
weighing over 200 lb.
Detection: Spotting either the rope tied to the spring material, the 
snare, or the Y trigger
Removal: The rope is carefully untied from the spring material 
while leaning heavily on it to keep it from triggering. Failure is 
as Effect or Special Effect, depending on the weight of whoever is 
removing the trap. 
Modifiers: Cover Tracks can help disguise the snare, removing 
the +20% detection chance. A flexible spring steel pole can be 
used, increasing the damage to each affected body area to 1d6+2. 
Furthermore, replacing the rope with wire will prevent trapped 
animals from chewing through the rope and escaping.

Deadfall Traps
Description: A weight is propped up, and any target who knocks 
away one of the props causes the weight to fall on top of the target. 
This is an easy-to-make trap with few components, most of which 
can readily be found in most forests or scrublands with a Foraging/
Forestry or Survival skill roll.
Light Deadfall
Construction Time: 5 Minutes
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +20%	
Remove: +20% 
Required: 
2-3 twigs 4-6” long (props)
1 or more rocks weighing a total of 50-100 lb. (deadfall)
A well-used path or animal run 
Triggered By: Knocking away a prop
Effect: Half Agility save to avoid deadfall, otherwise the materials 
fall onto the target and the target takes 2d6+2 damage to 1d4+2 
random areas and is pinned. A Strength save is needed to escape if 

===== PAGE 92 =====
86
the deadfall is under the target’s load limit.  
Special Conditions: This trap only pins targets who are under 2’ 
in height. Any attempt to push away the deadfall and escape takes 
2d6+4 seconds.
Special Effect: Targets on whom the weight falls who are taller 
than 2’ must make an Agility save or become tangled in the 
deadfall materials and fall prone for 1d6+1 seconds.
Detection: Spotting the props holding up the deadfall
Removal: Either the props are knocked away while no one is 
underneath the deadfall, or the deadfall is carefully lowered to the 
ground if within the remover’s load limit (a Strength save must also 
be made). Failure is as Effect or Special Effect, depending on the 
weight of whoever is removing the trap. 
Modifiers: Cover Tracks can help disguise the props, negating the 
+20% detection chance. A board can also be used such that dirt 
can be piled on the board to act as the deadfall. Furthermore, small 
logs can be used instead of rocks if they are of the appropriate 
weight.

Spring-Loaded Spike Traps
Description: Several sharpened stakes are attached crosswise to 
a flexible stick or tree, which is then pulled back like a spring and 
held in place with a rigid Y stick. This stick is tied to a trip wire, 
that when triggered, releases the spiked stick, which slams into the 
target. This is an easy-to-make trap with few components, most 
of which can readily be found in most forests or scrublands. A 
Foraging/Forestry or Survival skill roll is required to find all but 
the rope while in these environments. Sinew can be harvested with 
Butchering from most medium or large animals, and cord can be 
made with Leather Working from most pelts.
Small Spring Spikes
Construction Time: 5 Minutes
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +20%	
Remove: +20% 
Required: 
6’ of thin rope, twine, cord, or sinew (tripwire)
1 flexible stick or sapling 2-3’ long (spring)
3 sharpened stakes 3-4” long (spikes) 
1 small rigid Y stick (trigger)
A well-used path or animal run 
Triggered By: Hitting the tripwire
Effect: Half Agility save to avoid being hit by the spikes attached 
to the spring stick. The spring itself does 1d4+1 smashing damage, 
and the target will also be pierced with 0-3 spikes (1d4-1), each of 
which inflicts an additional 1d6+2 thrusting damage. 
Special Conditions: Since this trap is targeted for small game, the 
trip wire is set low to the ground, and targets taller than 3’ will be 
struck in a lower random body area by the spring and its attached 
spikes. 
Detection: Spotting the tripwire, the spiked spring, or the Y trigger
Removal: The tripwire is carefully untied from the spring stick or 
sapling, and the spring is slowly loosened until fully sprung. Failure 
is as Effect, unless there are no targets in the path of the spiked 
spring.  
Modifiers: Cover Tracks can help disguise the components, 
removing the +20% detection chance. A flexible spring steel pole 
can be used with affixed spikes, increasing the spring’s damage 
to 1d6+2 and each spike to 2d6+4. Wire can replace the rope as 
the tripwire, lowering detection by a further 10%. Poison can be 
painted onto the spikes for added lethality. This trap can also be 
mounted on a tree or other fixed surface off the ground as desired.

Earthen Pits
Description: This trap is trivial to create but takes a fair amount 
of time. A pit is dug out and either left open or covered with a 
woven pile of brush. Pits can also be embellished with spikes at the 
bottom. Those trapped within will either be stuck in the pit, unable 
to climb out, or may die of asphyxiation in an attempt to climb out 
and having the sides of the pit collapse on them. 
Shallow Earthen Pit
Construction Time: 1 hour (can be reduced by 10 minutes per 
additional digger with a tool, up to three total diggers)
Set: +40% 	
Detect: +40%	
Remove: +40% 
Required: 
1 large digging tool (shovel, shield, etc.) 
Earthen area 5’ x 5’ wide and 20’ deep
Triggered By: Falling into the pit
Effect: Agility save to avoid falling into the pit and taking falling 
damage
Special Effect: Targets that fall into the pit can climb out with a 
Climb skill roll, but there is a +5% cumulative chance per skill roll 
attempt that the pit will collapse and bury the target, resulting in 
the possibility of asphyxiation. Any buried targets must make a 
Strength save to dig themselves out.
Detection: Spotting the pit, either uncovered or through a woven 
covering of some kind
Removal: Either the pit is filled in, which takes 30 minutes, or logs/
boards are placed over the hole, which takes 5-10 minutes.  
Modifiers: Cover Tracks can be used to weave a pile of small 
branches, leaves, and grasses as a cover to the pit, reducing the 
detection chance by 20%. Spikes can be placed at the bottom of 
the pit, causing each target to fall onto 0-3 spikes (1d4-1), each of 
which inflicts 3d6+4 thrusting damage. Poison can be painted onto 
these spikes for added lethality.
Earthen Pit
Construction Time: 4 hours (can be reduced by 30 minutes per 
additional digger with a tool, up to four total diggers)
Set: +30% 	
Detect: +40%	
Remove: +20% 
Required: 
1 large digging tool (shovel, shield, etc.) 
Earthen area 10’ x 10’ wide and 40’ deep
Triggered By: Falling into the pit
Effect: Agility save to avoid falling into the pit and taking falling 
damage
Special Effect: Targets that fall into the pit can climb out with a 
Climb skill roll, but there is a +10% cumulative chance per skill 
roll attempt that the pit will collapse and bury the target, resulting 
in the possibility of asphyxiation. Any buried targets must make a 
Strength save at -10% to dig themselves out.
Detection: Spotting the pit, either uncovered or through a woven 
covering of some kind
Removal: Either the pit is filled in, which takes 1 hour, or logs/
boards are placed over the hole, which takes 10-20 minutes.  
Modifiers: Cover Tracks can be used to weave a pile of medium-
sized branches, leaves, and grasses as a cover to the pit, reducing 
the detection chance by 20%. Spikes can be placed at the bottom of 
the pit, causing each target to fall onto 0-3 spikes (1d4-1), each of 
which inflicts 3d6+4 thrusting damage. Poison can be painted onto 
these spikes for added lethality.
Deep Earthen Pit
Construction Time: 12 hours (can be reduced by 1 hour per 
additional digger with a tool, up to six total diggers)
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +40%	
Remove: +0% 
Required: 
1 large digging tool (shovel, shield, etc.) 
Earthen area 10’ x 10’ wide and 60’ deep
Triggered By: Falling into the pit
Effect: Agility save to avoid falling into the pit and taking falling 
damage.
Special Effect: Targets that fall into the pit can climb out with a 
Climb skill roll, but there is a +20% cumulative chance per skill 
roll attempt that the pit will collapse and bury the target, resulting 
in the possibility of asphyxiation. Any buried targets must make a 
Strength save at -20% to dig themselves out.
Detection: Spotting the pit, either uncovered or through a woven 
covering of some kind
Removal: Either the pit is filled in, which takes 1 hour, or logs/
boards are placed over the hole, which takes 10-20 minutes.  
Modifiers: Cover Tracks can be used to weave a pile of large 
branches, leaves, and grasses as a cover to the pit, reducing the 
detection chance by 20%. Spikes can be placed at the bottom of 
the pit, causing each target to fall onto 0-3 spikes (1d4-1), each of 
which inflicts 5d6+6 thrusting damage. Poison can be painted onto 
these spikes for added lethality.

Wilderness (Magical Traps)
These traps rely on special magical or divine skills, spells, 
invocations, or materials, such as spell-casting and magical plants.
Magical Plant Traps
Description: These traps make use of magical and mundane vines, 
grass, bushes, or trees and are usually set along a heavily trafficked 
road, trail, or open area.
Ensnaring Vine
Construction Time: 1 hour + spellcasting (if applicable)
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0% 
Required: 
2 trees, boulders, or structures on which to anchor the ends of the 
vine
Non-magical vine:
1 vine (a successful Plant Growth skill roll may be necessary to 
make the vine long enough for the desired trap area)
The spell Entwine or Plant Move to enchant onto the vine
The spell Delay or Set (optional) to delay the magical effect until 
triggered 
Magical vine:
1 blood or strangler vine (a successful Plant Growth skill roll may 
be necessary to make the vine long enough for the desired trap 
area)
A successful Herb Lore skill roll to carefully trim away the vine’s 
brain bulb and maw area so that the vine is no longer able to move 
or reproduce, but enough of the vine is left to cause entanglement.
Triggered By: Touching the vine
Effect: Agility save to avoid lower limbs being entangled by the 
vine, and a Strength save every 5 seconds to escape any resulting 
entanglement
Special Effect: Targets who weigh less than 150 lb. must make a 
second Strength save if entangled or fall prone. 
Detection: Spotting the vine twitch unexpectedly (if using a blood 
or strangler vine) or with a combination of Detect Trap, Detect 
Magic, and Herb Lore
Removal: The vine must be carefully cut away from its anchors 
and then chopped up or burned. Alternatively, the enchantment or 
innate magical ability may simply be dispelled.
Modifiers: Cover Tracks can help disguise the vine, lowering 
the detection chance by 10%. Strangler vines cause the following 
additional effect: Vine Constriction (5 seconds, 2d6+2 constriction 
per 5 seconds). Blood vines cause the following additional effects: 
Vine Constriction (5 seconds, 2d6+2 constriction per 5 seconds), 
Vine Whip with razor leaves (3 seconds, 3d4+2 cutting; since this 
damages the vine, any further attacks with the same leaves will spray 
an additional magical acid sap for 1d10 per hit).  
Enveloping Grass
Construction Time: 1 hour + spellcasting (if applicable)
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +10%	
Remove: -10% 
Required: 
Non-magical grass:
An area of grass with a 15-18’ circumference and whose roots are 
torn away from the dirt underneath so that it resembles a grassy 
rug (a successful 
   Plant Growth skill roll may be necessary to make the grassy area 
wide enough for the desired trap area)
The spell Plant Move to enchant onto the grass
The spell Delay or Set (optional) to delay the magical effect until 
triggered 
Magical grass:
1 enveloper grass (a successful Plant Growth skill roll may be 
necessary to make the grassy area wide enough for the desired trap 
area)
A successful Herb Lore skill roll to carefully slice off the grass’s 
nerve nodules every 1 to 2 inches while leaving the nerve fibers 
still connected, so that the grass will still envelop but can neither 
constrict nor absorb flesh
Triggered By: Touching any area within 1’ of the grassy area’s 
center
Effect: The grass suddenly folds into a ball around the victim. The 
grassy ball can then roll at a rate of 5’ per second in a direction 
controlled by the enveloper grass, or at a rate of 30’ per second 
in a direction controlled by the enchanter if using non-magical 
grass. Any attempt to escape from within the grassy ball requires 
an Agility save to retrieve small cutting weapons (under 2’ long) 
and a two successful Strength saves at -20% (5 seconds each). If 
the victim is unable to escape, whoever set the trap can tickle the 
enveloper’s nerve fibers in such a way as to release the victim, or 
another being may attempt to do this with a successful Herb Lore 
skill roll. 
Detection: For enveloper grass, the trap will be detected by 
spotting darker than normal grass that doesn’t seem to sway with 
the breeze. It can also be detected with a combination of Detect 
Magic and Herb Lore. For non-magical grass, the trap is detected 
upon realizing a large section of grass has been torn from the 
underlying dirt, and a combined Detect Magic and Detect Trap will 
confirm suspicions that this is a trap.
Removal: Bait must be given so that the enveloper grass activates, 
and then the purple veins (nervous system) must be scraped away 
in the center to keep it from enveloping again. Alternatively, the 
enchantment or innate magical ability may simply be dispelled.
Modifiers: Cover Tracks can help disguise the grassy area with 
debris, lowering the detection chance by 10%. To retain an 
enveloper grass’s Constriction ability, remove only half of the nerve 
bundles (the required Herb Lore skill roll is at -10%). The trap 
then gains the following effect: Constriction (5 seconds, 3d6+3 
constriction per 5 seconds).

Grabbing Limbs
Construction Time: 10 minutes + spellcasting
Set: +0% 	Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0%
Required: 
1 bush or tree
The spell Entwine to enchant onto the plant
The spell Delay or Set to delay the magical effect until triggered 
The spell Plant Move to make the plant mobile (optional)
Triggered By: Any target considered an enemy coming within 
range of the plant (either the maximum length of the plant’s limbs 
or 3’ per Aura used in the Entwine enchantment) 
Effect: The bush or tree reaches out in an attempt to grab the target 
and hold them in place. A roll to hit must be made for each part 
of the plant attempting to grab an enemy vs. a 10, as per standard 
combat grappling.
Special Conditions: Chance of grabbing and then holding are 
based on the size of the plant being used:

Entangling: The chance per 10 seconds of grabbing the victim if 
they are within range of the plant
Holding: The chance of holding the victim per combat round minus

Detection: The trapping plant may be detected as a delayed, set, or 
enchanted magical effect that has not yet been triggered).
Removal: The only sure way to remove the trap is by dispelling the

removal of the magical effect, it can be used to mark the area that

Modifiers: The plant can be directed ahead of time to entangle a 
target and then move them to a certain location and hold them 
there or release them into another trap or holding area. The spells 
Glamour or Non-Detection can be used to hide this magical trap, 
but a successful Detect Trap skill roll after a Detect Magic or Detect 
Aura will reveal that something seems “off” with no additional 
clarity. If Glamour was used and the searcher asks for and makes 
an Illusion Resistance, they will see through the illusion and detect 
the plant trap. 
Magical Earth and Rock Traps
Description: These traps use spells that alter the natural 
environment through use of set or delayed spells, such as pits 
appearing under one’s feet or rocks suddenly rolling down an 
incline.
 
Vanishing Ground
Construction Time: 5 minutes + spellcasting
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0%
Required: 
An earthen patch of ground large enough to encompass the pit’s 
desired dimensions
The spell Dig to enchant onto the earth
The spell Delay or Set to delay the magical effect until triggered
The spell Produce Earth to bury any victims who fall into the pit 
(optional)
Triggered By: Any being with an Aura field walking into the center 
of the Dig spell area 
Effect: Agility save at -20% to avoid falling into a pit that suddenly 
opens and taking falling damage. The pit’s size and dimensions 
are based on the Dig spell, and the falling distance determines any 
resulting damage. The target may not make a Magic Resistance to 
avoid this effect, since the Dig spell is set to activate slightly below 
the target’s Aura field (this removes most of the dirt under the 
target, causing the rest to fall in).
Special Effect: Targets that fall into the pit can climb out with a 
Climb skill roll, but there is a +5% cumulative chance per skill roll 
attempt that the pit will collapse and bury the target, resulting in 
the possibility of asphyxiation. Any buried targets must make a 
Strength save to dig themselves out.
Detection: The enchanted ground may be detected as a delayed, 
set, or enchanted magical effect that has not yet been triggered. 
The spells Glamour or Non-Detection can be used to hide the 
Vanishing Ground trap, but a successful Detect Trap skill roll after 
a Detect Magic or Detect Aura will reveal that something seems 
“off” with no additional clarity. If Glamour was used and the 
searcher asks for and makes an Illusion Resistance, they will see 
through the illusion and detect the trap.
Removal: The only sure way to remove the trap is to dispel the 
magic of the Dig spell (dispelling the Set spell will activate the 
trap). Although the skill Remove Trap does not function without 
removal of the magical effect, it can be used to mark the outline of 
the area to avoid.
Modifiers: The spell Produce Earth may be added as a second 
effect, set to appear once the Dig spell activates. Produce Earth 
must be cast on a ramp leading into the pit about 10’ up from 
the bottom (this causes any targets to be unable to make a Magic 
Resistance). The newly produced dirt will roll down the ramp and 
bury the trapped victims who must make both a Strength and 
Agility save once per minute to dig upwards 5’. After 3 minutes of 
being buried, targets begin asphyxiating.

The spell Produce Stone to create a rock
The spell Delay or Set to delay the magical effect until triggered 
Triggered By: Any being with an Aura field walking within range

The Howler
Construction Time: 10 minutes + spellcasting
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0%
Required: 
A natural object (i.e. stone, pine cone, mushroom, etc.)
The spell Alarm or Produce Sound to cast onto the object
The spell Produce Scent to cast onto the object (optional)
The spell Delay or Set to delay the magical effect until triggered
Triggered By: Any being with an Aura field walking within range 
of the triggered object
Effect: An animal cry suddenly sounds from the triggered object, 
which potentially calls a predator to the location. If within range, 
the trap setter will also hear the animal cry and know his trap has 
been triggered). 
Detection: The triggered object can be detected as a delayed, set, 
or enchanted magical effect that has not yet been triggered. Detect 
Trap must first be combined with some form of Detect Magic or 
Detect Aura to see the area that will trigger the effect. The spells 
Glamour or Non-Detection can be used to hide the triggered 
object, but a successful Detect Trap skill roll after a Detect Magic 
or Detect Aura will reveal that something seems “off” with no 
additional clarity. If Glamour was used and the searcher asks for 
and makes an Illusion Resistance, they will see through the illusion 
and detect the trap.
Removal: The only sure way to remove the trap is to dispel the 
magic of the Alarm or Produce Sound spell (dispelling the Set spell 
will activate the trap). Although the skill Remove Trap does not 
function without removal of the magical effect, it can be used to 
mark the outline of the area to avoid.
Modifiers: Produce Sent can be added to spray the scent of a 
delectable prey onto anyone setting off the trap, further enticing a 
predator to hunt down the target.
Urban (Mundane Traps): 
These physical and mechanical traps, created from 
manufactured pieces and weapons, are created to work 
in an urban environment. They are often set in hidden 
compartments to further confuse and endanger their 
intended targets. Because of the mechanical nature of these 
traps, the activating mechanism does not have to be a trip 
wire or pressure plate but rather a doorknob, lever, button, 
loose stone, etc. None of these will add to the cost, only the 
reusability and novelty of these traps. 
Hidden Weapon Traps
Description: When triggered, these traps activate a hidden weapon 
of some kind (crossbow, spear, blade, etc.), which shoots or swings 
at whoever is standing in its path.
Bolt Trap
Construction Time: 15 minutes
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +10%	
Remove: -10%
Required:
1 crossbow (weapon)
1 4-6’ wire or cord (tripwire)
1 fixed object to which the weapon will be affixed (stand)
1 fixed object to which the tripwire will be attached (anchor)
1 crossbow bolt (projectile)
Triggered By: Hitting the tripwire, which pulls the trigger on a 
loaded crossbow
Effect: Agility save (with penalties if applicable) to avoid being 
struck with a crossbow bolt in a body area that lies in the bolt’s 
path and taking the following piercing damage:
• Hand crossbow: Agility save or take 3d6 damage
• Normal Crossbow: Agility save at -10% or take 6d6 damage
• Heavy Crossbow: Agility save at -20% or take 9d6 damage
Detection: Spotting either the tripwire or the hidden crossbow
Removal: Carefully cut or remove the tripwire. If the crossbow is 
reachable, remove the bolt carefully. If a full crossbow was used 
in the making of the trap, it can be detached from the stand (and 
untied from the tripwire) with a critical success. 
Modifiers: Base costs for a Fixed Bolt trap are 45 gold (low), 60 
gold (medium), or 80 gold (high), plus the cost of the crossbow. 
A crossbow can be rigged as a trap hastily (in 5 minutes) without 

===== PAGE 98 =====
92
the additional cost, but then every time it is used, there is a 5% 
chance it will misfire (each with a 10% chance of breaking some 
part of the mechanism). Heavy, barbed, or piecing bolts can be 
loaded to increase damage. Poison can be coated onto the tip 
for added lethality. A pressure plate can be used and attached to 
a weighted system in place of a tripwire, reducing the detection 
chance to +0% but increasing the cost by 25% and the setup time 
by 1 hour. The crossbow can be placed behind a wall with a small 
slit for loading and unloading for an additional 10% cost. The 
crossbow can be stripped down into just the firing mechanism 
and fitted permanently into the stand to reduce crossbow costs by 
50%, but this adds 1 hour to the setup time. A secret compartment 
that hides the entire mechanism until it fires can be added for an 
additional 25% of the cost, reducing detection by 20%. A weighted 
reloading system can be added for an additional 10% cost, resulting 
in a limited number of possible reloads before the ammunition 
runs out.
Heavy Bolt Trap
Construction Time: 30 minutes
Set: +10% 	
Detect: +20%	
Remove: -20%
Required: 
1 ballista (weapon)
1 12’ wire or cord (tripwire)
1 fixed object to affix the weapon to (stand)
1 fixed object to which the tripwire will be attached (anchor)
1 ballista bolt (projectile)
Triggered By: Hitting the tripwire, which pulls the fire mechanism 
on a loaded ballista
Effect: Agility save (with penalties if applicable) to avoid being 
struck with a crossbow bolt in a body area that lies in the bolt’s 
path. If struck, the resulting piercing damage is as follows:
• Light Ballista: Agility save at -30% or take 12d6 damage
• Normal Ballista: Agility save at -40% or take 15d6 damage
• Heavy Ballista: Agility save at -50% or take 18d6 damage
Detection: Spotting either the tripwire or the hidden ballista
Removal: Carefully cut or remove the tripwire. If the ballista is 
reachable, remove the bolt carefully. If a full ballista was used in the 
making of the trap, it can be detached from the stand (and untied 
from the tripwire) with a critical success.
Modifiers: Base costs for a fixed Heavy Bolt Trap are 135 gold 
(low), 180 gold (medium), or 240 gold (high), plus the cost of the 
ballista. A ballista can be rigged as a trap hastily (in 10 minutes) 
without the additional cost, but then every time it is used, there is 
a 10% chance it will misfire (each with a 20% chance of breaking 
some part of the mechanism). Heavy, barbed, or piecing bolts can 
be loaded to increase damage. Poison can be coated onto the tip 
for added lethality. A pressure plate can be used and attached to 
a weighted system in place of a tripwire, reducing the detection 
chance to +0% but increasing the cost by 25% and the setup time 
by 2 hours. The ballista can be placed behind a wall with a slit for 
loading and unloading for an additional 10% cost. The ballista 
can be stripped down into just the firing mechanism and fitted 
permanently into the stand to reduce ballista costs by 50%, but this 
adds 2 hours to the setup time. A secret room that hides the entire 
mechanism until it fires can be added for an additional 25% of the 
cost, reducing detection by 20%. A weighted reloading system can 
be added for an additional 20% cost, resulting in a limited number 
of possible reloads before the ammunition runs out.
Blade Trap
Construction Time: 30 minutes
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +0%	
Remove: 0%
Required: 
1 blade for each slit (weapon)
1 gear welded to each blade (spin gear)
1 8’ wire or cord per blade (weight wire)
2 heavy weights attached to each weight wire (weights)
1 gear wound by rolling up the weight wire into it (weight gear)
1 6’ wire or cord (tripwire)
1 fixed object to attach the tripwire to (anchor)
1 release that attaches the tripwire to the anchor (release)
Steps to creating: Create slits in a stone or wooden panel. Attach the 
release to the anchor. Attach one end of the tripwire to the release 
and the other end to both weight gears. Wind up the weight wires 
on these weight gears. Attach weights to the weight wires. Attach 
the weight gears to the spin gear, which causes the blade to spin out 
of its slit and strike a target.
Triggered By: Hitting the tripwire, which releases the weights, 
which pull the gears, which spin the blades out of their slits
Effect: Agility save (with bonuses if applicable) to avoid being 
struck by the blades in a body area that lies in each blade’s path. 
Damage is based on the size of each blade and how heavy the 
weights are (see below). 
Detection: Sotting either the tripwire or a hidden blade
Removal: Carefully cut or remove the tripwire, or plug the blade 
slits. 
Modifiers: Base costs for a Blade Trap are 30 gold (low), 40 gold 
(medium), or 60 gold (high), plus the cost of each blade. Damage 
and cost are based on the size and number of blades and the 
weights used: heavier weights do more damage but take longer 
to swing, giving a better chance to avoid with an Agility save (see 
below). A pressure plate can be used and attached to a weighted 
system in place of a tripwire, reducing the detection chance but 
increasing the cost by 25% and the setup time by 2 hours. Poison 
can be coated onto the blades for added lethality. An automatic 
gear and weight system that will reset the trap after a set time can 
be added at +50% of the cost of the trap.

Structure Traps
Description: When triggered, these traps activate walls, ceilings, 
floors, stairs, etc. that fall or disappear. Though relatively easy to 
prepare, they take a long time to set up.

Stone Pit
Construction Time: 8 hours per 10’
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +20%	
Remove: +0%
Required: 
Enough stone to either cut away a new pit or to line an existing pit
Triggered By: Falling into the open pit in dim lighting or darkness
Effect: Agility save or fall into the pit and take falling damage
Detection: Either feeling or seeing the mouth of the pit in dim 
lighting or darkness (+50% when in bright lighting)
Removal: Cover the pit mouth with something that allows a safe 
crossing, such as boards.  
Modifiers: Base costs for a Stone Pit trap are by 10 cubic foot 
increments: 50 gold (low), 65 gold (medium), or 90 gold (high). 
A false floor can be added that gives way under a certain pre-set 
weight, reducing the pit’s detection chance to 0% and increasing 
the cost of the first 10 cubic feet by 25% per use. A hinged, 
resettable false floor costs 50% more for the first 10 cubic feet, and 
a counterbalanced version that resets automatically in 1 minute is 
double the cost of the first 10 cubic feet. When stepping onto this 
false floor’s edge, an Agility save is needed to avoid falling into the 
pit. This save is at -20% if stepping onto the false floor’s middle. 
Furthermore, the pit sides may be smoothed or even greased to 
make climbing out difficult or near impossible. Iron or steel spikes 
can also be added to the pit bottom and inflict damage based on 
the amount and size of the spikes (see below). Poison can be coated 
onto the spikes for added lethality.
