Stone Chute
Construction Time: 8 hours per 10’ of chute
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +20%	
Remove: +0%
Required: 
Enough stone to either cut away a new chute or to line an existing 
chute
1 slab of very thin stone or veneer meant to break or 1 hinged thick 
slab of stone meant to fall away (false floor) 
Steps to create: Excavate a multilevel stone layout so that targets 
have somewhere to be dropped. Polish the sides so they are nearly 
impossible to climb back up without special gear. Set the false floor 
over the opening, either lying across (if very thin) or hinged (if 
thick stone).
Triggered By: Stepping onto the false floor
Effect: Agility save or fall into the chute and slide to its destination. 
Success indicates the target successfully jumps free or grabs an 
edge. Targets standing on the false floor who are further than 5’ 
from its edge do not get a save to avoid falling into the chute. The 
first 10’ of the chute is generally straight down, then curves to its 
intended destination.
Special Effect: Damage taken is entirely dependent on where 
the targets end up. They could be thrown out a high cliff/wall to 
their automatic deaths or deposited into a water hole and take no 
damage. Targets will take falling damage according to distance 
of the final section, if it is a straight drop, as well as the type of 
material they land on (see Master’s Manual).
Detection: Either by spotting the false floor’s outline or noticing a 
slight give
Removal: Either cover the false floor with something that allows a 
safe crossing or use spikes to keep it from opening.  
Modifiers: Base costs for a Stone Chute trap are by 10 cubic foot 
increments: 50 gold (low), 75 gold (medium), or 100 gold (high). 
The basic fall away floor is a single-use veneer that breaks and falls 
down the chute with the target(s). A hinged, resettable version 
costs 50% more for the first 10 cubic feet, and a counterbalanced 
version that resets automatically in 1 minute costs double that of 
the first 10 cubic feet. Grease sprayers can be added to the chute 
at a cost of 10% per 10’ and can be reset by being lowered into the 
chute and squeezing new or recovered grease back into the spray 
holes.
Falling Portcullis
Construction Time: 6 hours
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +0%	
Remove: -20%
Required: 
1 portcullis, mounted above the falling area in a seam with runners 
to the floor and holes in the floor for the portcullis’s spikes to rest 
in when dropped (portcullis)
2 12’ wires or cords (tripwire, weight wire)
1 set of counterbalances weighing slightly more than the portcullis 
(weights)
1 fixed object to which the tripwire will be attached (anchor)
1 release that attaches the tripwire to the anchor (release)
Steps to create: Attach the release to the anchor, then one end of 
the tripwire. Attach one end of the weight wire to the weights and 
the other end of the portcullis. Make a Strength save to raise the 
portcullis into place. Attach the other end of the tripwire to the 
weights, holding them down until released. To reset this trap, make 
a Strength save to carefully pull the tripwire until the weights hit 
the floor and the portcullis is again aloft, then reattach the tripwire 
to the release.
Triggered By: Hitting the tripwire, which pulls the release 
mechanism that drops the portcullis
Effect: The portcullis drops and the target who tripped the tripwire 
is now in a trapped area where egress is blocked. Generally, the 

===== PAGE 101 =====
95
tripwire is far enough away from the portcullis that when tripped, 
there is no save to escape before it falls. Any additional targets 
within 5’ of the portcullis trap are allowed an Agility save to be on 
whichever side they choose; failure indicates that the target did not 
make it to the other side of the portcullis before it slammed down. 
In this case, a further Agility save at -20% must be made to avoid 
being hit by the portcullis and being pinned in a random area, 
which results in 6d6 smashing damage and being pierced by 1d4-1 
spikes, each inflicting an additional 3d6+3 damage. 
Detection: Spotting either the tripwire or the outline of the 
portcullis in its slot above the drop
Removal: Either use a hammer/mallet and spike to pin the tripwire 
or place 3-4 spikes in the portcullis to prevent it from falling. 
Modifiers: Base costs for a Falling Portcullis trap are 40 gold (low), 
60 gold (medium), or 70 gold (high). A pressure plate can be used 
and attached to a weighted system in place of a tripwire, reducing 
the detection chance by -10% but increasing the cost by 25% and 
the setup time by 2 hours. Secret compartments that open when 
activated, revealing the dropping portcullis and its side runners, 
further reduce detection by 10% and add 25% to the cost. 
Falling Cage
Construction Time: 12 hours
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +0%	
Remove: -20%
Required: 
1 metal cage 10’ x 10’ x 10’, mounted above the falling area in seams 
with runners to the floor and holes in the floor for the cage’s spikes 
to rest in when dropped (cage)
2 12’ wires or cords (tripwire, weight wire)
1 set of counterbalances weighing slightly more than the cage 
(weights)
1 fixed object to which the tripwire will be attached (anchor)
1 release that attaches the tripwire to the anchor (release)
Steps to create: Attach the release to the anchor, then one end of the 
tripwire. Attach one end of the weight wire to the weights and the 
other end of the cage. Make a Strength save to raise the cage into 
place. Attach the other end of the tripwire to the weights, holding 
them down until released. To reset this trap, make a Strength save 
to carefully pull the tripwire until the weights hit the floor and the 
cage is again aloft, then reattach the tripwire to the release.
Triggered By: Hitting the tripwire, which pulls the release 
mechanism that drops the cage
Effect: The cage drops and the target who tripped the tripwire 
is now in a trapped area where egress is blocked. Any targets 
(including the one who set off the trap) within 5’ of one of the 
cage’s sides are allowed an Agility save to escape the area before the 
cage falls. In this case, a further Agility save at -20% must be made 
to avoid being hit by the cage and being pinned in a random area, 
which results in 6d6 smashing damage and being pierced by 1d4-1 
spikes, each inflicting an additional 3d6+3 damage. 
Detection: Spotting either the tripwire or the outline of the cage in 
its slot above the drop
Removal: Carefully pin the tripwire with a hammer/mallet and 
a spike so it can’t be released or place 3-4 spikes in the cage to 
prevent it from falling. 
Modifiers: Base costs for a Falling Cage trap are 100 gold (low), 
150 gold (medium), or 200 gold (high). A pressure plate can be 
used and attached to a weighted system in place of a tripwire, 
reducing the detection chance by -10% but increasing the cost by 
25% and the setup time by 2 hours. Secret compartments that open 
when activated, revealing the dropping cage and its side runners 
further reduce detection by 10% and add 25% to the cost. 
Closing Walls

Set: +20%

Required: 
2 heavy stone panels (closing walls)
1 pressure plate (pressure plate)
2 12’ wires or cords (pressure plate wires)
2 sets of heavy weights (counterweights)
2 sets of heavy gears (heavy gears)
Steps to create: Attach both wires to the pressure plate in unseen 
runner channels beneath the floor. Attach the other end of the 
wires to the gears sets, then attach these to the ends of the walls in 
their runners. Make a Strength save to push apart the walls until 
they are even with the normal walls. This will raise the pressure 
plate until it is even with the floor. Set the pressure plate to activate 
at a certain weight (generally 50-250 lb.).
Triggered By: Stepping onto the pressure plate, which releases the 
counterweights, which pull the heavy gears on either side to bring 
the walls together 
Effect: All targets in the target area feel rumbling and hear heavy 
gears turning as the walls move inward. The targets have a few 
seconds to vacate the area or be crushed between the closing walls 
and take crushing damage (see below).

Sliding Stairs
Construction Time: 8 hours per 10’ of stairs
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +10%	
Remove: -10%
Required: 
1 pressure plate stair (pressure plate)
2 wires or cords that run the length of the stairs (pressure plate 
wires)
1 set of weights (counterweights)
1 pair of pivots per stair (pivots)
Steps to create: Install central pivots points.  Set stairs in pivots, 
then rail tying stairs together.  Finally create a weighted trigger 
mechanism.
Triggered By: Stepping on the stair that is the pressure plate, which 
releases the mechanism that causes the front of each stair to fall 
down and lock in place, converting the stairs into a slide
Effect: Agility save at -20% or fall prone and slip down the new 
slide. Success indicates the ability to stand, despite the lack of 
traction. If successful, any further movement up or down the slide 
requires a new Agility save at -20% per 10’ of stairs or fall prone 
and slip. 
Detection: Either spotting the pressure plate stair, noticing the 
smoothness of the stairs, or noticing a slight give in the steps. 
Removal: Either set a spike in the seam of each stair or use four 
spikes on the pressure plate stair.
Modifiers: Base costs for a Sliding Stairs trap are per 10’ of stairs: 
50 gold (low), 100 gold (medium), or 150 gold (high). Refillable 
grease spray bladders can be added that activate from the sides of 
the stairs when the stairs turn into a slide. In this case, targets must 
make a half Agility save to keep their footing, both initially and 
if attempting to move. Even when the stairs return to their stair 
form, Agility saves to maneuver the steps are at -20% until cleaned. 
These grease sprayers cost of 10% of the total trap cost and increase 
detection by 20%, since the holes can be seen. Resetting this trap 
involves cleaning away the grease and squeezing new or recovered 
grease back into the spray holes. Furthermore, an automatic gear 
and weight system that will reset the trap after a set time (10 
minutes, an hour, etc.) can be added at +50% of the cost. Also, this 
trap may be combined with a separate trap at the bottom of the 
slide, such as a pit, chute, spike, etc., that is activated at the same 
time as the Sliding Stairs trap. 
Miscellaneous Traps
Description: Including such devices as alarms and poisons, these 
urban traps are general deterrents which can be set practically 
anywhere, from slits in the wall to locks on chests.
The Alarm Bell
Construction Time: 30 minutes
Set: +10% 	
Detect: +10%	
Remove: +10%
Required: 
1 bell (alarm)
1 striker or mallet to strike the bell (striker)
1 6’ wire or cord (tripwire)
1 fixed object to attach the tripwire to (anchor)
1 release that attaches the tripwire to the anchor (release)
1 coiled spring to store energy (spring)
1 set of gears to increase the mechanical power (gears)
Steps to create: Attach the release to both the anchor and one end of 
the tripwire. Wind the coiled spring, then attach it to the other end 
of the tripwire. Attach the largest gear to the striker and set up the 
rest of the gears. Attach the coiled spring to the last gear.
Triggered By: Hitting the tripwire, which releases the coiled 
spring, which is attached by gears to the striker, which hits the bell 
several times
Effect: The bells clangs loudly. The distance of sound travel is based 
on the size of the bell and striker, and the number of strikes is 
based on the coiled spring size. 
Detection: Spotting either the tripwire, bell, or striking mechanism
Removal: Either cut/remove the tripwire, remove the bell, or 
remove part of the striker mechanism. 
Modifiers: Base costs for an Alarm Bell trap are 25 gold (low), 40 
gold (medium), or 56 gold (high). A pressure plate can be used and 
attached to a weighted system in place of a tripwire, reducing the 
detection chance by 10% but increasing the cost by 25% and the 
setup time by 1 hour. 
Poison Needle
Construction Time: 30 minutes
Set: +10% 	
Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0%
Triggered By: Attempting to open a lock without a key, which 
causes the needle to slide out of its hole and strike the target’s finger
Required: 
1 good lock (lock)
1 needle sleeve (sleeve)
1 small spring (spring)
1 catch to set the spring against (catch)
Poison
Steps to create: Inset the sleeve within the lock. Set the spring inside 
the sleeve. Tighten the spring and set it against the catch, which is 
attached to one of the lock’s tumblers. Next, poison the needle and 
set it carefully in the loaded sleeve with the tightened spring. If the 
Set Trap skill is failed when attempting to maneuver the poisoned 
needle, the setter must make an Agility save or make a Poison 
Resistance.
Effect: Poison save or suffer effects of the poison if the needle 
passes through armor. Anyone picking a lock with gloves usually 
has a penalty of -20%, so most often, a target’s hands will be 
gloveless.

===== PAGE 103 =====
97
Detection: Spotting the glisten of the needle inside the lock
Removal: Use a thin tool to spring the needle away so as to avoid 
being struck.   
Modifiers: Base costs for a Poison Needle trap are 25 gold (low), 50 
gold (medium), or 75 gold (high), plus the cost of the poison. For 
10% of the cost, the sleeve can have a rubber or wax membrane, 
allowing poison to be stored in it; this allows the sleeve to be 
refilled up to 10 times and to preserve poisons which lose potency 
over time. For an additional 5% cost, the needle can be welded or 
attached to the spring so it does not leave the mechanism and can 
be reset without replacing the needle. Also, for an additional 20% 
cost, the entire spring mechanism can have a second wound spring 
added so that it will reset automatically in 30 seconds (up to 10 
times) before having to be rewound. Alternately, for no additional 
cost, the needle can be set so that it ejects not out of the lock hole 
but a small fraction of an inch away and is set to eject when picked 
or when even the correct key is used improperly (turned the wrong 
direction, too far, etc.). This modification increases detection by 
10% as the needle hole can be seen by a careful observer. 
Poison Gas
Construction Time: 30 minutes
Set: +10% 	
Detect: +0%	
Remove: -10%
Triggered By: Hitting the tripwire, which releases something that 
breaks a glass flask filled with poison gas
Required: 
1 6’ wire or cord (tripwire)
1 mallet or weight set above the glass vial (breaker)
1 fixed object to which the tripwire will be attached (anchor)
1 release that attaches the tripwire to the anchor (release)
Poison gas (gas)
Glass flask (flask)
Steps to create: Create a compartment lined with holes. Set the 
release in the anchor, then attach the release to one end of the 
tripwire. Attach the weights to the breaker and set it above the area 
reserved for the flask. Raise the breaker into place and attach it 
to the other end of the tripwire, which holds up the breaker until 
released. Next, set the gas flask into the compartment. To reset the 
mechanism, carefully pull the tripwire until the breaker is raised, 
reattach the tripwire to the release, and add a new gas flask. 
Effect: Poison Resistance to avoid damage from the resulting 
poisonous gas if within 10’ of the gas holes
Detection: Spotting the tripwire or gas holes 
Removal: Either use a hammer/mallet to pin the tripwire with a 
spike or plug the gas holes. 
Modifiers: Base costs for Poison Gas trap are 20 gold (low), 40 
gold (medium), or 60 gold (high), plus the cost of the poison gas. 
In addition, a secret compartment can be added that hides the gas 
holes until the trap is activated; this reduces detection by 10% but 
adds 25% to the cost.
Urban (Magical Traps): 
These traps can be set through spellcasting or by kinetically 
altering the physical world through use of Kinetics 
Knowledge. Unlike wilderness magical traps, these are 
meant to be used in confined spaces or in ways that work 
well in urban settings or structures. Some are only meant 
to be used once, while others are permanently set through 
use of enchantment or Will Force cost. In order to create 
these traps with a spell, the user must enchant the targeted 
area with that spell through use of either Spell Lore or 
Enchantment, in essence, turning the area itself into a magic 
item activated by deed (touching a specific trigger area). 
Furthermore, traps created through a specific kinesis will be 
in place for 1 hour per Class Title or permanently at a cost 
of 1/10th of a Will Force, in which case the trap resets after 
10 seconds.
Magical Traps that Defy Physics
Description: Breaking the laws of physics, these traps pose 
as strong defense mechanisms using feats such as reversed 
magnetism, dangerous light and sound waves, teleportation, and 
other such tricks.
Magnetic
Construction Time: 10 minutes
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0%
Required: 
An area up to 5’ x 5’ per Class Title
The skill Magnetokinesis to kinetically alter an area
Triggered By: Any being with an Aura field walking into the 
triggered area
Effect: Strength save at -5% per Practitioner Title by all targets 
within 10’ of the trap to avoid losing grip on all ferrous metal 
objects currently being held, and Agility save at -5% per 
Practitioner Title by all targets within 10’ of the trap who are 
wearing ferrous metal armor to avoid being pulled into the trap 
and possibly knocked over prone, depending on the trap’s location.
Detection: The magic holding the potential energy of the 
magnetically altered area can be detected with Detect Magic or 
Detect Aura. To detect the trigger area itself, Detect Magic or 
Detect Aura must be combined with Detect Trap.
Removal: Dispel the magic on the set area to release the potential 
energy of the kinetically altered area (hence, triggering the trap). 
Alternatively, another Kinetics Knowledge skill user can safely 
remove this affect with a successful Magnetokinesis (Magnetic 
Trap) skill roll. Remove Trap does not function without removal of 
the magic effect but can be used to mark the outline of the area to 
avoid.
Gravitic
Construction Time: 10 minutes or spellcasting time
Set: +0% 	Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0%
Required: 
If using spells:
An area up to 10’ x 10’ x 10’ per 2 Aura

The spell Control Gravity to cause an immediate change in gravity
The spell Enchantment or Spell Lore to enchant an area
The spell Glamour to hide the trap through illusory means 
(optional)
If using skills:
An area up to 5’ x 5’ by 5’ per Class Title
The skill Gravikinesis to kinetically alter an area
Triggered By: Any being with an Aura field walking into the

Effect: Agility save at -2% per Aura (if the trap was created

Alternatively, when creating this trap with Gravikinesis, the user 
can apply one type of gravity alteration per Practitioner Title, up 
to a maximum of 3. For example, causing a target to be suddenly 
swept down a side hall and crushed against the wall at the end 
would take two steps: first removing the current gravity and then 
adding it back in, but from the wall at the end of the hall rather 
than the floor. If the user added a third step of doubling the 
gravitational pull, the target would “fall” faster toward the end of 
the hallway and take extra falling damage. The following are a few 
examples of effects that would count as one step:
• Removing gravity completely
• Adding gravity to an area without any gravity
• Doubling or halving the current gravitational pull (can be applied  
multiple times, causing cumulative effects)
• Altering the current gravitational pull for only one specific type of 
being or object (i.e. dwarves, zombies, metal, liquids, etc.)
Detection: If this trap was created with Control Gravity, the 
enchanted ground can be detected as a magical area with Detect 
Magic or Detect Aura. If this trap was created with Gravikinesis, 
the magic holding the potential energy of the kinetically altered 
area can be detected with Detect Magic or Detect Aura. To detect 
the trigger area itself, Detect Magic or Detect Aura must be 
combined with Detect Trap. The spells Glamour or Non-Detection 
can be used to hide the Gravitic trap, but a successful Detect 
Trap skill roll after a Detect Magic or Detect Aura will reveal that 
something seems “off” with no additional clarity. If Glamour was 
used and the searcher asks for and makes an Illusion Resistance, 
they will see through the illusion and detect the trap.
Removal: If this trap was created with Control Gravity, the only 
sure way to remove the trap is to dispel the spell’s magic. Although 
the skill Remove Trap does not function without removal of the 
magical effect, it can be used to mark the outline of the area to 
avoid. If this trap was created with Gravikinesis, dispelling the 
magic in the kinetically altered area will release the potential 
energy and set off the trap. Alternatively, another Kinetics 
Knowledge skill user can safely remove this affect with a successful 
Gravikinesis (Gravitic Trap) skill roll.
Repulsor
Construction Time: 10 minutes or spellcasting time
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0%
Required: 
If using spells:
An area up to 1’ radius per Aura 
The spell Repulsion to push away targets
The spell Enchantment or Spell Lore to enchant an area
The spell Glamour to hide the trap through illusory means 
(optional)
If using skills:
An area up to 5’ radius per Class Title
The skills Telekinesis and Kinetics Knowledge to kinetically alter

Triggered By: Any being with an Aura field walking into the

Effect: Agility save to avoid falling down and being pushed away

Alternately, if this trap was created with Telekinesis, all saves are

with no additional clarity. If Glamour was used and the searcher

Removal: If this trap was created with Repulsion, the only sure way

kinetically altered area will release the potential energy and set off 
the trap. Alternatively, another Kinetics Knowledge skill user can 
safely remove this affect with a successful Telekinesis (Repulsor 
Trap) skill roll.
Modifiers: The user can channel or direct the magical repulsion by 
enchanting nozzles, slits, holes, etc. rather than just an area. This 
allows the user to affect a specific height (i.e. a flat area 5’ above 
the floor, which would have no effect on midfolk and dwarves) or 
location (i.e. down a hallway that leads to a pit lined with spikes). 
In this manner, the user can combine the Repulsor trap with 
another type of trap.

Deafening
Construction Time: 10 minutes or spellcasting time
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0%
Required:
If using spells:
An area up to 3’ radius per Aura
The spell Thunderclap to create a deafening sound
Either the spell Enchantment or Spell Lore to enchant an area, or

The spell Glamour to hide the trap through illusory means

If using skills:
An area up to 5’ radius per Class Title
The skill Sonokinesis to kinetically alter an area
Triggered By: Any being with an Aura field walking into or near

Effect: If this trap was created with Thunderclap, targets must 
make a Magic Resistance or be struck deaf by a thunderclap for 
the next 1 hour per Aura used in the spell with a 1% chance per 
Aura of being permanent. If this trap was created with Sonokinesis, 
targets within 10’ per Practitioner Title must make a Magic 
Resistance or be struck deaf by an incredibly loud sound for 10 
minutes per Practitioner Title. Targets who make their save, along 
with anyone else within 50’ per Practitioner Title, will also hear 
this sound for a full 10 seconds.
Detection: If this trap was created with Thunderclap, the 
enchanted ground may be detected as a magical area with Detect 
Magic or Detect Aura. If this trap was created with Sonokinesis, the 
magic holding the potential energy of the kinetically altered area 
can be detected with Detect Magic or Detect Aura. To detect the 
trigger area itself, Detect Magic or Detect Aura must be combined 
with Detect Trap. The spells Glamour or Non-Detection can be 
used to hide the Deafening trap, but a successful Detect Trap skill 
roll after a Detect Magic or Detect Aura will reveal that something 
seems “off” with no additional clarity. If Glamour was used and the 
searcher asks for and makes an Illusion Resistance, they will see 
through the illusion and detect the trap.
Removal: If this trap was created with Thunderclap, the only sure 
way to remove the trap is to dispel the spell’s magic. Although 
the skill Remove Trap does not function without removal of the 
magical effect, it can be used to mark the outline of the area to 
avoid. If this trap was created with Sonokinesis, dispelling the 
magic in the kinetically altered area will actually release the 
potential energy and set off the trap. Alternatively, another Kinetics 
Knowledge skill user can safely remove this affect with a successful 
Sonokinesis (Alarm Trap) skill roll.

Falling Door Cage
Setting Time: 30 seconds 
Set: +20% 	
Detect: +20%	
Remove: +20% 
Required: 
A pre-purchased falling door cage trap
Bait as desired (increased likelihood of game but not of the trap 
working)
Triggered By: Moving past the pivoting plate, which releases the 
level rod and slams the cage door shut
Effect: Agility save to avoid the pivoting plate or be trapped in the 
cage
Special Effect: Targets having an Intelligence rating of 5 or more 
are afforded an Intelligence save to enter the cage, which is an 
obvious trap. 
Detection: It will be obvious the cage is a trap to anyone who sees 
it, but Detect Trap will reveal the pivoting plate as the trigger. 
Removal: Remove the lever rod from the pivoting plate or lift the 
door out of its runners.

Fool's Gold
Construction Time: Already constructed, setting takes 10 
Seconds.
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0%
Required: 
Unlucky spell. 
Lead painted gold.
Triggered By: When it is physically handled the effect goes off. 
Effect: causing the creature or being that triggered it to make a 
Control Resistance or suffer from 1 unlucky points per 2 Aura used 
in the spell, until exhausted. 
Special Conditions: Careful examination of the gold or Appraisal 
reveals it is gold paint on lead and nearly worthless. The trap’s 
duration will be based on the spell, or meta spell cast on it, up to 
and including enchantment. This usage of enchantment for this 
purpose takes 1 hour and costs 1/10th of a Will Force.
Special Effect: None.
Detection: The trapped gold can be detected as magical 
(specifically, a set, delayed or enchanted magical effect that has not 
yet been triggered). Detect Trap must first be combined with some 
form of Detect Magic/Aura first. Detect Trap after either Detect 
Aura or Magic or similar ability will reveal the target gold will 
trigger the effect.
Removal: Dispel the temporary (or permanent) magic on the set 
item. Remove Trap does not remove the gold but reveals that if it is 
not handled directly the effect will not be activated. 
Description: The spell is set on the coin, determining how unlucky 
the target will be. 
Modifiers: None. 
Special Modifiers: None.
Magic's Folly
Construction Time: Already constructed, setting takes 10 
Seconds.
Set: +0% 		
Detect: +0%	
Remove: +0%
Required: 
Way to Enchant (Enchantment spell, etc.)
A nice looking fake or truly valuable “item”
Triggered By: when someone attempts to activate one of the 
“powers” of the magic item. 
Effect: causes a Magical Mishap to occur. See Master’s Manual 
(Magical Mishap,) the effects vary. 
Special Conditions: This item is created with a purposefully 
failed enchantment such that every power that is activated doesn’t 
work but instead triggers a magical mishap at the Base Aura level 
of the item. It can be a single use trap for no Will Force cost or a 
continuous trap at the cost of 1/10th of a Will Force. 
Special Effect: None.
Detection: The trapped magical item can be detected as magical 
and the specific Aura it is at and even appears to have powers of 
Identify. None of these things trigger the “trap” except trying to 
activate one of the powers. A successful Detect Trap skill roll may 
be combined with any of the previously mentioned skills to reveal 
that the “item” is a trap and will be triggered when activated. 
Removal: Dispel permanent magic on the item. Remove Trap does 
not remove the item but reveals that something is off about it. 
Description: Appears to be a magical item of a specific kind. 
Appears to have the powers of a magic item if identified and 
definitely has the Aura used in the enchantment. Is not illusionary 
in anyway, just is a failed or purposely failed enchantment of an 
item with those powers causing magical mishaps everytime. 
Modifiers: None. 
Special Modifiers: None.

ABASEMENT
Attributes: Aura, Will Force	 	
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: 10 seconds
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill lowers the Control Resistance of the target 
being or beings.
General Usage: The user concentrates on an individual or group 
within sight and makes a skill roll. Success indicates that the target 
or targets suffer from a penalty to their Control Resistance of -5% 
per Practitioner Title (-25% maximum) for 1 hour per Practitioner 
Title. Target beings are allowed an Illusion Resistance to negate this 
effect, if requested.  
Notes: This skill can affect a maximum of 1 being per Class Title of 
the practitioner.
Critical Failure: The target being(s) become aware that the 
practitioner was attempting to affect their mind(s).
Critical Success: The target’s Control Resistance is lowered by an 
additional 10% (flat, not per Practitioner Title). 
Repeat Failure: Treat three failed attempts as a critical failure.
Requirements: Title 6 and Illusion Knowledge.
ANTICIPATION
Attributes: Agility, Will Force	
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: Special
Type: Disciplined, Magical	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill allows the Practitioner to have anticipated 
the last action of an opponent and choose a different action in 
response. 
General Usage: When an opponent takes an action, the 
practitioner can respond by making this skill roll. If successful, the 
last action the practitioner would have taken is discarded and any 
action that can occur in the same time as the discarded action is 
chosen instead, thereby replacing the action with a different one 
as if they had anticipated the opponent’s action. For example, the 
opponent casts Finger of Fire while the practitioner was swinging 
a war axe over the course of 5 seconds. When the opponent 
announces the Finger of Fire, the practitioner announces she is 
using Anticipation, makes the skill roll, and then discards the 5 
second weapon attack and substitutes activation of an Endure Heat 
magic item she carries that also takes 5 seconds. If her weapon 
attack had been only a 4 second attack, then Anticipation would 
not work because the activation would not resolve within the 4 
second window of the discarded weapon attack. However, if the 
skill roll is a critical success as noted below, 1 additional second 
is gained and then it would be possible. Likewise, if the replaced 
action took 6 or more seconds, then Anticipation could be used 
with the extra seconds simply being discarded. In no case is the 
action substituted allowed to be more than 10 seconds in length.
Special Usage: An opponent’s movement to engage the practitioner 
can be treated as an opponent’s action. In this case, the practitioner 
makes an Anticipation skill roll, and if successful, whatever the 
practitioner’s current action was can be discarded and replaced 
with the substituted action as long as the substituted action takes 
no more than the either the time to engage or the discarded action, 
whichever is greater. In no case is the action substituted allowed to 
be more than 10 seconds in length. 
Special Notes: If two practitioners of Anticipation face off, then it 
becomes a contest of skills. The winner of the contest then gets to 
choose to be the one to substitute an action if desired, and the loser 
may not substitute an action but rather must use their original 
action. 

===== PAGE 112 =====
106
Critical Success: The skill user gains 1 extra second, allowing 
a substituted action that takes up to 1 second longer than the 
discarded action. 
Critical Failure: The skill user loses both the normal action they 
were in the midst of and the substituted action, thus wasting the 
seconds.
Repeat Failure: None.
Requirements: Title 15, Weapon Lore, Weapon Dance, and Spin 
Strike, or Title 7 and Weapon Lore, Foresee, and Foretell
APATHY
Attributes: Aura, Will Force	 Rating: 14
Start Bonus: 2d6%		
Time: 10 seconds
Type: Magical	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: Causes the target being or beings to experience 
disregard for their current situation. 
General Usage: The user concentrates on an individual or group 
within sight and makes a skill roll. Success indicates that the 
target or targets suffer from complete apathy for 1 minute per 
Practitioner Title. Target beings are allowed an Illusion Resistance 
to negate this effect, if requested. Affected beings have the 
following negative modifiers:
•	 Strength melee damage modifier is reduced to 0.
•	 -2 damage with melee and missile weapons per Practitioner 
Title (-10 maximum)
•	 -1 to hit with melee and missile weapons per Practitioner Title 
(-5 maximum)
•	 +1 Initiative per Practitioner Title (+5 maximum)
•	 -5% to Control Resistance per Practitioner Title (-25% 
maximum)
•	 -10% to morale checks per Practitioner Title
Notes: This skill can affect a maximum of 1 being per Class Title of 
the practitioner.
Critical Failure: No further attempt on these targets may be made 
until the skill chance is increased.
Critical Success: The duration of the effects is doubled. 
Repeat Failure: Treat three failed attempts as a critical failure.
Requirements: Title 3 and Illusion Knowledge.
APPAROKINESIS
Attributes: Intelligence, Aura		
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: Varies
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill allows the practitioner to manipulate spatial 
energies to move objects instantly from one place to another.
General Usage: The user concentrates on the desired effect and 
mentally wills it to happen. Unlike casting spells, the amount of 
Aura needed to create an effect is constant. The Aura is drained 
from the practitioner’s Aura Pool and returns at her Aura 
Regeneration Rate. Note: Class Title in these usages always refers 
to the Class Title of the practitioner, even when the verbiage 
seems to indicate otherwise. Unless otherwise specified, effects are 
instantaneous in duration and have a range of 10’ per Class Title.
Forfeit (12 Aura; +30% modifier, 5 seconds): Causes an object 
currently touched by the practitioner to be placed in a random 
location elsewhere on the practitioner’s current plane (infinite 
range). The object can appear anywhere but will neither appear 
inside of nor displace another object or being. If the object to be 
affected is a magical or divine item or is within another being’s 
Aura field (i.e. being held by another being), the item or being 
holding it is afforded a Magic Resistance. Living beings cannot be 
affected by this usage. The item will also not be placed in such a 
way as to fall from great height or cause any indirect immediate 
harm. The GM can either choose the destination or decide 
randomly by rolling a d12 for direction starting with North at 1, 
then rolling a percentage where 100% equals the complete opposite 
side of the planet or the farthest possible distance away on the 
plane. 
Return (12 Aura; +30% modifier, 1 second): Causes a single thrown 
weapon, object, or set of projectiles to be marked in its/their 
current relative location in relation to the targeted being for return. 
Thus, if a spear is so marked and the skill roll is successful, then 
when it is thrown and strikes an object, it will return 1 second later 
to the wielder’s hand (or holster/scabbard if marked in a holster/
scabbard). Likewise, a quiver full of arrows or quarrels could be 
also marked, and each would return 1 second after striking a target 
to the quiver they were marked in even if the target moves before 
or during the use of the weapons. This effect is useable once per 
Class Title before having to reroll the skill chance.
Acquire (15 Aura; +15% modifier, 5 seconds): Causes an item 
to appear in the practitioner’s hand or within 1’ of their person, 
as desired. The practitioner must both know where the object 
currently is and have handled the object in the past for this usage 
to affect the object, and the object must be on the same plane as the 
practitioner. If the object to be affected is a magical or divine item 
or is within another being’s Aura field (i.e. being held by another 
being), the item or being holding it is afforded a Magic Resistance. 
Living beings cannot be affected by this usage.
Blink (15 Aura; +15% modifier, 2 seconds): The practitioner may 
teleport anywhere within visual or sensed range. The practitioner 
spends 1 second focusing on the target location, makes the skill 
roll, and then, if successful, dematerializes and rematerializes in the 
new location 1 second later. All objects carried by the practitioner 
blink with the practitioner regardless of weight. No other beings 
will blink with the practitioner, even if they are within the 
practitioner’s Aura field. 
Dispossess (15 Aura; +15% modifier, 5 seconds): Causes an object 
weighing no more than 20 lb. per Class Title and currently touched 
by the practitioner’s Aura field to be teleported to a location 
designated by the practitioner. The object can appear anywhere the 
practitioner desires but will neither appear inside of nor displace 
another object or being. If the object to be affected is a magical or 
divine item or is within another being’s Aura field (i.e. being held 
by another being), the item or being holding it is afforded a Magic 
Resistance. Living beings cannot be affected by this usage. The 
object cannot be placed in such a way as to fall from great height or 
cause any indirect immediate harm. The target location may be on 
any plane but must be somewhere that the caster has seen or can 
otherwise visualize.

===== PAGE 113 =====
107
Teleport Trap (15 Aura; +15% modifier, 10 minutes): Creates a 
trapped area no larger than 5 ft² per Class Title. This area is a set 
trap that, when touched by another Aura field, will be triggered 
and cause the creature or being that triggered it to make a Magic 
Resistance or be teleported away. During creation, the practitioner 
either envisions an area the being will be teleported to (within 
100’ per Practitioner Title) or leaves the trap random. If random, 
teleportation will be 1d10 miles away per Practitioner Title in a 
random direction (1d12 with north as 1). A randomly selected area 
must be relatively safe, meaning that no immediate harm (open air 
falls, acid pits, etc.) will come to the teleported target. The Teleport 
Trap will last for 1 hour per Class Title once set. Alternatively, 
1/10th of a Will Force can be spent to make the trap permanent; 
the trap will reset every 10 seconds once triggered. 
Teleport (16 Aura; +10% modifier, 10 seconds): Causes the 
practitioner and up to 20 lb. of additional material per Class Title 
to be teleported from their current location to another location on 
the same plane. A failure of the skill roll means the teleport does 
not occur. All objects that are to be teleported must be contacting 
the practitioner’s Aura field. The total weight of all objects and 
items must be under the practitioner’s weight limit or the skill will 
automatically fail. Consult the chart in Special Notes to determine 
modifiers to this skill based on the desired target location.
Specialization Ability, Mass Teleport (18 Aura; no modifier, 10 
seconds +1 second per additional being): Causes the practitioner 
and up to 1 willing being per Class Title to be teleported from 
their current location to another location if the skill roll succeeds. 
Failure indicates the teleport does not occur. Each affected being 
may carry up to 20 lb. of additional material per Class Title. All 
affected beings must be in physical contact with the practitioner’s 
Aura field or they will be left behind.  Unwilling beings are afforded 
a Magic Resistance to resist teleportation. The practitioner must 
teleport with the other beings; he cannot send them by themselves. 
All beings are sent to the same target area, so the target area must 
be large enough to accommodate all affected beings or the skill will 
automatically fail. Consult the chart in Special Notes to determine 
modifiers to this skill based on the desired target location.
Mastery Ability, Dispatch (20 Aura; -10% modifier, 10 seconds): 
Allows the practitioner to teleport one or more willing beings to a 
desired location. The practitioner does not accompany the beings 
and does not need to touch them, though all target beings must 
be within 10’ per Class Title of the practitioner. All beings are sent 
to the same target area, so the target area must be large enough to 
accommodate all affected beings or the skill will automatically fail.  
Consult the chart in Special Notes to determine modifiers to this 
skill based on the desired target location.
Special Notes:  The following situational modifiers govern the skill 
roll for the usages Dispatch, Teleport, and Mass Teleport:
Situation
Modifier	
Area never seen but imagined
-50%
Area viewed once
-25%
Area viewed two or three times
-10%
Area memorized
+0%
Area visited often
+15%
Area is within current sight
+30%
Area is being viewed by magic
+50%
Area is considered home
+75%
Critical Success: 1/2 Aura requirements.
Critical Failure: The skill user is unable to use Apparokinesis for 1 
minute and must make a Will Force save or suffer mental fatigue.
Repeat Failure: Treat 3 repeat failures as a Critical Failure.
Requirements: Title 7, Kinetics Knowledge, and Kinetics Lore
AURAKINESIS
Attributes: Intelligence, Aura	Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: Varies
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill represents the ability to directly manipulate 
magical energy.  
General Usage: The user concentrates on the desired effect and 
mentally wills it to happen. Unlike casting spells, the amount of 
Aura needed to create an effect is constant. The Aura is drained 
from the practitioner’s Aura Pool and returns at her Aura 
Regeneration Rate. Note: Class Title in these usages always refers 
to the Class Title of the practitioner, even when the verbiage 
seems to indicate otherwise. Unless otherwise specified, effects are 
instantaneous in duration and have a range of 10 ft. per Class Title.
Aura Message (10 Aura; +40% modifier, 1 second + writing time): 
Allows the practitioner to draw a design or message in the air 
using his finger. The design or message must be crafted with one 
continuous stroke and glows in the practitioner’s Aura color. The 
message lingers in the air for 1 hour per Class Title. This can be 
used to create temporary Runes (Rune Lore) or can be combined 
with the skill Sigil. 
Identify (12 Aura; +30% modifier, special): Allows the practitioner 
to use her Identify skill at range and without physically touching an 
item. This usage requires a successful skill roll for both Aurakinesis 
and Identify, and does not add any additional time to Identify.
Aura Spike (14 Aura; +20% modifier, 5 seconds): Causes one 
being to experience a sudden spike in Aura. The victim takes 1d12 
points of damage per Class Title to 1 body area and 1d12 to all 
surrounding areas. A Magic Resistance is allowed; success indicates 
half damage is taken and success made by half or more indicates 
no damage is taken. The target being need only be sensed, not 
necessarily seen, to be targeted.
Subvert Magic (16 Aura; +10% modifier, 10 seconds): Allows 
the practitioner an attempt to dispel one previous spell in effect.  

===== PAGE 114 =====
108
The chance for any one spell to be dispelled in this fashion is 
determined through a contest of the practitioner’s Aurakinesis 
skill roll versus the amount of Aura put into the target spell. The 
amount of Aura used in the spell is multiplied by 5 and percentile 
dice are rolled. If this roll succeeds by a larger percentage than 
the practitioner’s original Aurakinesis roll, Subvert Magic fails. 
Otherwise, the spell is dispelled and the Aura is automatically 
added to the caster’s Aura Pool. Permanent spells have a -75% 
chance to be Subverted. This skill cannot dispel the powers of 
magical items.
Aura Shield (18 Aura; no modifier, 1 second): Converts the 
practitioner’s Aura field into an anti-magic shield. This shield will 
absorb all effects and damage from magical sources at a rate of 5 
Aura worth of effects per Class Title. Each 5 Aura of effect drains 1 
level of the Aura shield until the shield is gone. If the last effect has 
any Aura left, then that much of the effect is applied. For example, 
if a 12 Aura Finger of Fire spell hits an Aura Shield with 1 level left 
in the shield, then 5 Aura of the Finger of Fire is absorbed and the 
other 7 hits the practitioner through the shield. While the shield 
is up, the practitioner does not regenerate Aura, nor can she cast 
spells, activate magic items, or use her Aura pool for any purpose. 
The shield remains until the practitioner cancels the effect or it is 
depleted.
Gather Aura (18 Aura; no modifier, 1 minute): Allows the 
practitioner to gather ambient Aura from his surroundings to 
temporarily boost his Aura rating by 2. This lasts 1 day before 
dissipating. Subsequent uses of Gather Aura have no further effect. 
This effect stacks fully with any other Aura-increasing effects, such 
as Draw Power.
Disintegrate (20 Aura; -10% modifier, 10 seconds): Allows the 
practitioner to magically dissolve the bonds holding a being’s 
form together. Failing a Magic Resistance, the affected being is 
disintegrated. Unlike the spell, no powder residue is left behind. 
Disintegrated beings cannot be resurrected but may be restored 
with a Wish or Miracle. The range is 20’ per Class Title.
Shred Aura (20 Aura; -10% modifier, 5 seconds): Allows the 
practitioner to forcefully rip apart an Aura field of another being, 
temporarily reducing their Aura Rating by 1 per Class Title. A 
being shredded in this manner regenerates their attribute points at 
a rate of 1 per hour. This process is extremely painful for the target, 
causing 1 level of mental fatigue per Class Title and doing 1d12 
damage per Aura lost to 1d2 random vital areas. Aura shredded 
in this manner may be absorbed immediately by the practitioner 
through Absorb Aura before it dissipates. A Magic Resistance is 
allowed to avoid all effects.
Warp Aura (22 Aura; -20% modifier, 5 seconds): Forcefully distorts 
the Aura of a being causing a random magical mishap to happen 
to the target unless both a Magic Resistance and an Aura save are 
passed. Failure of either indicates the mishap occurs with the target 
as the focus.
Specialization Ability, Aurafire (21 Aura; -15% modifier, 5 seconds): 
Allows the practitioner to temporarily expend his Aura in a 
dramatic and terrible display. The practitioner must have an Aura 
Rating of at least 21 to use this ability, as this ability requires that 
a minimum of 20 Aura be used in its execution. When used, the 
actual Aura Rating of the practitioner is reduced to 1, and a violent 
burst of searing Aura in the form of a stream 6” in diameter by 10’ 
long per Aura point expended is unleashed in a direction of his 
choosing. A stream created at 20 Aura would be 10’ in diameter 
and 200’ long. Beings unfortunate enough to suffer a hit from 
Aurafire take 1d12 per Aura point expended to all body areas 
caught within the blast, though a successful Magic Resistance 
results in only half damage, and a Magic Resistance made at half 
results in no damage. Beings immune to magic or fire still take half 
of any applicable damage. Immediately upon use of this ability, the 
practitioner is rendered unconscious for 1d10 hours, causing him 
to fall to the ground. His Aura Rating is permanently reduced by 1, 
and the remainder of his Aura Rating recovers at the rate of 1 point 
per hour regardless of the normal Aura regeneration rate. A critical 
success has no effect on this usage.
Mastery Ability, Aura Storm (25 Aura; -35% modifier, 10 seconds): 
Creates a buffeting miasma of chromatic pure Aurafire at a fixed 
height of 10’ and a radius of 2’ per Class Title that lasts for 10 
seconds per Class Title. The practitioner must concentrate on the 
storm to keep it maintained. The practitioner can move the storm 
with him at walking speed. Effects 1 and 2 are dependent on one 
Magic Resistance only. Beings immune to Aura energy effects 
are unaffected by this storm. All within its radius are affected as 
follows: 
•	 Make a Magic Resistance or take 1d12 damage per 2 Class 
Titles per 10 seconds to 2d4 exposed areas (any body area 
protected by less than 5 points of armor is considered exposed). 
•	 Make a Magic Resistance once per 10 seconds or be blinded 
and deafened by the chaotic lights and roar.  
•	 Make an Agility save every 10 seconds. Failure indicates the 
being has lost his footing and has fallen to the ground. 
•	 Make a Strength save to combat normally. Failure results in 
a penalty of -4 to hit, half damage to attacks, and -20% to all 
combat skills. 
•	 Missile weapons fired within an Aura Storm have an equal 
chance of striking any being within the area of effect. 
Special Use: The practitioner can make a skill roll when forced to 
suffer the effects of an Aura based attack or effect. If the skill roll 
is successful, the practitioner gets a +20% to Magic Resistance for 
that attack, and any damage from the attack is reduced by -1 per 
die. 
Critical Success: 1/2 Aura requirements.
Critical Failure: Skill user is unable to use Aurakinesis for 1 
minute and must make a Will Force save or suffer mental fatigue.
Repeat Failure: Treat 3 repeat failures as a Critical Failure.
Requirements: Title 8, Kinetics Knowledge, and Kinetics Lore.

BEGUILE
Attributes: Aura, Will Force	 	
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: 20 seconds.
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: By means of this skill a practitioner can take control 
of a humanoid or magical humanoid. 
General Usage: The practitioner speaks aloud in a language the 
target understands or alternately establishes any form of mental 
contact (Mind Dance, Though Projection, or telepathy effects) 
and attempts to control the being. After 20 seconds, the victim is 
afforded a Control Resistance. If the victim fails this resistance, 
they are now under the direct control of the practitioner and 
must accept commands both mental or spoken so long as they 
understand them. Beings who succeed in a Control Resistance 
against the practitioner cannot be the target of this skill again until 
the skill chance is improved. The control of the target will last 1 
hour per Practitioner Title and may not be renewed through use 
of this skill (although the skill Retain Control can prolong this 
duration). The target must first be released and then a new Beguile 
skill use can be attempted. Only 1 being or creature can be beguiled 
at a time per 3 full Class Titles or creature levels. 
Notes: Beings will not take an action that will directly kill them 
while beguiled, and receiving a command to do so affords them a 
new Control Resistance to break the control. A controlled being 
can be ordered into a dangerous situation that might cause their 
death, such as being ordered to fight a former ally, so long as that 
ally is not so superior that death is the obvious result. 
Special Usage: The skills Bind Control and Retain Control can 
change how the being is controlled and the duration respectively. 
Critical Failure: No further attempt to control the targeted being 
or creature may be made until the skill chance is increased.
Critical Success: The being or creature will continue to accept 
other commands from the practitioner, so long as these commands 
do not conflict with its given task or require an undead to leave an 
area it is guarding.
Repeat Failure: Treat three failed attempts as a critical failure.
Requirements: Title 7 and Charming or Intimidation.

Start Bonus: 2d6	
	
	
Time: 5 seconds
Type: Divine Magical	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: The ability to amplify a target’s voice, allowing it to be

Special Uses: By amplifying somebody’s voice, the radius of affect

a hymn he is singing, or an entire army could hear their general’s

Notes: This skill does not affect the level of success or failure of any

Critical Failure: The skill user must wait 30 seconds before 
attempting again.
Critical Success: Amplification lasts twice as long as it normally 
would have.
Repeat Failure: No further attempts may be made on this target 
until after the Bellow skill chance has been increased.
Requirements: Title 6 and the skills Intone, Whisper, and either 
Harmony or Discord.

CACOPHONY
Attributes: Piety, Will Force	 	
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10	 	
	
Time: 1 minute
Type: Divine Magical	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: Causes all listeners within a certain distance of the 
skill user to hear a horrendous, discordant mixture of bedlam and 
noise; the blackest and most evil sound imaginable. 
General Usage: The skill user spends 1 minute attuning himself 
to the surrounding noise (even that which is so minute as the 
practitioner’s very breathing). The practitioner gradually gains 
control over that noise and twists it into utter dissonance. The 
sound then radiates audibly at a radius of 100’ per Practitioner 
Title. This horrible noise can last up to 1 minute per Practitioner 
Title, but he can turn it off at any time. This cacophony causes the 
following effects:
•	 All Good-aligned living listeners must make a Control 
Resistance or be stunned (held inactive) for the duration of the 
skill.
•	 For every full minute, all Good-aligned living listeners have a 
20% chance per Practitioner Title of gaining a random Insanity.
•	 All Evil-aligned and undead listeners suddenly receive a burst 
of divinely inspired energy and are +5 to hit and +5 to damage.
•	 There is a 10% chance per Practitioner Title that 2d4 Evil-
aligned supernatural beings will be drawn to the cacophony 
and appear within the radius of affect.
Special Notes: This skill may be combined with Bellow, causing 
the radius of hearing distance to expand even farther. The bonuses 
from the social skill Music Theory do not apply to the skill 
Cacophony.
Critical Failure: The skill user is fatigued and suffers –20% to all 
skills for 2 minutes.
Critical Success: All Good-aligned supernatural beings must 
make a Control Resistance or be banished to their individual home 
planes.
Repeat Failure: The skill user becomes unconscious for 1d4 hours 
and suffers –60% to all skills for 24 hours after awakening.
Requirements: Title 10, Bellow, Discord, Hymn Lore, Intone, 
Psalm Lore, and Whisper.
CAUSTOKINESIS
Attributes: Intelligence, Aura		
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: 10 Seconds
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill represents the ability to manipulate acid 
and acidity.
General Usage: The user concentrates on the desired effect and 
mentally wills it to happen. Unlike casting spells, the amount of 
Aura needed to create an effect is constant. The Aura is drained 
from the practitioner’s Aura Pool and returns at her Aura 
Regeneration Rate. Note: Class Title in these usages always refers 
to the Class Title of the practitioner, even when the verbiage 
seems to indicate otherwise. Unless otherwise specified, effects are 
instantaneous in duration and have a range of 10’ per Class Title.
Sense Acidity (8 Aura; +50% modifier, 5 seconds): Allows the skill 
user to tell how acidic or alkaline a liquid is without touching it 
and whether from these factors alone it is safe to touch, drink, or 
use. Usage of this skill does not detect toxins, diseases, or other 
forms of dangers that may be present in the liquid. 
Etch (10 Aura; +40% modifier, 1 minute): Produces small amounts 
of acid which etches an image into a surface in the form visualized 
by the skill user. Surfaces which are magical or within the Aura 
field of another being are afforded a Magic Resistance to avoid 
being etched. The etching is permanent.
Alter pH (12 Aura; +30% modifier, 10 seconds): Allows the 
practitioner to permanently alter the pH of up to 1 gallon of liquid 
per Class Title 1 point in either direction. Successive uses of this 
skill are cumulative, but liquid can never be altered more than 5 
points in one direction or another from its original pH. A pH of 7 
is neutral; a pH of less than 7 is acidic, while a pH of greater than 
7 is alkaline. Damage from acidity can be strengthened by 1d10 
for each level of pH lower than 4 or lowered by 1d10 for each pH 
closer to 7. At 4 or higher. no significant acidic damage is done. 
Inert Defense (14 Aura; +20% modifier, 5 seconds): Creates an 
invisible sphere around the practitioner that causes any caustic 
substance passing into or out of the sphere to be shifted to a pH of 
7. The substance still strikes the practitioner (or leaves the sphere, 
as applicable), but no acid damage is sustained. The sphere does 
not restrict the movement of physical objects in either direction. 
The sphere lasts for 10 seconds per Class Title.
Acid Trap (15 Aura; +15% modifier, 10 minutes): Creates a trapped 
area no larger than 5 ft² per Class Title. This area is a set trap that, 
when touched by another Aura field, will be triggered and cause 
sprays of acid to come up/out from the area trapped, inflicting 
1d10 magical acid damage per Practitioner Title to 1d4 areas 
struck. Half damage is taken if a Magic Resistance succeeds, and no 
damage is taken if a Magic Resistance succeeds by half or less. The 
damage applies to armor first, destroying it at a rate of 1 point per 
point of acid damage done. Magical Armor can completely resist 
acid damage if it makes a Magic Resistance. The trap can only be 
triggered once. The sprays of acid can be narrowed or channeled 
by nozzles, slits, holes, etc. by setting the trap below or behind the 
channeling method. This can cause the area affected to narrow to 
target a specific height or location. The Acid Trap will last for 1 
hour per Class Title once set. Alternately 1/10th of a Will Force can 
be spent to make the trap permanent, resetting every 10 seconds 
once triggered. 
Caustic Bolt (16 Aura; +10% modifier, 10 seconds): Causes a bolt 
of acid to shoot from the skill user’s finger and strike a target if 
an Intelligence save is successful. The Caustic Bolt does 1d10 
damage per Class Title. Half damage is taken if a Magic Resistance 
succeeds, and no damage is taken if a Magic Resistance succeeds 
by half or less. The Caustic Bolt destroys armor and hide at a 1 
to 1 ratio before it affects flesh. The remaining damage is applied 
directly to the body part struck.  Magical armor will negate the 
Caustic Bolt if a Magic Resistance is made for the armor.

is successful, the practitioner gets a +20% to Magic Resistance for 
that attack and any damage from the attack is reduced by -1 per 
die. 
Critical Success: 1/2 Aura requirements.
Critical Failure: Skill user is unable to use Caustokinesis for 1 
minute and must make a Will Force save or suffer mental fatigue.
Repeat Failure: Treat 3 repeat failures as a Critical Failure.
Requirements: Title 5, Kinetics Knowledge, and Kinetics Lore.

CONSIPICIOUS CONCEALMENT
Attributes: Agility, Intelligence	
Rating: 17
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: 1 second
Type: Stealth/Intrusive	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: Allows the practitioner to stand unseen in plain sight 
in any environment. 
General Usage: When the practitioner wishes, she may remain 
unnoticed in plain sight of all around her. This effect lasts as 
long as the practitioner remains relatively still, leaning against 
a wall or tree, seated on a bench, etc. The practitioner is neither 
camouflaged nor is she invisible; she is simply overlooked or 
dismissed as irrelevant by anyone glancing her way. This skill 
requires the practitioner to remain in the same place for 1 second 
before making a skill roll. Success indicates that anyone looking 
her way, even directly at her, will not notice her presence. Donning 
concealing clothing, hiding in a crowd, or remaining completely 
motionless is unnecessary.
Notes: This skill is only proof against visual inspection. Life 
Sense and similar effects will still detect the practitioner.  Anyone 
looking specifically for the practitioner (they must know her face 
and generally how she is currently dressed) is afforded a single 
Perception Check to see through the effects of this skill.  
Special Notes: Anyone looking directly at the practitioner for 
5 or more seconds will see the practitioner without needing a 
Perception Check if they are separated by less than 20 ft. minus 
1’ per full 10% of the skill chance, with a maximum reduction of 
10 ft. For example, if Alea has a 76% chance in this skill and is 
standing 12 ft. from Tamrien, Tamrien will be able to see Alea if he 
looks directly at her for 5 seconds (76/10=7, 20-7=13, 13>12). If 
she were 13’ away or more, Tamrien would be unable to see her.
Critical Success: Perception Checks can no longer see through the 
effect.
Critical Failure: The practitioner is readily discernible by anyone 
looking in her direction.
Requirements: Title 5 and Shadowing.

DECEPTION
Attributes: Aura, Will Force

Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: Allows the practitioner to permanently plant a single,

persons while speaking and chooses a single, simple untruth to 
plant into their minds, e.g. they’re descended from royalty, or that

effect.

until the skill chance is increased.
Critical Success: The Aura cost is halved but still affects only the 
originally applicable number of targets. E.g. the skill used at 20 
Aura will affect 3 people; if a critical success is made, it only costs 
10 Aura but still affects only 3 people.

Attributes: Will Force	
	
Rating: 16
Start Bonus: 2d6%		
	
Time: 5 seconds
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill represents the ability to defy and strongly

lowering the practitioner’s supernatural footprint. This allows him

the practitioner to avoid the Defy Divinity effect dropping. If the 
practitioner falls unconscious, then the effect automatically drops.
Special usage: The state of defying divinity can be turned off at will 
after 1 second of concentration. No skill roll is required. 
Critical Success: An additional +5% modifier applies to all 
resistances against divine-based sources.  
Critical Failure: No additional attempts may be made to enter a 
state of defying divinity for 1 hour. Mental fatigue is accrued.   
Repeat Failure: Treat 3 repeat failures as a Critical Failure.
Requirements: Title 5 and the skills Defy Magic, Fearless, and 
Steadfast.

failure occurs. This skill may not be used non-acquired.

to the Commune chance bonus.
Critical Failure: All those who were attempting to engage in 
Devout Supplication must make a Piety save to avoid Divine 
Denial for a period of one hour.
Requirements: Title 7, Divine Knowledge, and 9 divine magical 
skills.
DISAPPEAR
Attributes: Aura, Will Force	 	
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 2d6%		
	
Time: 1 Minute
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: Causes the practitioner to appear to have simply 
ceased to be.
General Usage: After spending one minute concentrating, a skill 
roll is made. Success indicates that for one hour per Practitioner 
Title the practitioner cannot be detected by any sense, magical 
or otherwise, including but not limited to sight, hearing, heat 
patterns, odor, life sense, air movement, mental contact, detection 
effects, etc. To those with magical tracking abilities, the caster has 
simply ceased to exist. Additionally, this skill works as though the 
spell Non-Detection had been cast on the practitioner. The effect 
lasts until the end of the duration or until the caster takes any form 
of hostile action.
Notes: Detect Protection is the only effect that detects the 
practitioner, and even then, only detects that Disappear is in use. 
Critical Success: The duration is doubled.
Critical Failure: The practitioner may not again attempt Disappear 
until the following day.
Requirements: Title 10, Conspicuous Concealment, and Scroll 
Knowledge.
DISCORD
Attributes: Piety, Will Force	 	
Rating: 14
Start Bonus: 2d6%		
	
Time: 5 Seconds
Type: Divine Magical	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill causes sounds (including music, speech, 
and mechanical noise) within earshot of the skill user to sound like 
discordant, jarring noise. 
General Usage: The skill user concentrates on the targeted source 
of sound (up to 1 per Practitioner Title) for 5 seconds and makes 
a skill roll. Failure indicates no effect. Success indicates a sudden 
change in the source’s sound, creating unintelligible, clashing 
bedlam. If the skill user targets himself, anything he says or sings 
during the skill’s duration will be affected. This effect lasts for 1 
minute per Practitioner Title, after which a new skill roll must be 
made to continue affecting the targeted source of sound (the user 
may reroll at any point before the duration is up to continue the 
discord without interruption).
Special Uses: This skill may be used to “adjust” a musician’s 
performance, making the music terribly off-pitch instead of in 
tune, or the skill user may cancel out the effects of a song, ballad, 
rhythm, hymn, or psalm being sung or played by any Good-
aligned user. For instance, a Dark Dwarf Cacophonist may use this 
skill to cancel out the effects of a River Midfolk Bard’s “Song of 
Flying.” Since this skill also garbles speech, it can be used to disrupt 
spellcasting, invoking, rituals, and skills requiring speech (such as 
Deception). Anyone wishing to resist the effect of the skill Discord 
is allowed a Control Resistance.
Special Notes: If this skill is being used specifically to counter 
the effects of the Harmony skill, there is a contest of Will Force 
between the two skill users; the targeted sound will be controlled 
by whoever makes their Will Force save by the greatest amount.
Critical Failure: The skill user must wait 1 hour before attempting 
to affect this sound again and now has mental fatigue.
Critical Success: Any resulting discord cannot be canceled by the 
skill Harmony.
Repeat Failure: The targeted sound becomes even more 
discordant, and all listeners other than the practitioner must make 
a Will Force save or attempt to either stop the sound or go where 
they cannot hear it.
Requirements: Title 4 and Intone.

General Usage: While awake, the practitioner concentrates for 1

hostile and even attack the practitioner unless she uses an effect 
such as Tame Animal, Speak to Animal, etc. The summoned dream 
animal will remain for 1 hour per Class Title of the practitioner. 
Alternately, the practitioner can use this skill on the Dream Plane 
to call either a specific dream animal or the nearest dream animal

DREAM CREATE
Attributes: Aura, Will Force	 	
Rating: 16
Start Bonus: 2d6%		
	
Time: 1 minute
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: By means of this skill a practitioner can create or 
summon a dream object. 
General Usage: The practitioner must first Dream Shift or Plane 
Shift/Walk to the Dream Plane and then concentrate for 1 minute 
on the object they wish to create. The object can weigh no more 
than 5 lb. per Class Title and may be no more than 1 ft3 per Class 
Title. If the skill roll is made, then the item appears as it was 
imagined in the hands or at the feet of the practitioner (depending 
on size). The item is only as good as the practitioner can imagine it; 
thus, it will be a serviceable item of that type unless the practitioner 
has applicable social skills for that item type to improve its quality. 
Once an item is created on the Dream Plane, it will always exist 
unless removed or destroyed. It will drop wherever the practitioner 
leaves it or where she leaves the Dream Plane. 
Special Usage: The practitioner may summon items as follows:
Summon Item on the Dream Plane: The practitioner can spend 10 
seconds, make a successful skill roll at +20%, and summon any 
dream item they have previously created from anywhere on the 
Dream Plane to themselves somewhere else on the Dream Plane. 
Only the item comes. If the item was a container, anything within it 
is left where it was before being summoned. 

===== PAGE 121 =====
115
Summon Item from the Dream Plane: The practitioner can spend 10 minutes and make a successful skill roll at -20% to summon one of 
their dream objects from the Dream Plane onto another plane. The dream object is now with the practitioner outside the Dream Plane 
and is no longer summonable on the Dream Plane. The object appears in every way to be a normal object of that type, but a residue of the 
practitioner’s Aura identifies the magical origin of the item. Also, the item is considered supernatural (origin Dream Plane) and detectable 
as such. The object can be sent back to the Dream Plane in the last place the practitioner appeared there with a normal skill roll. If the 
dream item was magical (through use of the skill Dream Enchant), then it is not magical outside of the Dream Plane unless permanent 
Will Force is spent upon the summoning of the item to make the enchantments real (outside of the Dream Plane.) If this Will Force is 
spent, then the item is now permanently magical and cannot be sent back to the Dream Plane. 
Critical Failure: No further attempt may be made to create this type of object until the skill chance increases, and no further attempt may 
be made to summon that particular dream item this night. 
Critical Success: The dream item has a +10% chance to be summoned in the future (inside or outside of the Dream Plane)
Repeat Failure: Treat three failed attempts as a critical failure.
Requirements: Title 5 and Dream Shift.
DREAM ENCHANT
Attributes: Aura, Will Force	 	
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: Varies
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill can be used for a multitude of purposes around imbuing, enchanting, and disenchanting items on the Dream 
Plane. 
General Usage: While on the Dream Plane, this skill allows the practitioner to enchant magic items in a fashion similar to the skills 
Empower, Metal Lore, Stone Lore, Wood Lore, Crystal Lore, etc. and as shown on the tables below for armor, weapons, and miscellaneous 
items, with the following restrictions:
•	 The enchantment(s) are dream enchantment(s) and therefore can only be created and used on the Dream Plane. 
•	 Time spent to enchant can be done in successive dreams spend on the Dream Plane. 
•	 Temporary enchantments disappear the moment the practitioner leaves the Dream Plane. 
•	 Permanent enchantments result in a temporary loss of Will Force spent which return at a rate of 1 per hour.
•	 No more than 1 dream enchanted item per Class Title can exist at any given time. 
•	 Once the practitioner returns to the Dream Plane, dream enchanted items always appear in the practitioner’s Aura field, no matter 
where they had been while the practitioner was away from the Dream Plane. 
•	 A dream enchanted item is not considered magical if taken out of the Dream Plane. However, it will appear to have a permanent 
magical residue of the practitioner’s Aura. An item can be made magical if the temporary Will Force cost to make it on the Dream 
Plane is paid permanently (see Dream Create). Once that cost is paid, the item no longer counts as a dream enchanted item and is now 
a true magical item of supernatural origin (Dream Plane).

Dream Enchant Armor Notes: The armor and its powers and abilities are considered to be an Aura level of 2x the Class Title of the 
practitioner plus the Aura Control modifier for Intelligence. Temporary Will Force cost is half of the number of Enchant slots used. Thus, 
if 2 Enchant slots are used, then 1 temporary Will Force is spent. If no Enchant slots are used, then the cost is 1/10th of a Will Force per 

===== PAGE 122 =====
116
magical plus of the item.
Enchants: The following enchantments can be applied in any order, limited by the number of available enchant slots: Adhere, Catch, Clean, 
Distortion, Duplicate Self, Float (weightless armor), Fade, Force Armor, Invisibility, Invulnerability, Protection, Rebound*, Repair, Reflection, 
Repulsion, Silence, Size Change (to fit wearer), Spell Turning.
Armor Threshold: This is not the amount the armor protects but the point at which the armor has a chance of breaking. Threshold is 
determined by taking the final magical armor value and setting the threshold by percentage of this value as shown. Every point above 
this threshold adds a 1% chance that the armor will be broken. Thus +2 plate armor thus has a damage threshold of 66 (33 magical 
armor value) x 150%. If a 70-point blow strikes the armor, there is a 4% chance the armor will be broken (70-66 = 4). If the armor is not 
broken, it still takes 1 point of damage from the attack that exceeded its threshold. The armor value is then reduced by 1 and threshold is 
recalculated. Damaged magical armor can only be repaired by magical means.
Energy Endure: One enchant slot can be used to provide the ability Endure of 1 energy type (magical and normal) making the wearer 
immune to that energy damage type. This effect is considered an ability and is thus constant but does not require a slot that is constant/
at will. Any slot used becomes a constant ability when this effect is imbued. The type is based on Class Title or less. Thus, a 7th Ttitle 
practitioner could make an armor piece with Endure Heat, Endure Kinetic, Endure Cold, or Endure Sonic. Only 1 Endure energy effect 
can be applied to the armor. 
*These spells/powers appear in a future bestiary.

Dream Enchant Weapon Notes: The weapon and its powers and abilities are considered to be an Aura level of 2x the Class Title of the 
practitioner plus the Aura Control modifier for Intelligence. Temporary Will Force cost is half of the number of Enchant slots used. Thus, 
if 2 Enchant slots are used, then 1 temporary Will Force is spent. If no Enchant slots are used, then the cost is 1/10th of a Will Force per + 
of the item.
Enchants: The following enchantments can be applied in any order, limited by the number of available enchant slots: Accuracy, Animate 
Object, Clean, Disruption, Foe Strike*, Frictionless, Fulcrum, Invulnerability, Lesser Force Weapon**, Phase Weapon, Piercing, Repair, 
Shadow Weapon, Sharpness.
Skills and Weapon Speed: Speed and skill modifiers are GM optional. Decreases to weapon speed do not lower the minimum weapon 
speed, only the starting weapon speed. If the adjustment would lower the minimum weapon speed, then it will not lower it further. Thus, 
even a +10 dagger still has a 2 second weapon speed.
Weapon Threshold: This is the amount the weapon strength increases. Thus a +2 longsword has 68 weapon strength. A normal long sword 
has a 44 weapon strength (x150% = 67.5 or 68). Since a longsword is made of forged metal which has an object strength of 35, each point 
over 103 (68+35) adds a 1% chance the weapon will break and lose its enchantments. A +2 Mithreel longsword  that parries an attack 
of 110 damage would have a 7% chance of breaking (110-103=7). Even if the weapon does not break, it will take 1 point of damage and 
decrease its strength by that same 1 point. Damaged magical weapons can only be repaired by magical means.
Energy Damage: The weapon can use 1 enchant slot to inflict magical energy damage upon a successful hit (if the target’s Magic Resistance 
fails). When calculating energy damage, the number of dice is per Class Title of the Dream Enchanter, and any energy of the current Class 
Title of below can be chosen. For instance, a 7th Title practitioner could use 1 enchant slot to add flaming, repulsion, cold, or sonic energy 
damage. Energy effects are considered abilities and are thus constant but do not require a slot that is constant/at will. It can be any enchant 
slot, though only 1 energy type is allowed per weapon.

*These spells/powers appear in a future bestiary. Any slot used becomes a constant ability when this effect is imbued.
**Lesser Force Weapon creates a temporary magical force weapon of the + shown on the table and of the desired weapon type. Lesser 
Force Weapon lacks the automatic Sharpness, Disruption, etc. of Force Weapon.
