SYMPATHIZE
Attributes: Piety	
	
	
Rating: 16
Start Bonus: 2d6%		
	
Time: 10 seconds
Type: Divine Magical	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: Removes damage from one being while applying it to 
another. 
General Usage: The skill user concentrates for 10 seconds on any 
two beings within 3’ per Will Force rating of the practitioner (the 
practitioner himself can be one of the targets). After a successful 
skill roll, both targets are afforded a Magic Resistance, if desired. 
If either makes a Magic Resistance, nothing happens; otherwise, 
all current physical and magical damage is moved from the first 
target to the second target in each body area they have in common. 
Nothing happens with body areas the two targets do not have in 
common, such as between a centaur’s hind leg or avian’s wing 
trying to be moved to a human.
Special Notes: The new wounds created are identical to the 
lessened wounds. For instance, if one target is burned, burns at half 
the damage would appear on the second target as they are fading 
on the original target. Poison, disease, control, hold effects, mental 
effects, etc. are not affected by this skill.
Critical Success: Each body area’s wound is reduced by 1d4+1.
Critical Failure: No additional attempts may be made to 
sympathize between these two targets for 1 hour, and the 
practitioner now has mental fatigue. 
Repeat Failure: Treat 3 repeat failures as a Critical Failure.
Requirements: Title 11, Divine Knowledge, Equalize, and Life 
Sense.
TEMPOROKINESIS
Attributes: Intelligence, Aura		
Rating: 20
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: Varies
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: Grants the ability to magically manipulate time, 
which is generally a terrible idea.  
General Usage: The user concentrates on the desired effect and 
mentally wills it to happen. Unlike casting spells, the amount of 
Aura needed to create an effect is constant. The Aura is drained 
from the practitioner’s Aura Pool and returns at her Aura 
Regeneration Rate. Note: Class Title in these usages always refers 
to the Class Title of the practitioner, even when the verbiage 
seems to indicate otherwise. Unless otherwise specified, effects are 
instantaneous in duration and have a range of 10’ per Class Title.
Slow (14 Aura; +30% modifier, 5 seconds): Causes 1 being within 
sight of the practitioner to move through time at a slightly faster 
rate than everyone else. The user concentrates on the target 
and makes a skill roll. Success indicates that the target becomes 
relatively slower to observers for 10 seconds per Practitioner Title. 
The target becomes slowed by 1 second per Practitioner Title (up 

===== PAGE 164 =====
158
to a maximum of 10 seconds). Slow seconds are applied first, so if 
there are 5 slowed seconds (5th Practitioner Title), then each of the 
first 5 seconds takes 1 second longer. Target beings are allowed a 
Magic Resistance to negate this effect.  
Haste (16 Aura; +20% modifier, 5 seconds): Causes 1 willing being 
within sight of the practitioner to move through time at a slightly 
slower rate than everyone else. The user concentrates on the target 
and makes a skill roll. Success indicates that the target become 
relatively faster to observers for 10 seconds per Practitioner Title. 
The target becomes hasted by 1 second per Practitioner Title (up 
to a maximum of 10 seconds). Haste seconds are applied first, so if 
there are 5 hasted seconds (5th Practitioner Title), then each of the 
first 5 seconds gets an additional second of action. Target beings 
are allowed a Magic Resistance to negate this effect if requested.  
Time Sight (18 Aura; +10% modifier, 10 minutes): Causes the 
practitioner to see up to 1 day forward or backward in time per 
Practitioner Title in the area the practitioner is present in. Futures 
seen are possible futures and the very act of seeing the future can 
change it (at GM’s discretion).
Stasis Trap (18 Aura; +10% modifier, 10 minutes): Creates a 
trapped area no larger than 5 ft² per Class Title. This area is a set 
trap that, when touched by another Aura field, will be triggered, 
causing the target to make a Magic Resistance or be held in stasis 
for 10 seconds per Practitioner Title. While in stasis, the affected 
being or creature cannot be harmed. The trap can only be triggered 
once. The Stasis Trap will last for 1 hour per Class Title once set. 
Alternatively, 1/10th of a Will Force can be spent to make the trap 
permanent, resetting every 10 seconds once triggered. 
Specialization Ability, Time Stop (20 Aura; no modifier, 5 seconds): 
Causes 1 being within sight of the practitioner to make a Magic 
Resistance or be nearly frozen in time as per the spell Stasis. This 
effect last for 1 minute per Practitioner Title. While a target is in 
stasis, it cannot be damaged. 
Mastery Ability, Temporal Shift (22 Aura; -10% modifier, 1 minute): 
Allows the practitioner to permanently expend Will Force to 
move through time. Movement can be either forward or backward 
through time at a distance of 1 hour per Will Force point spent. 
The Temporal Shift is permanent, unless the practitioner expends 
additional Will Force to return to his original time. The Will Force 
used to power this usage may come from a Will Force reservoir.
Critical Success: Half Aura requirements.
Critical Failure: The skill user is unable to use Temporokinesis for 
1 minute and must make a Will Force save or suffer mental fatigue.
Repeat Failure: Treat 3 repeat failures as a Critical Failure.
Requirements: Title 10, Kinetics Knowledge, Kinetics Lore, and 
Kinetics Mastery.

TRANQUILITY
Attributes: Intelligence, Will Force	
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: N/A
Type: Disciplined, Magical	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: The ability to create perfect mystical stability within 
one’s mind.
General usage: The skill user enters a meditative state and then 
must succeed at both a Meditation roll and a Flowing Thought 
roll first before rolling Tranquility. If the Tranquility skill roll is 
successful, the skill user gains the following benefits in addition to 
those of Meditation and Flowing Thought:
•	 Aura regeneration occurs as if the practitioner were 1 
Practitioner Title higher (2 Titles total with Flowing Thought).
•	 +1 Intelligence per full 30% of Tranquility (+6 total maximum)
•	 Is immune to illusions
•	 Is immune to and cannot be afflicted by insanity; if previously 
insane, Tranquility immediately cures the insanity
•	 Is immune to mood changes and effects
•	 Is immune to Control Resistance penalties due to a high 
Appearance and/or Charm of an opponent
•	 Gains an additional -1 to Initiative if Intelligence is used for 
initiative
•	 Skills or effects that scan the surface of the skill user’s mind (for 
example, Mind Dance) only reveal a state of calm.
•	 Mental Combat cannot be initiated against the skill user unless 
the skill user allows it.
•	 If the skill user enters mental combat, Will Force loss resulting 
from attacks and defenses used against the skill user is reduced 
by 2 to a minimum of 1.
The effects of this skill last for a number of days equal to the skill 
user’s Class Title. In addition, the durations of the effects of both 
the Meditate skill and the Flowing Thought skill are also extended 
to a number of days equal to the skill user’s Class Title.
Special Usage: Any time the skill user fails a Will Force save 
to avoid Insanity, he may roll Tranquility as a second chance to 
avoid the Insanity. Even if the Tranquility save is failed as well, the 
insanity suffered is generally extremely mild, lasts at most 1d10 

===== PAGE 165 =====
159
minutes, and is never a psychotic break
Notes: May not be used non-acquired.
Special Notes: The skills Berserk and Blood Lust are impossible 
to use while under the effects of Tranquility. Also, a Mind Blast 
practitioner may initiate mental combat against a Tranquility 
practitioner; however, the extra effects of both skills are ignored. 
Instead, treat the mental combat as a standard mental combat. 
Note that the effects of Meditate and Flowing Thought still apply.
Requirements: Title 11, Body Control, Flowing Thought, and 
Meditate.
TRUE DREAM
Attributes: Aura, Will Force	 	
Rating: 20
Start Bonus: 1d6%		
	
Time: 1 Hour
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: Allows the practitioner to create or alter the 
dreamscape itself while on the Dream Plane. 
General Usage: The practitioner concentrates for 1 hour and 
makes a skill roll. If the skill roll is made, 100 ft3 per Class Title 
of the dreamscape (the terrain on the Dream Plane) is created or 
changed as desired. This includes creation of a desired landscape, 
forming of structures and items, etc. within the area of effect. 
Notes: When this skill is acquired, all item limits for the skill 
Dream Create are removed, and those for the skill Dream Enchant 
are doubled. Parts of the dreamscape created by other beings 
cannot be altered while they are present on the Dream Plane, nor 
can the practitioner’s areas be modified by others while she is 
present. 
Special Usage: One area created in this fashion can be declared 
the home of the practitioner. The dream home gives the following 
benefits and effects:
•	 The dream home cannot be changed by another until the 
practitioner who creates it dies permanently. 
•	 The practitioner is now home at this place on the Dream Plane. 
If this being is banished from any other plane, they will appear 
here. 
•	 The practitioner is now considered supernatural on all planes 
except the Dream Plane. 
•	 The area designated is treated as the spell Enchant Area (for 
the practitioner) whether she has the spell or not. See the spell 
Enchant Area in the Player’s Guide 
•	 Barriers (invisible or otherwise) appear around the area. 
These are only permeable to the practitioner’s allies. A door 
or entrance must be designated, along with a way to open 
that door and enter the area. This opening must be achievable 
to an average dreamer, but it can be abstract like a code, 
combination, or through a series of dream items, etc. The door 
should take no more than 10 minutes to open through the 
specified method. 
•	 If the practitioner is immortal, dying causes their body to 
reform at the dream home’s center, heart, or designated area as 
the spell Rebirth (see the Player’s Guide) with the requisite loss 
of Will Force. 
•	 If the being is irrevocably killed or killed in their home, then 
the area (or part of it) becomes a Ravening Haunt (see this 
creature in Mysteries of the Planes).
Critical Failure: No further attempts this day may be made to alter 
or create a new dreamscape. 
Critical Success: The area created can be 20% larger. 
Repeat Failure: Treat 3 failed attempts as a critical failure.
Requirements: Title 15.

Description: The very presence of the practitioner bolsters the

•	 +20% to morale checks per Practitioner Title
•	 All wounds are healed 1d4 points per Practitioner Title.

effects:
•	 Evil beings with a Will Force of 15 or less must make a Control

•	 All Evil beings remaining in the area of effect must make a

•	 Undead are turned or destroyed as the skill Turn Undead.
•	 -20% to morale checks per Practitioner Title (-100% 
maximum)
•	 Notes: This skill can only be used once per day. The effects last

Critical Success: The area of effect is doubled.
Critical Failure: The practitioner may not attempt this skill again 
for the rest of the day.
Requirements: Title 10 and 12 divine magical skills. 
UMBRAKINESIS
Attributes: Intelligence, Aura		
Rating: 12
Start Bonus: 2d10%	
	
Time: Varies
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: A perversion of Lumokinesis, this skill grants the 
ability to magically create or alter shadows and darkness.
General Usage: The user concentrates on the desired effect and 
mentally wills it to happen. Unlike casting spells, the amount of 
Aura needed to create an effect is constant. The Aura is drained 
from the practitioner’s Aura Pool and returns at her Aura 
Regeneration Rate. Note: Class Title in these usages always refers 
to the Class Title of the practitioner, even when the verbiage 
seems to indicate otherwise. Unless otherwise specified, effects are 
instantaneous in duration and have a range of 10’ per Class Title.
Blind (16 Aura; -20% modifier, 5 seconds): Causes 1 being to be 
blinded by a darkness over their visional sense for 10 seconds per 
Practitioner Title.

160
Cast Shadow (6 Aura; +30% modifier, 2 seconds): Causes darkness 
to emit from an object or being, creating a desired shadow for 1 
hour per Class Title. This shadow extends outward from the object 
or being up to 5’ per Class Title. 
Dim (10 Aura; +10% modifier, 1 second): Causes light to weaken 
within a 5’ radius per Practitioner Title, decreasing light at the 
practitioner’s discretion by up to 10% per Practitioner Title. This

Fade to Gray (6 Aura; +30% modifier, 5 seconds): Removes all color 
from a being, object, or area, making light that reflects from them 
only do so in various shades of gray. Living things and magic items 
are afforded a Magic Resistance to negate these effects. If cast on an

Move Unseen, and Shadowing and lasts for 1 hour per Class Title.
Fade Sight (8 Aura; +20% modifier, 2 seconds): Must be used on 
a being with some form of vision. This causes their vision to fade 
to half strength reducing the range of their vision by half and 
lowering Perception to half when sight is used. Victims get a Magic 
Resistance to avoid this effect. 
Shade (10 Aura; +10% modifier, 5 seconds): Causes 1 being to be 
surrounded by a gray shadow, affording a bonus of -2 to be hit with 
melee and -4 to be hit with missile weapons. This effect lasts 10 
seconds per Practitioner Title. This gray shadow is lost when the 
target being becomes invisible or faded. 
Image (16 Aura; -20% modifier, 10 seconds): Creates a three-
dimensional projection of an imagined image in shades of gray. 
This image may be animated, but this requires concentration. Alert 
viewers are afforded an Illusion Resistance to notice that it has no 
substance and is only shadow. Lasts 10 minutes per Practitioner 
Title or until dismissed by the skill user.
Shadow Trap (15 Aura; -15% modifier, 10 minutes): Creates a 
trapped area no larger than 5 ft² per Class Title. This area is a set 
trap that, when touched by another Aura field, will be triggered, 
causing a darkness field to momentarily appear. A Magic 
Resistance is required for all within 20’ of the triggered trap or they 
will be struck blind for 10 minutes per Practitioner Title. The trap 
can only be triggered once. The Shadow Trap will last for 1 hour 
per Class Title once set. Alternately 1/10th of a Will Force can be 
spent to make the trap permanent, resetting every 10 seconds once 
triggered. 
Shadow Vision (12 Aura; no modifier, 10 seconds): Amplifies 
and shifts the frequency of light which enters the skill user’s eyes 
allowing them to see outside the visible spectrum and in low light 
conditions. This provides the user with Farsight, Ultravision, 
Infravision, Underwater vision, or Night Vision (Enhanced) 
as desired for 1 hour per Class Title. It also allows them to see 
through any darkness or shadow effects they have created (by skill, 
spell, or ability) as if they were not there.
Specialization Ability, Fade (Varies, see below, 5 seconds): Causes 
light to fade around the user, making her partially invisible. The 
field starts to take effect immediately and fully establishes itself at 
the completion of the skill. The user is partially invisible (-4 to be 
hit), leaving only a gray shadow in the air. The Aura required and 
difficulty of the skill is based on the ambient light level where the 
user is. Whenever the lighting conditions change, a new skill roll 
must be made but no additional aura is consumed. Any loss of 
concentration, attacking, or other offensive action ends the field. 
Picking up or dropping an object creates a momentary increase in 
light where the object enters or exits the field. This effect persists 
for 1 minute per Class Title. With a Critical Success, only half the 
Aura is required, no increase of light is visible, and the user is at a 
-8 to be hit due to being invisible.

Description: Allows the practitioner to combine multiple effects of

Caustokinesis, Cryokinesis, Electrokinesis, Energetic Dissolution,

combining Sonokinesis and Cryokinesis). Each individual effect

Special Notes: The time required to execute this skill is equal to the

Mastery. It is executed as one skill, however, rather than separate 
rolls.
Critical Failure: This specific combination of effects may not be 
attempted again until the Unification skill chance has increased.

USURP CONTROL
Attributes: Aura, Will Force	 	
Rating: 18
Start Bonus: 1d10%	
	
Time: 10 Seconds
Type: Magical	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: Allows the practitioner to take over an existing 
control effect of an already controlled being or creature, or to 
remove the controlling effect from a controlled being or creature.
General Usage: The practitioner first determines that a being 
or creature is controlled, either through directly observing the 
controlling influence or by making mental contact with the being 
or creature through skills or effects like Mind Dance, Though 
Projection, telepathy, etc. The skill user then attempts to usurp 
control with a contest of a skill roll versus the skill or effect that 
initially controlled the being or creature. If the effect is a spell or 
invocation, then the opposing chance is at 5% per Aura or Piety 
level. If the controlling effect was initiated by a skill, then that skill 
is rerolled. The practitioner must make her Usurp Control skill 
roll by more than the controlling skill/effect roll. If the practitioner 
wins, then the control is usurped and the control effect now passes 
to the practitioner as if the practitioner had herself caused it. The 
new control is under the same rules and effects as the original 
control, and the duration continues rather than being reset, unless 
a Critical Success is rolled. Only one being or creature can be under 
usurped control at any time; however, Bind Control will allow that 
control to be extended and externalized, and Retain Control can be 
used to extend the duration of the control effect. Once the duration 
has expired, the usurping ends and the controlled being or creature 
is no longer controlled by anyone. 
Special Usage: An uncontested skill roll may be made to simply 
remove the controlling effect from a controlled being or creature. 
The practitioner discerns the control as noted above, then makes 
a skill roll. If successful, the being or creature is afforded a new 
Control Resistance to remove the effect. If no Control Resistance 
was originally granted for the control, then the being or creature is 
freed automatically. 
Critical Failure: No further attempt to usurp control of the 
targeted being or creature may be made until the skill chance is 
increased.
Critical Success: The duration of the controlling effect resets from 
the beginning. 
Repeat Failure: Treat 3 failed attempts as a critical failure.
Requirements: Title 3 and a skill which can cause control or 
control-like effects, such as Charming or Beguile.
VOICES OF CACOPHONY
Attributes: Piety, Will Force	 	
Rating: 20
Start Bonus: 1d6%		
	
Time: 1 Minute
Type: Divine Magical	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: Causes all listeners within a certain distance of the 
skill user to hear a horrendous, discordant noise uttered by a 
horde of supernatural beings surrounding the user. The resulting 
cacophony is worse than the blackest and most evil sound 
imaginable.
General Usage: The skill user spends 10 minutes summoning a 
horde of Evil supernatural beings (specific types are at the GM’s 
discretion). They are invisible to normal vision but can be seen 
with Detect Supernatural, Divine Sight, etc. The supernatural 
beings begin uttering and singing their horrendous discordant 
noise. The skill user cannot command this horde to perform any 
actions other than utter their black speech. The radius of hearing 
distance is 1,000’ per Practitioner Title. The cacophony lasts for 10 
minutes per Practitioner Title, after which the horde fades. This 
horrible noise causes the following effects:
•	 All Good-aligned living and supernatural listeners must make 
a Control Resistance or be stunned (held inactive) for the 
duration of the skill.
•	 For every full minute listening to the cacophony, all Good-
aligned living and supernatural listeners have a 40% chance per 
Practitioner Title of gaining a random Insanity.
•	 All Good-aligned living and supernatural listeners must make 
a Will Force save or permanently lose 1d4 Will Force.
•	 All Evil-aligned living, undead, and supernatural listeners 
suddenly receive a burst of divinely inspired energy and are +2 
to hit and +5 damage per Practitioner Title for the duration of 
the skill.
•	 All Evil-aligned living, undead, and supernatural listeners 
receive 1 Divine Favor point per Practitioner Title.
•	 There is a 10% chance per Practitioner Title that 1d4 Evil-
aligned undead and/or supernatural beings will be drawn to 
the skill user and perform any one action commanded by the 
skill user.
Special Usage: This skill may be combined with Bellow, causing 
the radius of hearing distance to grow. 
Notes: The user must devote full concentration to keeping the 
supernatural beings nearby. If the user takes more than 10 points 
of damage, he must make an Intelligence save at -5% per minute 
the cacophony has been active or be forced to stop. Bonuses from 
the social skill Music Theory do not apply to the skill Voices of 
Cacophony. This skill can only be used once per day.
Critical Failure: The skill user is fatigued and suffers –50% to all 
skills for 10 minutes.
Critical Success: All Good-aligned supernatural beings must 
make a Control Resistance or be banished to their individual home 
planes, and all corpses in the area of effect rise as uncontrolled 
zombies and/or skeletons.
Repeat Failure: The skill user becomes unconscious for 2d4 hours 
and suffers –80% to all skills for 24 hours after awakening.
Requirements: Title 15 and Cacophony.

WEAPON CALL
Attributes: Agility, Will Force	
Rating: 16
Start Bonus: 2d6%		
	
Time: Special
Type: Combat	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: The ability to magically mark weapons and call them 
back to one’s hand. 
General Usage: The practitioner holds a weapon and spends 
10 minutes concentrating on forming a magical bond between 
himself and the weapon. With a successful skill roll, this bond now 
connects the weapon to the practitioner, allowing him to know the 
distance and direction of that weapon anywhere on the same plane. 
The user can mark up to 1 weapon per 3 Class Titles. A second 
Weapon Call skill roll allows the practitioner to summon a marked 
weapon to his hand in 1 second from anywhere on the same plane. 
If the weapon and practitioner are on different planes, the bond is 
still intact but inaccessible.
Special Usage: The practitioner may make a Weapon Dance skill 
roll at the same time as a Weapon Call skill roll to summon a 
marked weapon and add it directly to a current weapon dance (or 
to begin a new weapon dance). Only 1 second total is spent both 
summoning the marked weapon and adding it to a weapon dance. 
Notes: Both the practitioner and his marked weapon detect as 
having a magical effect when sensed with Detect Magic. The 
bond between them can only be dispelled when applied to the 
practitioner, not the weapon. The bond between the practitioner 
and a marked weapon is permanent until dispelled or the user 
releases the bond, either willingly or upon death.
Critical Success: When rolled as part of the initial marking 
process, this grants +20% bonus to any future Weapon Call skill 
rolls in an attempt to call this particular weapon to the user’s hand. 
When rolled to summon a previously marked weapon to the user’s 
hand, this grants a +20% bonus to any Weapon Dance or Weapon 
Parry skill rolls attempted in the same round. 
Critical Failure: When rolled as part of the initial marking 
process, the user cannot attempt to mark this particular weapon 
again until his skill chance improves. When rolled to summon 
a previously marked weapon to the user’ hand, the user cannot 
attempt to call this particular weapon again for 1 hour.
Repeat Failure: Treat 3 failed attempts as a critical failure.
Requirements: Title 7, Weapon Knowledge, and Weapon Dance.
WEAPON DANCE
Attributes: Agility, Will Force	
Rating: 14
Start Bonus: 2d6%		
	
Time: Special
Type: Combat	
	
	
Restricted: Yes
Learn Time: N/A
Description: This skill represents the ability to juggle two weapons 
with the same hand and perform two simultaneous attacks. 
General Usage: The practitioner begins with a primary weapon in 
one hand and then begins juggling an additional weapon with that 
same hand (a skill roll is not necessary). Both weapons must have 
an adjusted weapon speed of 3 seconds or less. The user’s other 
hand is free to either perform an action or wield a third weapon. 
While the practitioner is juggling the two weapons, he can attack 
with both of them in the same second, attacking simultaneously 
using the weapon speed of the slower weapon. Upon making a 
successful to-hit roll with the first weapon, all damage and effects 
are applied normally. A successful attack with the second weapon 
results in damage applied without strength, charging, or diving 
damage bonus modifiers. If either weapon is stuck in the opponent 
or drops to the ground, the juggling ends. If the second weapon’s 
to-hit roll is missed, a second Weapon Dance skill roll can be made 
to recover this weapon and resume juggling after 1 additional 
second is expended by either hand to continue juggling it.
Special Usage: A skill roll can be made to draw a second weapon 
while already holding a first weapon. This action takes only 1 
second, and the second weapon is now considered being juggled.
Notes: The practitioner must make a new Weapon Dance skill roll 
for each attack. This skill may not be combined with Spin Attack or 
Sweep. 
Critical Success: Strength damage can be added to the secondary 
weapon.
Critical Failure: The second weapon drops and the practitioner 
requires an Agility save to avoid being off balance.
Repeat Failure: None.
Requirements: Title 7, Second Weapon Knowledge, Second 
Weapon Lore, Spin Strike, Sweep, Weapon Lore, and Weapon 
Knowledge.

ability to be heard.
General Usage: The skill user performs a quick 5-second ritual 
while concentrating on the target (any living creature with a voice, 
whether animal or humanoid) and must make a skill roll. Failure 
indicates no effect. Success indicates that the reduced hearing 
distance from the target is 10 less feet per Goal of skill user, with 
a minimum of 0 (complete silence). The target’s voice remains 
softened for 10 seconds per Practitioner Title.
Special Uses: Softening somebody’s voice reduces the radius 
of affect for anyone who would be affected by the target’s vocal 
spells or skills (various songs, Battle Cry, Cure Insanity, etc.). 
For instance, a Harmonist might prevent her companions within 
normal hearing distance of a Dark Priest from hearing his evil 
invocation of Command Word, or a Cacophonist might protect 
himself and his companions from a Banshee’s wail or a Siren’s song.
Notes: This skill does not affect the level of success or failure of any 
skill performed by the target; it merely reduces the radius at which 
the target can be heard.
Critical Failure: The skill user must wait 30 seconds before 
attempting again.
Critical Success: Softening of the voice lasts twice as long as it 
normally would have.
Repeat Failure: No further attempts may be made on this target 
until after the Whisper skill chance has been increased.
Requirements: Title 5, Intone, and either Discord or Harmony.

Combat
Martial Knowledge and Lore Stances
The following stances can be learned by a Martial Knowledge practitioner with a successful Martial Knowledge skill roll 
after thirty-six hours of training (per attempt). When Martial Lore is acquired then each stance can be mastered successfully 
with a Martial Lore skill roll with thirty-six hours additional hours of practice per attempt. Each stance provides modifiers 
in combat and can be entered in after 3 seconds of action without a required roll. Only one stance can be entered in at a time 
and while in these stances the practitioner cannot use the basic combat engagements such as desperate defense or furious 
attack. 
See without eyes (Martial Knowledge): Opponents obscured, invisible or in darkness are easier to hit: -8 to hit penalty is 
reduced to -4, defensive adjustment is now gained even against opponents they cannot see and distortion spell/effects are 
ignored. None of these modifiers apply to silenced opponents. 
Mastery (Martial Lore): Unseen opponents are even easier to hit: -8 to hit penalty is reduced to -2, defensive adjustment 
applies against unseen opponents who no longer gain modifiers when attacking from the side or rear. Distortion spell/effects 
are still ignored. None of these modifiers apply to silenced opponents.
Flow as water (Martial Knowledge): Defensive adjustment increases by -6, Dodge, Feint and Sidestep are +30% to skill rolls. 
Offensive actions can be taken but they are with the following modifiers: -2 to hit and damage, +1 second per action. 
Mastery (Martial Lore): Defensive adjustment increases by -8, Dodge, Feint and Sidestep are +50% to skill rolls. Offensive 
actions can be taken with only a -1 to hit penalty.
Strike as wind (Martial Knowledge): Attacks are +3 to hit and damage, starting weapon speeds are reduced by 1 second 
(not to be lowered below minimum.) Initiative rolls are -2. Defensive adjustment decreases by +2. Critical, Focused Attack, 
Perfect Shot skills are at +20% 
Mastery (Martial Lore): Attacks are +4 to hit and damage, and starting weapon speeds are reduced by 2 seconds (not to be 
lowered below minimum). Initiative rolls are -4. Defensive adjustment decreases by +1. Critical, Focused Attack, Perfect 
Shot are at +50% 
Calm in the storm (Martial Knowledge): +25% resistances to effects which hold or effect movement. +10% to resistances 
against control. All Parry skills or martial moves as well as Disarm and Trap Weapon skills are at +10%. +20% to all Agility 
saves.
Mastery (Martial Lore): +50% resistances to effects which hold or effect movement. +20% to resistances against control. All 
Parry skills or martial moves as well as Disarm and Trap Weapon skills are at +25%. +40% to all Agility saves.
Drunken fighting (Martial Knowledge): +2 to hit and +1 per die damage after failing at least 1 Vitality save for intoxication. 
+10% to combat skills and Martial Knowledge attack subskills. If more than 3 saves are failed for intoxication, all modifiers 
are lost and normal intoxication rules apply.
Mastery (Martial Lore): +4 to hit and +2 per die damage after failing at least 1 Vitality save for intoxication. +20% to combat 
skills and Martial Knowledge/Lore attack subskills. If more than 5 saves are failed for intoxication, all modifiers are lost and 
normal intoxication rules apply.
Imagine Jousting 
These are the rules used in tournaments. Obviously, anyone with skill can fight anyway they please when not engaged in a 
ritual tournament. Jousting is the upper echelon of the game of knights, if you discount politics, and as such rules are set.  
The general goal of jousting is unseating your opponent. Which is the equivalent of a knock out in today’s boxing. The horse 
is considered to be off limits as a target except in the most brutal competitions. The examples below are sample tournament 
completions followed by the Imagine combat mechanics.  
All Tournaments: A barrier is raised to just below the average height of a horse’s flanks. This is referred to as the list. One 
knight enters the field on the right side of the list with a shield and a lance. The other enters the other end of the list on 
the opposite side. A signal is given and they charge toward each other holding their shield and aiming with their lance 
until they cross paths and then targets are declared by each and hits are determined. After the damage is calculated and 
applied, resolution occurs. In resolution it is determined if the lance has cracked or broken and if either or both riders were 
unseated. Points or victory is then determined depending on the tournament type. In most tournaments a knight can yield 
due to wounds, inability to mount or stay mounted, or they cannot enter the list and ready themselves.  

===== PAGE 174 =====
168
Combat
Victory by Points: Points determine the outcome of each match. Each match is three runs between two opponents. Points 
are as follows. 1 point for striking your opponent (in the shield or any other legitimate area). 2 points for breaking your 
lance against your opponent. 3 points for an unseating. Broken lances are replaced between runs. Knights can remount 
between runs. The best score wins. If it is tied, runs continue until there is a victor, the tournament host calls a tie or the 
knights agree to a tie.  Points reset after each match between each knight. Losing knights are out of the tournament and 
tournament play continues with the remaining knights until there is only one winner or a tie is declared. If a knight has no 
more lances (because all of them have broken) they are then eliminated (unless the opponent lends them a lance, as this is 
their option in this type of tourney.)
Victory by Unseating: Matches between knights are set into runs. Each run is an opportunity to unseat the other knight. 
The first to hit the ground is eliminated. If they both fall then they may both remount and try again. Runs continue until 
there is a clear elimination by unseating.  The tournament continues as winning knights are matched against each other and 
there is a final unseating between the last two knights that determines the tournament victor. If a knight runs out of lances 
they are then eliminated. Typically, ten lances are considered sufficient for most tournaments. Other knights watching the 
competition may “throw in a lance” by having their squires or men-at-arms give one of their lances to the lanceless knight to 
allow the competition to continue. 
Victory by Elimination: This is the most brutal of tournaments. Knights take runs at each other until one or the other 
yields, is knocked unconscious, or killed. In some of these tournaments the mount is now a legal target. If a knight uses all 
of his lances up they simply draw another weapon. If either mount is killed then one knight stands and is charged by the 
other knight and they exchange one run at each other this way. If both mounts are out, then they simply fight with melee 
weapons in one final run until either one yields, is knocked unconscious, or killed. 
Prizes: In a hosted tournament, the host generally sets prizes that are awarded to the tournament winner, the runner-up, 
and the third-place finisher. In most kingdoms prizes have to be worth enough for the knights to risk their arms and armor, 
their horses, and themselves. Thus, an average first place prize for a yearly tournament might be 200 gold, with 100 gold 
for second and 50 gold for third. Special prizes may be awarded for most unseatings, iron hide (most lances broken against 
them), bravest knight (continuing on while wounded, damaged armor, or without a lance, etc.) these prizes typically are no 
more than the third-place value or 50 gold. 
Honor: Knights may fight for their honor or someone they champion. In some lands, noble women, even married ones, 
will choose champions and the champions will fight for their honor and prestige. Others joust just to see who is best among 
equals.
Dueling: Jousting can also be used as a form of dueling to settle matters of honor. With the loser apologizing to the victor or 
humbling themselves before them.  If the matter of honor is serious it may be handled as a victory by elimination.
Jousting Rules: Initiative is not used in jousting. There is no surprise. Body Parry, Weapon Parry, Critical, Focused Attack 
and Trap Weapon skills are not used. 
Start: Each combatant indicates that they are ready, then a horn is blown or a flag is dropped and the two opponents charge 
at each other on their mounts. If one knight is awaiting a charge because their horse is dead or incapacitated in some 
forms of special jousting, then they stand in center and await the charge. 
Closing: Getting the horse quickly into a gallop requires either a successful Riding skill roll or if they have Horsemanship 
it is an auto success. Skittish horses (non-warhorses) may require a morale check (base 20%) if they are not properly 
trained. Failure of any of these means that the knight must make an Agility save at -20% or fall off their horse before they 
even make contact with their opponent. 
Contact: Each knight declares their target (see the diagram). They then roll to-hit with a 20-sided dice and is considered a 
hit only for a dead center roll (center of attack chart) all others are misses. If an attacking knight has their lance braced 
(Brace skill roll) then they suffer a -2 on their to-hit roll. If one of the knight’s declares that he is moving his shield out of 
position in order to Shield Parry a blow not already aimed for his shield, then the other knight can declare intention to 
hit a different target. The jousters have a contest of Shield Parry versus Weapon Knowledge. If the Shield Parry wins, then 
the weapon is blocked by the shield in the best possible way (knock strike type) with no modifier to the remain seated 
roll. If a hit is determined then damage is assessed based on the type of weapon, and the type of strike (see below.)
Resolution: Depending on the hit, rolls are made to determine if one is unseated, or even remains conscious.  This is based 
on the area struck. If they were struck at all they must make a Riding skill roll or a Horsemanship roll to remain seated. 
Modifier is by the area struck (see below.)
Finish: If the jouster keeps their seat they have finished the run successfully. Points are awarded or the match if they have 
unseated, incapacitated or eliminated their opponent depending on the tournament type.

Strike Type
Once it is determined if the target was struck then it is determined 
how well it was struck. The jouster striking the target makes a Weapon Knowledge skill roll and compares it to the 
opponent’s Horsemanship (or Riding) skill roll to determine the type of hit. The jouster can elect to brace their lance before 
the attack gaining a -20% to their Weapon Knowledge skill roll but they also suffer a -2 to hit when they attack.

Damage Done
Strength of the jouster is ignored for damage bonus purposes. Weight of the horse is applied as a modifier (see below).  
Damage is then applied by weapon type. Generally, lances used in tournaments have blunted tips unless this rule has been 
waived or is being ignored (cheating, etc.). Once all the damage has been determined and the Strike Type and modifiers 
have all been applied then double the damage due to the two jousters charging each other. If both of the jousters choose a 
slower run, then the damaged is not doubled. This is sometimes done in training or when knights give deference to each 
other.

Lance Breaks
Because of the speeds and forces involved damage to the lances can be severe. Chance of damaging or breaking is as shown 
below. Apply all damage the lance does to the opponent to itself as well. Also apply damage to it if it is targeted by the 
opponent based on the opponent’s damage. Damage to the weapon is applied to the weapon strength whenever it exceeds 
the damage threshold. Break chance is for each point done over the threshold. Like all weapons, lances also break when 
weapon strength reaches zero.

‑*May apply to weapon strength or armor damage threshold as relevant (see below). 
Armor: For armor this is not the amount the armor protects but the point at which the armor has a chance of breaking. For 
armor damage, threshold is determined by taking the final magical armor value and setting the threshold by percentage of 
this value as shown. Every point above this threshold adds a 1% chance that the armor will be broken. Thus +2 Mithreel 
platemail has a damage threshold of 66 (or 44 magical armor value x 150%). If a 70-point blow strikes the armor there is a 
4% chance the armor will be broken. 70-66 = 4%. If the armor is not broken it still takes no armor damage. Magical armor 
does not take damage unless it breaks completely. 
Weapons: For weapons this is the amount the weapon strength increases. Thus a +2 longsword has 68 weapon strength. 
A normal long sword has a 44 weapon strength (x150% = 67.5 or 68). A long sword is made of forged metal which has an 
object strength of 35 thus each point over 103 (68+35) adds a 1% chance the weapon will break, losing any enchantments. A 
110-point damage attack parried by a +2 Mithreel longsword thus will have a 7% chance of breaking (110-103=7%). Even if 
the weapon does not break it will take no damage, as magical weapons do not take damage unless they break. 
Note: Speed and Skill modifiers are GM optional modifiers to weapon speed and skill chances with that weapon. Weapon 
speed decreases do not lower the minimum weapon speed, only the starting weapon speed. If the adjustment would lower 
the minimum weapon speed, then it will not lower further. Even a +10 dagger still has a 2 second weapon speed.
Expanded Head Injury Effect (Stroke)
Head Injury: Serious damage to the head (or brain case, reducing Vitality below -10) can cause a stroke. There is a 5% 
chance per damage point under -10 Endurance per hour the wounded being remains in this condition of having internal 
hemorrhaging that induces a stroke (see below). There is also a 1% cumulative chance of a stroke happening every time a 
being/creature with a brain is knocked unconscious because of damage to the head or brain case. The chance is reset when 
magically healed. 
Stroke: This effect is as follows: 5d4 additional damage to the head. No actions may be taken for 1d4 hours. During this time, 
they are suffering from profound confusion and may not recognize anyone or anything. Roll on the table below for effects of 
the stroke.

Expanded Dehydration/Starvation (Base Endurance Damage)
Additional effects that will lead to death if not eased, are added to the effects from the Master’s Manual. Listed below are the 
full, combined effects for these conditions including new damage to Base Endurance at the end of the existing effect. 
Dehydration: Full dehydration effects are as follows: For each full day without water, all physical and mental attributes of a 
character are reduced by four. Additionally, three levels of fatigue are assessed, eventually requiring Vitality saves to avoid 
passing out. Once adequate water has been ingested, attribute points are restored at the rate of eight per day. In addition 
to these effects after three full days of dehydration a Vitality Save must be made each day upon attempting to wake (at 
the reduced rate for any lost Vitality as shown above). failure indicates a loss of 1d6+1 base endurance. If base Endurance 
reaches 0 – lowered Vitality death is the result. 
Starvation: Full starvation effects are as follows: All physical and mental attributes of a character are reduced by one for 
each full day they go without food. Also, the character suffers from a level of fatigue each day, which eventually requires him 
to make Vitality saves to remain conscious. Attribute points are restored at the rate of two per day once adequate food has 
been consumed. In addition to these effects after three full weeks a Vitality Save must be made every other day (starting with 
the first) upon attempting to wake (at the reduced rate for any lost Vitality as shown above). Failure indicates a loss of 1d4+1 
base Endurance. If base Endurance reaches 0 minus lowered Vitality, death is the result.
Loss of Pressure
When a humanoid being is in an area with no or very low pressure their blood boils and their soft tissues are damaged very 
quickly. To simulate this when a humanoid is exposed to low or lack of pressure, they will take 1d10 damage per second to 
general endurance and 1d6 damage to each body area. 
Extreme Pressure
When a humanoid is under extreme pressure because they are deep underwater or something similar, they take crushing 
damage of 1d10 per 3 times normal pressure per second to all body areas, generally dying very quickly. 
Missile Weapon Fumbles: In addition to the chance of hitting another random target if a fumble with a missile weapon 
occurs (because the wielder’s failed an Agility save) it can have a mishap.

Vulnerabilities
Called Shots
Called shots or attacks are made when someone aims for a possible vulnerability. Called shots chances are 21 - 1 per Attack 
Skill (unmodified) as defined in the Player’s Guide. Rolling anything other than the natural roll or higher on a d20 results in 
a miss of the vulnerable area even if modified it would be enough for a hit. Damage is halved on called shots that miss the 
vulnerability but do strike an area. Called shots are the only way to strike the vulnerable sub areas mentioned below. 
Vulnerable Sub Areas
These are sub areas that are armor weaknesses, have less than normal endurance or can result in sensory, or other disabilities 
when destroyed. Generally, these are left to the common sense of the GM with the standard 1/10 endurance for sub areas 
used. The tables below show standard vulnerabilities, their effects ,and ways to counter the vulnerability.  The attacker must 
size up his opponent to discover what the vulnerable effect will be.  They are divided into types, some are vulnerabilities 
of the armor types, others of the body type of the target. In the cases of armor types, a counter allows the vulnerability to 
be removed. These are meant to be samples and to further illustrate finesse attacks but are not exhaustive and indicative of 
every situation. As always, GM discretion applies.

Weapons
Weapon Term Clarifications
War Axe: Great Axe and War Axe are synonymous; they are the same weapon by two names. War axe values can be found 
under Great Axe in the Player’s Guide.
Bastard Sword: This is sometimes referred to as a Claymore or Hand-and-a-Half sword. All combat values are the same and 
found under Bastard Sword. 
New Weapons
Bokken: A wooden katana. Normally used for practice but an effective wooden weapon regardless. 
Falchion:  Essentially a heavier, wider cutlass. 
Mace Variants:  There were many variants of maces from a simple stick with a ball on the end to a gothic, wedge mace. 
Adding to these are now a closed metal fist variant and an open hand with metal claws as well as the more common, 
morning star variant which is a spiked ball mace. 
Machete:  A wide, dagger sized bladed weapon with a one-sided wedge blade, useful for chopping. The backside or flat of the 
blade can be used for smashing (inelegantly).
Messer:  A simple, easy to construct, flat blade whose tang is sandwiched between two pieces of wood.
Morning Star:  There is some confusion between the morning star and a single ball flail. The morning star is listed below as a 
new form of spiked mace rather than as the one-ball, spiked flail it is often confused with. 
Whip Sword:  A handle attached to a metal whip cable, at intervals along the cable there are embedded sharp blades an inch 
to inch and a half long. When whipped, the blades strike quickly and at a great distance but for light damage. 
Compound Bow: A bow with multiple wheels and pulleys removing the minimum strength required to pull the draw. 
Recurve Bow: A bow with limbs that curve away from the center when unstrung, adding more power to the draw.

New Weapons Customizations
Envenomed: Make a blade with a hollow blade center all the way to the tip that goes to a compartment in the hilt that holds 
1 dose of poison per 10% additional weapon cost (up to 5 doses). When the weapon thrusts into a target and does 10 or 
more actual damage, then 1 dose of poison is applied to the target. It takes twice the normal weapon speed to open the 
compartment and refill the poison.
Arm Blade: Take any bladed weapon between 2 feet and 4 feet long. Turn the handle at 90 degrees and an additional one-
sided blade attached to the handle that runs back along the forearm one-third the length of the starting weapon length. 
When completed the arm blade handle can be held across the palm and the back-blade rests against the forearm with the 
original blade jutting outwards to its original length. This costs an additional 50% of the original weapon costs and lowers 
the maximum weapon speed by 1 but adds +20% to Weapon Skills. The starting blade length above is based on wielders 
between 5 and 7 feet tall. The length of the weapon that can be converted can be 1 foot longer for each 2 feet taller the 
wielder is over 7’ and must be lowered by 1 foot for each foot under 5 feet. 
Chain Weapon: Any weapon which has a Maximum speed of between 3-5 seconds can have a chain added to it to extend 
its reach. The cost is 20% of the weapon costs and changes the weapon in the following ways: weapon length is now +6 feet; 
maximum weapon speed is now +2 and minimum is +1 but does +1 dice damage.
Hooked Blade: Any bladed weapon can have a hook added to the end. It costs +10% of the original weapon costs. Thrusting 
attacks are removed, but any time the weapon would be considered to have stuck in the opponent (10 or more actual 
damage through armor/hide) the opponent is considered to be grappled and now requires a contest of Strength between 
the wielder and the target to escape the grapple. Also, the weapon cannot be used to perform a weapon twist for additional 
damage; however, it does weapon twist damage automatically when the wielder breaks free of the hook, unless a successful 
Chirugeon or Leeching skill roll is made to remove it. 

===== PAGE 182 =====
176
Combat
Sprinkler: Any smashing weapon can have holes drilled in it and a compartment added in which a special refillable metal 
vial is placed such that a catch/button can be hit while swinging, causing it to release a liquid from the holes (holy water, 
poison, acid, etc.).  The cost is 10% of the weapon cost per use until needing to be refilled, up to 5 uses. It takes twice the 
normal weapon speed to open the compartment and refill the liquid. 
Armor
Armor Term Clarifications
Banded: Banded refers to chain which has leather bands woven through it to increase the strength of the mail. The term 
Banded can cause confusion because Laminar armor (Roman and ancient styles of banded metal strips fastened together) 
was sometimes referred to as Banded. In Imagine Banded is banded chain (or banded mail), and Laminar refers to the 
banded-metal-strips type of armor. 
Brigandine: A modified form or Laminar where heavy cloth is used on the outside (see New Armor Modifications).
Fur: Sometimes leather is referred to as fur or hide. This just means it is left in an undyed or unfinished state or still has the 
fur (if any) attached to the worked piece of leather. There is no distinction in terms of armor. Fur does add protection from 
the cold and when worn, acts as cold weather gear without adding additional armor values. Otherwise treat fur and hide as 
leather. 
Gambeson: This is a form of padded or cloth armor that comes in shirts, armlets, leggings, and body suit. It can be doubled 
padded (6 points), triple padded (thick, 9 points) or quadruple padded (heavy, 12 points). The 9- and 12-point Gambesons 
are considered semi-flexible armor. The cost is x1 more for each doubling of the padded. So, a single doubling is x2 cost, 
triple, x3, etc. 
Lamellar: This is another name for scalemail. This is sometimes confused with Laminar (long banded strips of metal) which 
it is not.  
Laminar: This refers to segmented metal bands fastened together and should not be confused either with banded chain 
or scalemail which is sometimes called lamellar. Some versions of laminar were made with bolted leather strips (double 
thickness heavy leather bolted together). These are treated as a variant of bolted leather and not laminar in Imagine. 
Leather: Leather comes in three grades (soft, normal and hardened). Hardened is sometimes referred to as heavy leather, 
boiled leather or even thick leather but the armor value is still the same 6 points of protection. If two thicknesses of 
hardened leather have been bolted together with bolts (or any other form of fastener), then it is rigid armor and is referred 
to as bolted leather. 
Mountain Chain: This is a special form of chain where each link looks like an inverted V (or mountain). Armor value and 
statistics are as banded chain but at the price of heavy chain. This form of chain is not known by all armor smiths and was 
not common. Except for scale, mountain chain is the strongest form of non-magical, semi-flexible armor made.
New Armor
The armors shown below are available to purchase at GM discretion because some have planar and divine influences. Others 
like Laminar and Gambeson are more common. They match values that are in the Master’s Manual armor design section 
but are reproduced here in additional variants as armor pieces using these variants. They will be available in the Equipment 
section of this book. 
Laminar: Segmented bands of plate metal fastened together in strips around the body.  Their overlapping nature gives them 
a slight increase in armor value, but lack of practical flexibility means there are fewer available pieces of laminar. This type of 
armor thus gave way to hinged/fastened plate sections form-fitted to the body. It is available in older cultures and those who 
kept it because of tradition even though other more practical kinds of armor exist. This is treated as heavy plate for combat 
modifiers. 
Gambeson:  Padded armor that is woven into layers. It comes in types: normal (x2 padding or 6 points), thick (x3 padding 
or 9 points) or heavy (x4 padding or 12 points).  Thick and heavy versions are considered semi-flexible, where as normal is 
flexible like padding. 
Stainless Steel:  A form of heavy plate with chromium and nickel added, so that it never tarnishes and gleams like chrome. 
Move Unseen/Blend skills are -20% but Morale bonuses for all followers are +20%. This is a time consuming and expensive 

===== PAGE 183 =====
177
Combat
armor to be made, and requires someone with a successful Metallurgy social skill roll for each batch of Stainless Steel used 
in the armor making process. This is treated as heavy plate for combat modifiers.
Bloodricite/Pearlacite: Refers to a very-tough, jade-like, stone minerals found in the color of blood (Bloodricite) or a milky 
white reminiscent of pearl (Pearlacite). Both varieties are slightly lighter in armor thicknesses than heavy or stainless steel 
plate and tend to chip rather than break. Unfortunately, they can only be repaired with magic such as the skills Stone Lore 
or Crystal Lore (either work) or spells/effects like Repair.  These are found in fantasy worlds and in planar realms. They are 
non-magical, though rare substances. This armor has no combat modifiers.
Tempered Plate: Refers to a form of plate combining three kinds of steel and tempered to gain both flexibility and strength. 
This process is expensive and usually reserved for rare bladed weapons. It is only the crazy master armorer over many 
months who would make an entire suit of tempered plate. This armor has no combat modifiers regardless of piece.
Titanium: Generally, this is unobtainium in a medieval setting because it requires the best steel and aluminum smelted 
separately until pure, then recombined with molybdenum and other minerals to produce an amazing metal which, like 
stainless steel, never tarnishes, and in armor thicknesses weighs about half of normal plate. Normally, it would take a high-
tech furnace to produce, but with planar and divine influences, it is possible. This armor has no combat modifiers regardless 
of piece. Available at GM discretion.

New Armor Customizations
Armor Weapon Catches: for 5 gp each, a set of weapon catches can be added to any piece of rigid armor. This allows a Trap 
Weapon skill to be used automatically (at -20%) against any non-smashing weapon that has struck the piece of armor, either 
because an attack hit there or a successful Body Parry was used with that area as the selected area. No hands, weapons, 
or additional time is required to be used. The Trap Weapon skill roll immediately follows the strike or Body Parry. It only 
works against thrusting or cutting weapons; smashing weapons cannot be caught with weapon catches. 
Armor Weapon Hooks:  for 2 gp each, a weapon hook can be added to any piece of rigid armor to hold a weapon for easy 
access.
Brigandine: Any Laminar armor piece can have a heavy piece of cloth bolted as the outer layer increasing its armor value by 
3. This adds 10% to the cost of the piece. 

===== PAGE 184 =====
178
Combat
Codpiece/Girdle: Cost and armor types are the same as a Gorget. Can be worn as a 4th layer of armor, protecting genital-
called shots. 
Face guard:  Added to a great helm, half or composite helm, this protects against called shots to the face, redirecting them to 
the helm. +10% of the cost of the helm. This piece still allows called shots to the eyes.
Goggles: Made from any flexible material and then glass or crystal lenses. This protects the eyes from called shots. 2-3 Gold. 
Neck Guard Pauldrons:  Any existing rigid pauldron can have neck guards added for +25% of the cost. These now protect 
side and rear attacks from aiming for the neck, redirecting them to the shoulder instead. With this modification only direct 
forward thrusts and piercing attacks can strike the neck.
Painting: Armor can be dyed or painted at +10% of the price. If painted dark (+10% Move Unseen, and Blend at night). If 
painted the color of the terrain then (+10% Move Unseen, and Blend when in a terrain that matches that pattern or color 
and -10% when not).
Visor:  Added to a half or composite helm, this protects against called shots to the face and eyes. +20% of the cost of the 
helm.
New Magical Weave Armor
The new armors below are various versions of a flexible material with magical or divine metals or minerals drawn into (or 
embedded in) then threaded and sewn in to the fibers creating a magic weave armor. This process is expensive and rare as 
the costs in the equipment section will show. The values here are provided for combat as needed. It is treated as hide for 
damage absorption and as magical flexible armor for layering with other armors.

Addiction
Addiction can occur when a being’s mind or body gets used to any intoxicant, herb, potion, or elixir. Magical spells, rituals, 
skills and all divine effects are considered non-habit forming. Use the rules below for checking for addiction and dealing 
with its effects. Beings with 18+ Will Force cannot become addicted. 
Becoming Addicted (Make a Will Force save to avoid addiction when): 
•	 When a being drinks alcohol to the point of inebriation at least three times in a one-week period. (Dwarves/Giants 
ignore this.)
•	 When a being uses an herb or chemical intoxicant at least four times in a one-week period. (Fae/Midfolk ignore this for 
herbs.)
•	 Whenever a non-intoxicant, non-healing, or non-curing herb is used three or more times in a 24-hour period or four 
times in a week. 
•	 Whenever a non-healing or non-curing potion is used two or more times in a 24-hour period. 
Any failed Will Force saves indicate addiction to whatever substance was used. 
Using, Once Addicted (Make a Will Force save, [and possibly Wisdom, see below] to avoid using when): 
•	 Alcohol: Three per day, at waking, noon and 6 pm, or every time alcohol is presented.
•	 Herb/Chemical Intoxicants: Twice per day, at waking, and 2 pm, or every time the intoxicant is presented.
•	 Herbs non-intoxicant, non-healing or non-curing: Once per day, at noon or every time the herb is presented.
•	 Potions: Once every other day, at noon or every time the potion is presented.
If the addicted experienced full withdrawal and made their Wisdom Save after, they are now afforced a Wisdom save as well 
to avoid using and only have to roll a Using check, once per week (or when presented with it) instead of the time periods listed 
above. 

===== PAGE 185 =====
179
Combat
Withdrawal Effects (Make a Vitality Save to avoid after a period of no usage): 
•	 Alcohol: After three days, make a Vitality save every 6 hours or suffer -3 Agility and -4 Vitality and begin sweating. 
Concentration becomes difficult (Intelligence Save for every attempt). The user is considered at 4 levels of Fatigue/
Mental Fatigue. Full withdrawal takes 8d6 hours. 
•	 Herb/Chemical Intoxicants: After four days, make a Vitality save every 6 hours or suffer -2 Agility and -3 Vitality and 
suffers from chills. Concentration becomes difficult (Intelligence Save for every attempt). The user is considered at 3 
levels of Fatigue/Mental Fatigue. Full withdrawal takes 6d6 hours. 
•	 Herbs non-intoxicant, non-healing or non-curing: After five days, make a Vitality save or suffer -1 Agility and -2 
Vitality and suffer difficulty concentrating (Intelligence Save for every attempt) for the remainder of the day. The user is 
considered at 2 levels of Fatigue/Mental Fatigue. Full withdrawal takes 4d6 hours.
•	 Potions: After a week, make a Vitality save or suffer -1 Agility and -1 Vitality and suffer difficulty concentrating 
(Intelligence Save for every attempt) for the remainder of the day. The user is considered at 1 level of Fatigue/Mental 
Fatigue. Full withdrawal takes 3d6 hours.
After Full Withdrawal Effects: 
•	 The Withdrawal effects do not need to be checked or rolled again until the character uses again, then hits a new 
withdrawal period. 
•	 The user is still addicted and needs to make Will Force saves to avoid using. Though the addiction has not been cured, 
they are afforded a Wisdom Save after fully withdrawing and seeing those effects on themselves. If they make this 
Wisdom Save, then the user will be afforded both a Wisdom save and a Will Force save to avoid using again each time. 
Also, the Using required rolls are reduced to once per week or when presented. If they failed that initial Wisdom save, 
then they haven’t yet learned and will likely have to go through uses and withdrawal again. Each successive Wisdom Save 
after the first Full Withdrawal is at -10% cumulative chance. There are only so many chances to find Wisdom. 
Curing Addiction (Ways): 
•	 Cure (5% chance per Piety Control.) No Withdrawal.
•	 Cure Disease skill made at -30%. No Withdrawal.
•	 Whenever Will Force increases to 18 or above, an attempt can be made to cure any and all addictions. Full Withdrawal 
will still occur before each addiction subsides. 
Living with the Addiction (Ways): 
•	 Go through Full Withdrawal and make a Wisdom Save after. All future usage opportunities now allow both a Wisdom 
Save and a Will Force save to avoid using, and the Using roll is reduced to once per week or when presented. Either 
success will suffice. 
•	 Use a Quest or Geas spell/effect on the being and make breaking the addiction the quest. Full Withdrawal will occur. 
They now get Wisdom Save and a Will Force save to avoid using. Either success will suffice. Reward: After 1 year 
the quest/geas is considered passed. The user gets an increase of 1 Will Force and 1-3 Wisdom (not to exceed racial 
maximums for either.) If the user reached 18 Will Force, then they are cured. Otherwise, they will have to continue 
making Wisdom/Will Saves, now at +10%.
•	 Control is used on the being, only to stop them from using. Full Withdrawal will occur. They will not use while under 
Control but they also must make a Will Force save once per month. If they fail that Will Force save, then they lose 1 Will 
Force point permanently. This can continue until they lose the will to live at 0 Will Force and die.

New Coinage 
In the larger planar setting coins are used that value far above gold. The use and exchange of these varies by setting. Their 
properties, values, weights, etc. are listed below. 
Bloodracite Pieces
Value:  20 gold per piece. 
Shape: lozenge shape (thinner in the middle)
Weight: 30 pieces per pound.
Appearance: Red stone mineral with dark red motes and streaking, when polished it becomes a blood red in color. 
Magical Properties: None
Origin: Hellish planes and the places affected by the hellish planes. 
Pearlacite Pieces
Value:  20 gold per piece. 
Shape: triangles
Weight: 30 pieces per pound.
Appearance: Milky white mineral with iridescent flakes, when polished it gleams in white. 
Magical Properties: None
Origin: Heavenly planes and the places affected by the heavenly planes. 
Chromantium Pieces
Value: 400 gold per piece. 
Shape: Small ovals
Weight: light, 40 pieces per pound.
Appearance: Swirling iridescent metal, in all the colors of the rainbow and some new colors that seem unreal. 
Magical Properties: Each coin stores 7 to 9 Aura and is +7 to +9 in magical grade. Also, they are their own source of magic 1,2 
or 3 Aura, regenerating even in the absence of other sources of magic at a rate of 1 Aura per minute. They can be used in places 
where magic is not normally found. 
Origin: Plane of Magic/Chaos or places affected by this plane.
Crysteel Pieces
Value: 300 gold per piece. 
Shape: Squares
Weight: 30 pieces per pound.
Appearance: Translucent Green (some blue and red versions exist).
Magical Properties: Each Coin is +5 or +6 in magical grade. 
Origin: Plane of Magic/Chaos or places affected by this plane.
Memory Pieces
Value: 500 gold per piece. 
Shape: hexagonal
Weight: 10 pieces per pound.
Appearance: The material seems semi-translucent and the colors vary widely from a swirling pattern to a single color but all are 
translucent. 
Magical Properties: Each Coin contains a single memory. Some are seconds long, but others last an hour or more. 
Origin: It is said that Reapers mint the coins from the memories of the deceased when they shepherd them into the planes 
after death; that a particular interesting memory catches them and they capture it for all times. The mineral itself is a form 
of memory crystal from the plane of dreams/veil of illusions. These coins are heavily traded by immortals beings and plane 
walkers. 
Soul Pieces
Value: 1000 gold per piece. 
Shape: decahedrons (10 sides)
Weight: 20 pieces per pound.
Appearance: The color varies from deepest black, to purest white, but most are marbled gray with white and black streaks. 
Magical Properties: Each Coin contains 1 Will Force point purposely placed there. Useful for many things. 
Origin: Unknown and possibly varied. The coins seem to be both metallic and porous having the properties of both metal and 
bone. These coins are highly sought for their usefulness.

Armored Suits
The first suits represent two of the best pre-medieval armors, 
and the last five the best non-magical theoretical armor 
available. These five armor suits represent what craftsmen 
might have been able to do at the peak of their skills, simply 
to produce normal grade versions of these armored suits. 
The first 2 suits can be made at +20% armoring and the last 
5 at -20% armoring. 
Bloodred Plate Armor: Bodysuit of hardened leather, full 
chain shirt, chain headgear, chain gauntlets, and chain 
leggings. Helm, gorget, breastplate, pauldrons, armlets, 
arm bracers, gauntlets, leglets, leg bracers, and footgear of 
Bloodracite. 44 points in the head, neck, upper and middle 
torsos, shoulders, arms, forearms, hands, legs, shins, and 
feet. 36 in the lower torso. All external armor is blood red 
except for the double layer of chain in the lower torso. There 
are no penalties with this armor. Weight is 80 pounds.
Legate/General Armor: Headgear and sandals of hardened 
leather. Decorated helm, breastplate, gorget, pauldrons, 
armlets, arm bracers, gauntlets, long skirt and leg bracers of 
laminar. 27 armor in the head and neck, 21 in upper, middle 
and lower torso, shoulders, arms, forearms, hands, legs, and 
shins. 6 in the feet. There are significantly more penalties 
with this armor. -25% to skills, +2 defensive, +2 initiative, 
and +2 weapon speed. Weight is 37 pounds. 
Legion/Centurion Armor: Headgear, gauntlets and 
sandals of hardened leather. Bolted leather gorget, armored 
skirt, arm bracers and leg bracers, helm, breastplate, and 
pauldrons of laminar.  The head and forearms have 27 
armor, 21 in the upper and middle torsos, and shoulders, 18 
in the neck, 12 in the lower torso, forearms and shins, and 6 
in the hands and feet. Arms and Legs are exposed. Modifiers 
are minimal at -5% to skills, +1 defensive, +2 initiative, and 
+1 weapon speed. Total weight 31 and 1/2 pounds. 
Pearlescent Plate Armor: Bodysuit of hardened leather, 
full chain shirt, chain headgear, chain gauntlets, and chain 
leggings. Helm, gorget, breastplate, pauldrons, armlets, 
arm bracers, gauntlets, leglets, leg bracers and footgear of 
Pearlacite. 44 points in the head, neck, upper and middle 
torsos, shoulders, arms, forearms, hands, legs, shins, and 
feet. 36 in the lower torso. All external armor is iridescent 
milky white except for the double layer of chain in the lower 
torso. There are no penalties with this armor. Weight is 80 
pounds.
Shining Plate Armor: Bodysuit of hardened leather, full 
chain shirt, chain headgear, chain gauntlets, and chain 
leggings. Helm, gorget, breastplate, pauldrons, armlets,

Magical Weapons and Armor 
The value of other magical items is listed with the item 
in various books, but the basic value of magical weapons 
and armor, even before enchantment, is listed here to give 
relative worth. This does not mean it is for sale, but in the 
planar realms and in the largest cities at least some of it 
often is. With these evaluations appropriate, values can be 
set. Each will be shown by category. Low, Medium and High 
values now are by type of weapon or armor as noted below. 
Magical Weapons
For weapons instead of the usual low, medium, high armor 
each cost type will refer to a grade of weapon damage 
output. Low damage weapons such as a dagger, short sword, 
rapier, hand axe, etc. Medium will be long swords, maces, 
axes. High will mean great axes, great swords, pole arms, 
war hammers, etc. In a given category some weapons will be 
weaker, for instance a battle axe might slightly lower than 
the high value where a halberd would be a little higher than 
the value listed for (high). Use best judgment.

if some of the statistics provided may be lower than what the spell, invocation or skill would provide, the completeness of 
the elemental powers, skills and abilities make it a more useful summoned companion. In the following tables, PC stands for 
Piety Control while PT is Practitioner Title.

Air Whyll, Brainbush (Supernatural, Magical Plant, Level 2)
This elemental air plant is a small, blue bush, but it only grows on the heads and brows of humanoids. From a distance 
appears as blue hair, but up close it is clearc that the bush is growing out of the eyes of the humanoid. It has fine leaves that 
are fern like and delicate. There is a small nub at the base of each leaf that aids in its sensing ability, able to detect both heat 
and life. The brain bush is a true parasite, robbing the victim of normal sight but replacing it with a visual sense of heat and 
life sense within 120 feet. It changes the being by causing all their hair to fall out and removes all attraction to other beings 
for reproduction purposes. The victim loses -4 appearance but becomes much more logical, adding +2 Intelligence. Also, the 
being becomes completely resistant to electricity and immune to illusions. 
Habits/Life Cycle: The brainbush releases a cloud of spores (once per year) around other humanoids. This creates a blue 
cloud of spores that drift around until they contact the eyes and the fluid of the eyes of other humanoids. The initial cloud 
is about twenty feet in diameter but wind will carry or disperse them depending on wind strength. It requires a Disease 
Resistance for all those who contact it until it is flushed out of the eyes with water or by other means. If the victim’s Disease 
Resistance fails, the spores infect the eyes and the being goes blind in 1d4+1 hours. Thereafter, the eyes are consumed by the 
brain bush. No pain is felt because a strong local anesthesia is released by the spores as they consume the eyes and the fluid 
therein. Within 1d4+1 days, the victim’s eyes are gone and the strongest of the spores has now grown into shoots coming 
out of the eyes and also boring into the brain (again without pain). 1-3 weeks later the sprouts grow into a brain bush which 
replaces the being’s hair from the eyebrows upward. The being now “sees” through the parasitic brain bush sensing life and 
heat within 120 feet. The bush survives as long as the humanoid it inhabits lives. 
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Air, and gases linked to this plane, also anywhere that infected humanoids go.
Body Type: Small (bush x1 area)
STR N/A, AGL N/A, VIT 5, MEN N/A, PER N/A, MYS N/A

Weight:  1-2 lb.

Spores Cloud: When other humanoids come within range (once per year)

wind strength. It requires a Disease Resistance for all those who contact

Experience Value:  0 (avoidable)

Special Notes: If the brainbush is destroyed it will regrow out of the eye sockets of the infected being. Only by completely 
removing the plant from the eye sockets and brain of the victim can the brain bush be killed. Magical or divine effects 
which cure disease will kill the brainbnush but the being will still be blind due to the loss of eyes and the brain’s visual 
system. Magical cure blindness effects will restore the eyes but the brain has still lost its visual cortex and this will need to be 
restored with strong magical healing (Regeneration, Recover, etc.).

Air Wyrd, Cloud Fisher (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 14)
The cloud fisher emits and holds a large gaseous cloud around itself. This, combined with its translucence makes it nearly 
invisible from an even close range. It is a large creature that would weight many tons if it were not magically buoyant due 
to levitation. It is much much like the angler fish, save for its tremendous size, membranous fins and tail, and magical 
propulsion jets that allow it to move slowly through the air. It has a long stalk that extends from its head. At the end of the 
stalk is a scaled object which glows slightly, drawing creatures close enough for the cloud fisher to bring its massive jaws 
and needle-sharp teeth into play. These creatures live for centuries and can wait dormant for years until a food source comes 
along. 
Habits/Life Cycle: The cloud fisher female has the male cloud fisher imbedded within her. When she is young, a male cloud 
fisher sacrifices himself, burrows into her side and loses most of its body (including its brain) but saves its reproductive 
organs which are now supplied by her blood. Every century or so she will lay a clutch of 24 to 48 fertilized eggs. When these 
hatch, they will consume each other until only a few are left. During this time several of the males will attempt to attach to 
remaining females and the whole process will continue. 
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Air, and gases linked to this plane.
Body Type: Gargantuan (Fish)

Air Wyrd, Darter (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 7)
This gray conical air wyrd resembles a sea creature in that it has fins and a tail. It is tri-symmetrical with an eye, breathing 
hole, fin, tail and a tentacle each positioned around the creature in thirds. It has a tail from which magically generated air 
extends allowing it to speed around, guided by its fins and tails as rudders. It remains buoyant due to magical air bladders 
that condense lighter than air gasses. Its forefront ends in a very sharp beak that can pierce metal and from which electricity 
sparks. These beings can use their tails as rudders and can make themselves spin very fast, further enhancing their beak’s 
attack. Once they pierce a living creature, the beak opens like a corkscrew doing continual twisting damage as it burrows 
deeper and deeper into the victim. Its skin is covered in gray scales, and it can smell blood at a great distance. On smaller 
targets it will grasp with its tentacles and then repeatedly strike with its beak. 
Habits/Life Cycle: Mating once every three years and then the female finds a solid surface to lay 2-5 eggs. The female darter 
protects the eggs until they hatch. They climb out and onto her, securing themselves with their tentacles around her fins. 
Generally, she can support only three of the offspring, so any others are left to fend for themselves. The immature darters 
feed of any prey that she is able to kill for the first three months. They are then able to hunt on their own, and reach full 
maturity in three more months. 
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Air, and gases linked to this plane.

Air Elemental, Alpha (Supernatural, Level 15)
An Alpha is a leader among the ordered (the Lerell) or the chaotic (the Erella) Air Elementals. They lead their lesser in 
most matters, only the prime overrules them. An Alpha is an extremely powerful Air Elementals that embodies the best and 
greatest values of their beings. They are True Neutral with order or chaos tendencies depending on their faction.
Habits/Life Cycle: Air Elementals are magical beings that do not breathe, eat, or sleep. One Endurance per week is lost 
if these beings are kept out of gasses by trapping them in solids or liquids. They reproduce by joining and losing part of 
themselves to make 1-2 zephyrs or tiny Air Elementals. They do this very infrequently unless they are in times of strife. 
Zephyrs grow based on need in any clean gaseous source. They achieve full size in as little as a year. 
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Air and gases linked to this plane.
Body Type: Special (head x1, torso x2, whirlwind x3, 8 tendril-limbs x1)
