Air Wyrd, Fizgig (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 5)
The fizgig is a blue and gray spherical creature. It is just over a foot and a half in diameter.  It has openings in its spherical 
carapace, at the top, from which three “wings” can emerge when active. There is a gap around the wing holes and when 
the wings are out the entire top spins allowing the wings to gain lift in a helicopter-like effect. There are three similar 
holes near the bottom edge from which three leg/stingers emerge. It has three recessed, protected eyes on its equator that 
are equidistant apart allowing it to see in a full 360 degrees. It hears and smells through holes in the legs (when they are 
extended). The central bottom section also has a large opening that allows its beak-like mouth to protrude when in use. This 
creature is very agile in the air and can hover for long periods of time as the energy used to keep it aloft is magical. Its legs 
end in flexible foot pads that can also be used as graspers and from which a spur can extend that is a stinger. The stingers 
can either inject or spray a virulent death poison making this creature very dangerous. 
Habits/Life Cycle: Females release small clutches of buoyant floating egg sacks from their retracted foot pad holes, each 
egg has a gaseous pocket to keep it aloft. They are slightly sticky allowing them to clump together. Males release spores from 
their retracted foot pad holes and fertilize the floating eggs. They do this every other year when healthy and active. The 
fertilized eggs hatch in clumps of 3-30 and grow to full size in three months. They are omnivorous and voracious eaters but 
they also can retract their wings, levitate and go dormant for weeks at a time when no food is available. 
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Air and gases linked to this plane.

a sharp poison stinger. It has three recessed, protected eyes on its equator that are equidistant apart allowing it to see in a 
full 360 degrees. It hears and smells through holes in the tentacles (when they are extended). The central bottom section 
also has a large opening that allows its large, beak-like mouth to protrude when in use. This creature is very agile in the air 
and can hover for long periods of time as the energy used to keep it aloft is magical. Its legs end in flexible tentacles that can

Air Whyll, White Shroud (Supernatural, Magical Plant, Level 3)
This elemental air plant grows in pod clumps of 1 to 10. It magically floats in the air due to an innate levitation power in 
each pod. The pods are naturally sticky and require a strength save to remove. The pod surface is peppered with holes. Each 
hole can shoot a dart with a string of web attached up to 30 feet and then slowly reel it back in. The holes can release white 
spores in a cloud around the pod out to about 10 feet. It only does this when it reels in an object that is warm. The spores 
gravitate towards any warm object covering it in as many spores as possible. The spores contain a special contact poison. 
A strong, virulent paralysis toxin that paralyzes its victims for hours.  The spores also release a concentrated acid, eating 
through armor, clothes, flesh, etc. at a high rate. Water can flush off the spores but is required in large volumes, about 1 quart 
per foot of average height, circumference, etc. of the being or object to clean. It can also be burned off, but fire damage is 
doubled to living targets because the spores are quite combustible. 
Habits/Life Cycle: White shroud reproduces when the spores it releases consume enough flesh to grow into pods 
themselves. It takes about 10 lb. of organic material and about 12 hours for each reproductive spore to become a pod.

Chaos Wyrd, Discorporator (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 12)
These dwarf-sized creatures are spherical when resting in their perfect dormant state. Their skin is dark and partially 
absorptive with, a mix of muted colors that are always in motion, blending in to the dark underside of the maelstrom of 
chaos they reside in. These beings awaken whenever a magical effect is finished, opening a one-way gateway to the effect 
and pulling in the matter or energy. They pull it apart with their hands and pinchers and force it to return to its potentiate 
state, throwing it back into the maelstrom. Unlike incorporators, they are not attuned to a single magic effect, Any of them 
can perform the necessary action. They do tend to gravitate to a particular effect to dissolve, so some might specialize in 
magical or normal fire, and another might be focused on things which produce stone or earth. Without them most magic 
would continue on and upset the balance between becoming and ending. It is not possible to interrupt this process without 
stopping all discorporators, a nearly insurmountable feat. Every hour that a discorporator is kept from gathering and 

===== PAGE 209 =====
203
dissolving magical effects, it needs to make a Vitality save and a Will Force save. If it fails either, it dies as its body dissolves 
back into potentiate. 
Habits/Life Cycle: Infrequently, they eat potentiate from the magical maelstrom of chaos turning it into sustenance. All 
discorporators are male. Their counterparts, the incorporators are female. When a new incorporator or discorporator is 
needed the two sexes meet in the middle of the maelstrom. They mate and produce a small, spherical egg that grows quickly, 
in less than an hour, and then hatches. Then in another hour the new magical animal grows into the full-sized incorporator 
or discorporator. The new entity goes off with the mother or father to be shown how to perform its role. The same pair will 
never mate again as each mating is with a different incorporator and discorporator pair.
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Chaos, and great sources of magic linked to this plane.

Chaos Wyrd, Incorporator (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 12)
These dwarf-sized creatures are spherical when resting in their perfect dormant state. Their skin is a silvery, partially 
reflective mix of bright colors that are always in motion, blending in to the maelstrom of chaos they reside in. They are 
attuned to a being, or magical effect. When that effect is first activated, they open and use their scoop-like tail to gather 
potentiate from the chaotic maelstrom of The Plane of Chaos. They use their pincher lower arms to cut the material and 
their humanoid upper arms to shape it into the matter or energy the effect is calling upon. When they have finished shaping, 
they open a one-way portal to the Aura pocket, or pattern of the effect and send the gathered energy or matter to the effect 
and then return to their dormant state. Incorporators fulfill the unspoken requests of magic use everywhere. Without them, 
most magic would fail. It is possible to temporarily halt a being or item’s power by finding the connected incorporator and 
stopping it from performing the shaping of matter and energy from potentiate. Every hour that an incorporator is unable to 
fulfill the magic requests of a being it needs, to make a Vitality save and a Will Force 
save. If it fails either, it dies as its body dissolves back into potentiate. 
Habits/Life Cycle: Infrequently, they eat potentiate from the magical 
maelstrom of chaos turning it into sustenance. All incorporators 
are female. Their counterparts, the discorporators are male. 
When a new incorporator or discorporator is needed the 
two sexes meet in the middle of the maelstrom. They mate 
and produce a small, spherical egg that grows quickly, in less 
than an hour, and then hatches. Then in another hour, the 
new magical animal grows into the full-sized incorporator 
or discorporator. The new entity goes off with the mother 
or father to be shown how to perform its role. The same 
pair will never mate again, as each mating is with a different 
incorporator and discorporator pair.
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Chaos, and great sources of 
magic linked to this plane.
Body Type: Small Humanoid (with a tail, and an extra pair of

Death Wyrd, Death Dog, Harvester (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 9)
This dog-like creature has a large three-part maw with rows of razor-sharp teeth and two yellow or red eyes, one above and 
one below their maw. They have three semicircular ear flaps just behind each section of the maw. These flaps cover or expose 
highly sensitive ears. They have translucent fur and foot pads that end in a row of three razor sharp claws and a hook claw 
opposing. They seem fearsome when seen but rarely appear to living beings or creatures. Instead, they remain faded into 
shadow and hunt recently dead animal spirits that last mere hours after the death of the animal (1 hour per Will Force). 
They consume the animal spirit, and when they are full return to The Plane of Death and regurgitate the spirit energy into 
troughs at the bottom of the plane. They keep only a little of this energy to sustain themselves in their hunts. They will 
sometimes bond with a Reaper from The Plane of Death and hunt with them. 
 Habits/Life Cycle: The Harvester or Death Dog gives birth through pathogenesis (without mating.)  When they have fed on 
dozens of spirits, too much to carry back to The Plane of Death. They will sometimes lay 1-3 black shadowy eggs in a dark 
corner or shaded area. These eggs are faded, as the spell fade, just as Death Dogs themselves are. There they will remain until 
an animal dies or an animal spirit or other spirit is within 100 feet of the eggs. Then they hatch and each Harvester pup will 
take a few bites of a spirit then run off to grow. They do this three times, each time growing more, until within 3 days (or 
three meals) they are full sized Death Dogs. Then they will go to The Plane of Death and shadow another Harvester or bond 
with a Reaper, learning to hunt animal spirits. They live forever or until they are destroyed. 
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Death, and anywhere there is a recently deceased animal or magical animal.

Death, Reaper (Supernatural, Magical Humanoid, Level 12)
The Reaper is a class of being that guides the dead from the place they died to their final destinations, be it afterlife, in the 
heavens, or hells, or purgatory, or to oblivion. They can appear as any humanoid, but when on The Plane of Death, they are 
generally gray beings with few features and distinguishing marks. It is said that they answer to death itself, a being or deity 
that personifies this aspect of reality. Others say they report to deities with death as a sphere of influence. Whichever is the 
case they come to the recently dead within a window of 3 hours to 3 days of death depending on their current workload. 
They come to help the dead leave the Natural Universe. The Reapers themselves never know what the dead being’s final 
disposition will be, as it is dependent on the life the being led, and how they measured up to their own standards and the 
standards set by the gods they worshipped and/or the society they came from. They have many tools to aid the dead, from 
last looks at things the recently departed have done, to a few last glimpses of what was left behind. The Reaper opens the 
portal to the final end with Call of the Light and encourages the dead (ghost) to move on. When the dead being moves on, 
there is a split. Part of the essence is left and collected by the Reaper and taken to The Plane of Death for reprocessing. This 
essence is what is seen as the ‘motes’ in the plane of death. There is much confusion as to what this essence is. Some claim 
it is everything but the soul. Others that it is only the spirit and many other combinations of mind, spirit and soul. Most are 
sure that the discarded ghost form is certainly part of it. Reapers can be of any alignment, with the good ones careful and 
gentle stewards of the departed, and the evil ones unconcerned and forceful in their approach to the dead. 
Habits/Life Cycle: The source of the original Reapers is a mystery. Some claiming they were failed angels or weakened 
devils. Now it is believed that new Reapers are chosen from the recently dead. Some say it is those who killed many. If they 

===== PAGE 227 =====
221
have done so to defend their people or a cause, then they become good aligned Reapers. If they have been murderers and 
sociopaths, then they become evil aligned Reapers. Many end up somewhere in between and become Neutral Reapers. 
Some say Reapers know their own and will choose a recently deceased to return with them if they fit a certain profile, taking 
the new Reaper as an apprentice whom they train for a year and a day. What is known is that becoming a Reaper keeps a 
being from moving on. Reapers also weaken and fall. They may fail in their duties and leave too many ghosts in the natural 
universe. Most eventually tire of their work. What is sure is how they end. One day the Reaper simply opens the portal to 
the final end with Call of the Light and steps through themselves. No one is sure how long a Reaper will last. Some say there 
are still original Reapers, others that they can only make it decades or a century before the soul of the Reaper becomes too 
weary and faces its own final end. Just remember – you might be a king or a little street sweeper, but sooner or later you 
dance with the reaper.

Dream, Dreamwalkers (Supernatural, Magical Humanoid, Level +2)
Some humanoids give in to their animalistic tendencies when they are dreaming and imagine they are animals. When they 
consume dream food as dream animal, they must make a Disease Resistance each time. If the dreamer fails this resistance, 
they are inflicted with dream lycanthropy. This means when they enter the Dreamscape thereafter, they become as dream 
animals but having the spirits of magical humanoids. Every three true dreams in the Dreamscape they are afforded a 
Will Force. If they make the save there is a 5% increasing cumulative chance that on their next true dream, they become 
completely aware of their condition and gain control of their dream lycanthropy. Once they gain control, they can assume a 
form of their choice: as a Dream Animal, a Dream Hybrid (half animal form) or as their humanoid form. 
Note: For all Dream Lycanthropes, in any form, various parts provide hermetic benefits as follows: 
Hermetics Lore: Eye: Sight Illusion (Average), Skin: Touch Illusion (Average), Tongue: Taste Illusion (Average), Blood: 
Sense Illusion (Average), Ear: Sound Illusion (Average), Nose: Sound Illusion (Average)

Dream, Jabberwock, Nightmare Dragon (Supernatural, Magical, Level 15)
The dreaded Jabberwock, or Nightmare Dragon is the most dangerous creature in all of the dreamscape. Their breath is a 
triple poison; a virulent paralysis poison, a virulent nightmare poison and a death poison chaser. Their roar causes fear and 
their talons and fangs are long, magically sharp, and piercing respectively. The Jabberwock has black scales and a gray-green 
underbelly. Though it has wings, these are feeble and do not allow it to fly. It has a prehensile tail that is strong enough to 
allow it to raise up and attack with the talons of its rear legs as well. Their eyes provide them with true sight and they can life 
sense. They can fade into near darkness and are silent hunters. In the dreamscape, their bite can also slay dreamers outright. 
Unlike other dragons the Jabberwock never sleeps. While some dragons can be talked to, the Jabberwock does not care to 
speak to any save its own kind and then infrequently. Their minds are proof against mental combat or even mental contact. 
They are formidable foes and their transfixing eyes and wicked grin are rarely seen twice. Only the bravest heroes bearing 
weapons as sharp as a Jabberwock’s claws stands any chance against them. 
 
Habits/Life Cycle: These evil creatures mate rarely and when they do the female lays a clutch of 1-3 eggs. They have little 
regard for their eggs and do not defend them. Each egg therefore has only a 33% likelihood to hatch. It only takes 3 months 
for these eggs to mature. The juveniles can fly and do so nearly continuously, only landing to feed. Unlike other dragons they 
achieve full size in one year, lose their ability to fly, and thereafter do not grow. The Jabberwock can live up to 1000 years. 
Climate/Habitat: The Dream Plane and places connected to it.
Body Type: Giant Reptile (with wings)

Dream, Pearlescent Dragon (Supernatural, Magical, Level 15)
This beautiful dragon has pale white, protofeathers between its pearlescent scales and full feathers on its wings. They are soft 
to the touch. They are thinner than most dragons though not true wyrms since they have full magical wings. Their wings 
are more birdlike and less reptilian than most dragons. These dragons can be quite shy of most humanoids, not because of 
fear, but because they avoid misunderstanding and aggression against other sentient beings unless there is no other option. 
They are mortal enemies of the Jabberwock and Night Stalkers. They have a magical singing voice and many dream powers 
that make them strong forces within the dreamscape. Their breath weapon is a virulent (-20% resistance) paralysis gas, and 
their touch can cause paralysis if Magic Resistance fails and they desire it to be in effect. They have an intimidating roar and 
a transfixing gaze when they desire. These dragons are said to work towards the greater good and are known to sometimes 
take an interest in young true dreamers who need guidance or have suffered a great loss. Unlike other dragons, they do not 
sleep and they are self-sustaining, magically allowing them to eschew the need for food and drink to focus on their ethical 
pursuits. They are also known for the rare ability to grant a single wish to a deserving person, generally after much guidance 
and other help, though this rarely occurs. They work through animals but sometimes take humanoid form, losing their 
physical size and attacks, but maintaining their other magical abilities. They are always good but rarely fanatical.    
Habits/Life Cycle: These dragons are the only dragon to give live birth after mating and are only fertile once every 100 
years. They gestate for a full year before giving birth. Both parents raise their offspring for seven years, hunting Drell and 
Night Stalkers and other dream menaces, to feed the offspring in the first year. The pearlescent dragon reaches full size 
in three more years’ time and spends another three years in the company of their parents learning an ethical and moral 
framework. Then they choose a cause and venture out into the dreamscape to pursue it. They can live a thousand years. 
Climate/Habitat: The Dream Plane and places connected to it.
Body Type: Giant Reptile (with birdlike wings)

Dream, Ravening Haunt (Supernatural, Magical, Level See chart below)
These creatures are a form of spirit echo, leftover from dying dreamers who have created especially detailed areas over long 
periods in the Plane of Dreams. The spirit occupies and becomes the place where the dreamer spent their time making it 
their own. Their bodies are the areas, their minds and hearts are special objects within them. They are empty, hungry spirits 
and, though they are not undead, they do live off of the fear of the victims who enter the Ravening Haunt. Eventually, the 
victims are lured into a special area that is the stomach of the haunt where they become permanently paralyzed and are 
then consumed by their manifest fears. As the Ravening Haunt gains Will Force it begins to have manifestations. First, 
Grotesqueries, caricatures of the victims that it has killed. In the beginning, these will be animals who appear as delightful 
versions of those that have previously died within; then they transform and become fearful killing machines. Next as the 
haunt gains power it forms Masquerades: parodies of the people who have died within it. They also will have knowledge 
and feelings of the people they are parodies of, though always with some form of wicked twist. At the height of the haunt’s 
power, it forms a Mockery, becoming the Ravening Haunt’s avatar: a near copy of the original dreamer with most of their 
knowledge, feelings, and even desires save with many dark twists and outright insanities. In its final form as the Macabre, 
the Ravening Haunt can move itself from place to place and even to other planes. The first stop is always the Plane of 
Shadow, though additional plane shifts can be to anywhere reachable. 
Ravening Haunts are hard to recognize and dangerous. The only way to kill one is to destroy the heart, mind, and stomach, 
as well as the Mockery (avatar) if these exist. If any one of these is destroyed then the exits fail after 10 minutes, allowing 
escape. If all of these parts are destroyed then the Ravening Haunt is killed and decays away over the next hour, with all 
exits failing within 10 minutes. Then the creatures dies in the next 20 minutes, and finally the area collapses and decays into 
dust and ash in an additional 30 minutes. Some small magical token, a discarded object left by the original dreamer, will 
remain with one useful magical power. It is actually the seed of a new Ravening Haunt and, if carried by another who dies, 
will make a new haunt. The Ravening Haunt begins as an instinctual creature with no way to block escape from its areas, but 
does have one area as a designated stomach with the others as body parts. Then it grows gaining a full mind and exit parts 
to block egress, then a heart from which it will dispense creatures and finally an avatar. It can reshape itself (with Animate 
Object and Mold) once it has a mind. So even if someone were unlucky enough to encounter it twice, it might be vastly 
different each time. The creatures below will describe each part of the Ravening Haunt. 
Examples of Ravening Haunts include: a deeply overgrown hedge maze, a haunted mansion, a series of branching 
unclimbable ravines, a strange and mysterious zoo, a dark carnival, a bizarre section of a city that few return from, a glowing 
grotto of unearthly caves, and as many more as can be imagined as long as they are completely enclosed with few entrances 
and exits and no more than 1000 feet in any one dimension. The Ravening Haunts are always insane even if they have not 
formed a Mockery (avatar). These spirits are essentially immortal though they do lose a Will Force a year and can eventually 
starve. 
Climate/Habitat: Plane of Dreams, Plane of Shadows and rarely other planes. 
Body Type: Special (each of the parts below, and the whole connected place cannot be more than 1000’ feet in any one 
direction.)
Notes: They have very large Will reservoirs (1000 points), and their parts and powers are based off the size of the current 
Will Force stored within.

Ravening Haunt Stomach (Supernatural, Magical)
This represents a single, enclosed, special section of the Haunt. This is where victims the Haunt is tired of toying with are 
discarded and slowly decay. There is always a separate exit (from the stomach) similar to a Haunt Exit but destroying it and 
breaking through only allows escape from the stomach (not the Haunt). Those within are subject to a constant nightmare 
poison gas that is invisible and odorless and requires a Poison Resistance every 10 seconds. All victims must also make a 
Magic Resistance every 5 seconds or be permanently paralyzed. Also, every Will Force save failed due to fighting their fears 
from the nightmare poison also requires a Control Resistance or they suffer the loss of 1 Will Force. When victims reach 0 
Will Force they die and their bodies fade away, though their spirit echoes are stored within the stomach to someday become 
Haunt Masquerades as needed or desired. This area will regenerate on its own whether there is Will Force in the reservoir 
or not. If this area is destroyed all spirit echoes of victims, be they creatures or beings, are lost and the Haunt must begin 
collecting victims again before it is able to create Haunt grotesques and masquerades.

Ravening Haunt Mind (Supernatural, Magical)
This area will be something intricate or complex within the haunt. It will be a large object, like a magical clockwork, a 
curious tapestry, a weird steam machine, several trees deeply woven together, a rich painting, a relief map of the haunt, a 
strange puzzle room, etc. It represents the mind of the Haunt. If the haunt has no Mockery (avatar) then this is the only 
place where the haunt can direct other parts of itself to work in coordinated effort. If there is a mind, then it is able to 
directly coordinate all parts of itself including using telepathy to its grotesques (animals), and masquerades (beings), and 
mockery (avatar). The room this is found in, a Haunt Body, will not attack those within, except to keep them away from the 
mind by mental combat. It is the weakest part of the Haunt but will regenerate as long as the Stomach, Heart, or a Mockery 
(avatar) exists. It will attack by mental combat and has 20 Will Force always and never loses as it can always reset its Will 
Force by draining Will Force from the stomach if any are available in the Stomachs Will Reservoir up to 20.

Haunt Mockery (Humanoid)  (Supernatural, Magical Humanoid, Level/Title +4)
The highest forms of Ravening Haunts have avatar(s) in the form of a mockery. The macabre even has three of these at once. 
It is a deep copy of the original Dreamer who was the spirit echo of the Haunt. It has nearly all of that being’s memories, 
skills, and knowledge and powers, save those that are divine unless the deity involved allows it (some evil deities will). It is 
the master of the show, directing all that happens within the Haunt and will even toy with victims, meeting them, confusing 
them, or offering them help, etc. The avatar is merely a manifestation of the Haunt though and as insane and hungry as it 
is, and eventually succumbs to these desires. The avatar is susceptible to beings it remembers loving and may spare them 
despite its urges and madness.

Haunt Seed (Supernatural, Level 1)
When a Ravening Haunt dies, it leaves behind a useful magic item, that has one or two powers (see powers below). The form 
of the item might relate to the previous Haunt or it might just be a random object. It is glamoured to only appear to be that 
magic item and not what it truly is, a Ravening Haunt seed. The item is innocuous operating as a normal magic item right 
up until someone carrying it dies. Then the item breaks and a new Haunt is born somewhere in the dreamscape with the 
dead wielder as the template for the Haunt and eventual avatar. Thus, the cycle continues. 
Climate/Habitat: The dreamscape or wherever it is carried.
Attacks: 
The Haunt seed never attacks just piggybacks on the bearer’s death to project itself into the dreamscape and begin a new Haunt. 
Experience Value: 1,000 when destroyed (100 if avoided or discarded)
Abilities: Acts as a magic item as shown below. 
Powers: Life Sensing (constant.) 
Disabilities: Immobile.
Immunities: Illusion, Transformation of Form
Special Notes: The dead bearer is unaffected by the Haunt seed. The seed only activates as a seed when the bearer dies, making 
a spirit echo of the bearer (no resistance or save) and then breaking, as it projects its Haunt essence back into the dreamscape to 
start a new Haunt, of the youngest type. That Haunt will begin with Will Force equal to the dead bearer and grow from there as 
it consumes. 
Haunt Seed as a Magic Item
Form (Varies) either choose something original or an item that fits the previous haunt that died, such as a nice rope in a 
haunted mine, or a candelabra in a haunted mansion, or a walking stick in a haunted wood, etc.
Base Aura: Matches the Aura of the last Mockery (avatar) of the previous Haunt but must be at least 5. 
Abilities: Glamour (constant, only appears to be a magic item, hiding the special ability and its haunt seed essence.)
Special Ability: Item breaks, a Spirit Echo of the dead bearer is created and the essence of the item planeshifts to the 
dreamscape starting a new haunt of the youngest type, with Aura equal to the dead bearer. No resistance or save. 
Power(s): 5 Seconds, activated by thought. No Aura required to activate.

Earth Elemental, Arch (Supernatural, Level 12)
Earth Elementals fall in two groups, order (the Kraga) and chaos (the Graka). Arch Earth Elementals are strong members 
of their factions. They have risen above the general fray and fight as champions for their cause. They are True Neutral with 
order or chaos tendencies.
Habits/Life Cycle: They can live indefinitely and do not age. Earth Elementals do not breathe or have normal bodily 
functions. They are magical beings. They lose 1 Endurance per day if they are not in contact with earth or rock. They 
reproduce by joining and losing part of themselves to make 1-2 Moundlings or small Earth Elementals. They do this very 
infrequently unless they are in times of strife. Moundlings grow based on need while in contact with any earth or rock and 
will be full-sized within a year.

Earth Whyll, Foottrap (Supernatural, Magical Plant, Level 3)
The Foottrap grows in soft planar earth fields generally in clumps of 10 to 30. Each plant grows in an 8 to 12-foot circle. 
Most of the plant grows below ground. When it is mature it sends tendrils towards the surface that dig away 3-foot cones 
of earth leaving hollows. A crystalline spike grows up in the center of these hollows from the plant’s root. Tendrils grow 
to the surface. Once there, the vines grow circular leaves that cover and camouflage the empty space at the top of the 
cone, disguising it and creating 3-foot traps with spikes in the center. When an unfortunate being or creature steps on 
the camouflage leaves, they plunge through, generally unto the spike. The tendrils grasp the foot or area that fell into the 
trap keeping them stuck on the spike. Their blood spills and the roots drink the nutrients. There are generally 6 to 8 of 
these spike cone traps radiating outward from the center of the plant. In the center there is a similar cone, but this one is 
twice as wide at 6 feet and leads to the maw of the plant which tries to consume any flesh that falls into the cone trap. The 
camouflaged leaves take a week to regrow after they are disturbed. The spikes take a month to regrow if they are broken off. 
The plant can only be killed by destroying the central pod that holds the maw and nervous system.

Fae, Boggart (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 2 [4])
The Boggart is a small, nearly insane, monkey-like animal. They have wide, expressive faces. Most resemble an upright, 
brown-furred, black-skinned, racoon with an overwide mouth. Boggarts are sometimes friendly when well-fed and kindly 
treated. Their hands and feet stick to everything because of their magical ability to adhere. They can be a nuisance and are 
known tricksters, stealing baubles and food from anyone they can. Still, the wise advise caution in dealing with Boggarts, 
especially when trying to recover pilfered items. When Boggarts are threatened or very annoyed, they go berserk, becoming 
extremely dangerous; growing to twice their normal size, small claws extending into talons, mouth becoming a maw that 
can open as wide as its face, and furry tail growing throwable, poisonous quills. They become quite aggressive, attacking 
fearlessly and in groups. In this form they are dangerous to all but the most hardened adventurers. They are immune to 
control whether berserk or not. Some sages say that Boggarts were the original creatures that Brownies, Leprechauns, and 
Gremlins evolved or were uplifted from. In the statistics noted here the normal values are followed by the berserk form of 
the Boggart in brackets [ ]. 
Habits/Life Cycle: These creatures are omnivores and will literally eat anything though they have a sweet tooth for fruit and 
sugary food.  The Boggart is a careful breeder because their emotional states can be dangerous even to each other. Therefore  
they are shy breeders, and many females avoid their kind during their yearly estrus cycle. Finally, when they do become 
sexually paired, they go even farther away from other Boggart and breed for two weeks. The female sneaks away from her 
mate and finds a hiding place where she enters hibernation for six weeks. She loses about 20% of her body fat during this 
time then awakens and gives live birth. She raises the young Boggart alone for another 6 weeks and then rejoins her Boggart 

===== PAGE 275 =====
269
troop with her offspring. Boggarts grow to their normal size in one year but take another year to reach full maturity and 
gain their Berserking abilities. Boggarts leave thankfully short lives of no more than 20 years.

Fae, Cutterfly (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 2)
The Cutterfly looks like a butterfly from a distance save its praying mantis-like forearms that are sharp cutters for a creature 
of its size. It has a maw that secretes acid and poison stinger tail. They generally do not attack humanoids as their preferred 
food is rotting wood and vegetable matter. The Fae cultivate them for this ability and use them in their orchards and fields to 
remove dead wood and diseased plants. Though they are insects, their body parts are fused and a close inspection shows a 
nearly humanoid body shape. Some even claim that lesser Fae, such as Fairies, were created from Cutterflies.
Habits/Life Cycle: Females lay clutches of 3d12 unfertilized eggs at the end of their 1 year of life; the male fertilizes them 
and also dies. Three weeks later the full-grown Cutterflies hatch, spread their wings, and begin their lives.

Fae, Gwegar (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 8)
The Gwegar is the shapeshifting larger cousin of the Gwe. It is smarter and can change into larger (and smaller) creatures: 
ranging in size from a mouse to an elephant. They can also use Evoke to assume up to 8 aspects of any other animals 
whether they are in their natural or shifted form. The natural form of the Gwegar is a large, ape-like creature with an 
expressive face, double joined at the hips and knees allowing it to scamper on its hands and feet or stand upright. This form 
has opposable thumbs that are calloused enough to run on. Once a year, they gather in a predetermined area to mate and 
share their experiences through a primitive dance and sign language.  They are sentient but low in intelligence, lacking a 
true culture, any form of writing, permanent dwellings or tool-making, though they will use tools created by others. They 
sometimes mimic humanoids especially when caught, hoping this will help them gain freedom. 
Habits/Life Cycle: The Gwegar is only fertile in its native form. The females are interested in mating once per year in the 
early spring after the first thaw.  It gives birth to a single, live young 8 months after fertilization. The young are born with the 
ability to shift and will follow their mother for the first 2 years of life. Gwegar mothers are very close to their offspring and 
protective of them. The pair remain secretive for the first year. It takes six years for the Gwegar offspring to reach maturity. 
The mother stays in contact with her young until maturity, but gives them more and more autonomy after the second year 
until they are completely on their own at six years. Gwegar are highly sought as both shape-shifting mounts and fighting 
companions. They can live up to 70 years.

Fae, Hartebeast (Supernatural, Magical Plant, level 5) 
Though these creatures bear a similar name to a type of antelope they are anything but. In their natural form they look like 
nothing more than an oddly-shaped bush with thick, knobby limbs. Yet when touched by a mature Fae being an affinity 
check is made. If the check is made, the Hartebeast awakens and assumes its final form, a magically-animated bush with 
hardened, wooden riding surface atop its central core and vine stirrup mounts. The rest of it shapes itself into a majestic 
riding beast with a beautiful, flowering mane and tail (though it can turn these inward to hide its coloration). The roots pull 
up and transform into hooves, and two branches form into the head, neck, and forequarters of the beast while the other 
becomes the hindquarters and tail. Their foliage surrounds these features to make the Hartebeast appear to be an elk-like, 
bushy mount. The “head” even forms dense, wooden, “antlers” that the creature can use for defense of its rider. As long 
as there is strong light (daylight, or bright magical light) it is fully animated and can serve any Fae it has an affinity for. In 
lower lighting conditions it slows to half its normal speed, losing all of its magical powers save animation and life sensing. In 
darkness or low light, it becomes torpid, and its hooves sink into any available soil. These creatures require a gallon of water 
per day and have many magical abilities that make them serve as superior riding beasts. These creatures connect through a 
light form of mental contact to those they have an affinity for. The Hartebeast can hear through its branches, sense life, and 
feel vibrations.  
Habits/Life Cycle: The Hartebeast is essentially a bush when not animated, and each is both a male and female of its species. 
During the spring, if it is allowed to be immobile for at least four hours a day in sunlight, it will flower and can either self-
pollenate or cross pollenate with others of its kind. In six weeks, pollenated flowers will become small, seed-bearing, fleshy 
fruit that grow over the next month to the size of an apricot, and the color of a cherry. The fruit of the Hartebeast tastes like 
blueberry mixed with plum. The fruit’s seeds will grow into Hartebeast bushes if planted in fertile, magical soil or watered

Fae, Hedgemog (Supernatural, Magical Humanoid, Level 4)
The Hedgemog are very social, Wild-one humanoid race that were raised up by seelie Fae. They appear to be capybara and 
guinea pig humanoids. Their heads and eye placement give them very wide fields of view and make them hard to surprise. 
They have a keen sense of danger and are mildly empathic with other humanoids and even animals. They can grant animals 
the ability to speak and are excellent at animal training, taming, and speaking to them directly. It is said, years after they 
reached true sentience, and through their own volition, they pledged their race’s service to the seelie court’s pursuit of order 
and law. Their service was reluctantly accepted by the seelie king. Ever since, they have been fearless defenders of seelie law 
and order. Thus, most members of this race serve seelie Fae directly or indirectly though none are forced to do so. Some go 
their own way and are relieved of their court oath. Nearly all Hedgemog are good. Most have tendencies of moral, order or 
both. 
Habits/Life Cycle: These wild-ones are mammalian and generally mate for life. They are only fertile once per year, gestate 
for 6 months, and then give live birth. Their offspring reach maturity in three years and live up to 50 years. 
Climate/Habitat: Fae, enchanted forests, and wherever they go in service of the

Fae, Xar'Vell/Cranium Spider (Supernatural, Magical Animal or Humanoid, Level X)
This medium-sized spider is an aberration created in the laboratories of either Shadow or Dark Elves. It is said these spiders 
were originally from the homeworld of the Xar’Xeth insectoids but they have since been widely modified. They have little 
web making ability, using it only when egg-laying. Even these strands are not very sticky or strong. Their size would make 
them seemingly less dangerous than their giant spider origins; however, they are far more insidious. They have been called 
Cranium Spiders because they have two probes below their mandibles that allow them to tap into humanoid brains. Their 
bite, while not particularly strong, secretes a virulent (-20% Poison Resistance) venom that causes instant paralysis. They 
then latch on to the paralyzed victim, seating their concave bodies backwards onto the victim’s head. They chew on the 
neck, opening up a wound just big enough to insert the two probes. These probes allow the Cranium Spider to achieve 
symbiosis with the victim with two merging to become a new creature. By the time the poison wears off in 1d4 hours+1, 
the transformation is complete and a new Xar’Vell has been created. The spider is now firmly clamped down on the victim’s 
head tightly with all eight legs. Its spider is head turned downward covering the probes. The original parasite cannot 
be removed without killing host, as the probes are connected to the brain stem where autonomic functions occur: like 
regulation of the heart, breathing, etc. 
The Cranium Spiders were likely meant to make subjects controllable by proxy. A dark Fae master would control the 
Cranium Spider and it in turn would latch on to a humanoid, take over its mind, and then allow control of the victim by way 
of the parasitic spider. It seems the experiment got away from them, literally and figuratively. The new hybrid creature not 
only breaks any control in place but is also extremely hard to control thereafter. These creatures have fled to many planes 
and are very dangerous. They can be found in many forms. Alone they can be dangerous, working together they are deadly, 
and in hive form they are nearly unstoppable. They consider all other life forms to be inferior food stock and nothing more. 
There are no good Xar’Vell. 
Habits/Life Cycle (by form): The original form of Cranium Spider reproduces just as spiders do (once, with 3d12 eggs 
before dying). They will live only five years if they are unable to find a sentient humanoid host. 
The Xar’Vell hybrids take many forms as they grow in the symbiosis depending, on the mental capabilities of the host. 
At first, they are near zombie-like, acting instinctively. These creatures are dangerous as the Cranium Spider’s thick shell 
protects the head and allows them to see both through the humanoid’s eyes and the spider’s eyes. They rub their body, 
especially the hands, in the poisonous secretions of the parasitic Cranium Spider. They use these to touch victims, paralyze 
then and then consume them alive, including their brains which also feeds the growing parasite. This form will last only 1-3 
months before transforming. These creatures are referred to as Xar’Vell Shell Heads.
After a 1-3 months their progression takes one of two forms. If the victim’s original mind was not strong enough (Mental 
attributes of 15 or less) then the parasite grows its mandibles and probes slowly, sliding its spider body down the victim’s 
back, over several days and meals. The original humanoid’s legs atrophy and the parasitic spider quickly grows to the size of 
a giant spider. The parasitic spider’s head and the lower torso of the victim merge until the new form is created. Half spider, 
half humanoid, these mature creatures regain the strong web weaving abilities of giant spiders. They grow mouth mandibles 
on their humanoid faces that allow them to bite and to inject a magical death poison. They also lose the need to feed on 
brain matter. These creatures can survive 50 years. These forms are referred to as Xar’Vell Spidataurs. 
After a 1-3 months, if the victim was mentally strong (average 16+ Mental attributes) then the Cranium Spider becomes less 
spider-like, molting its shell, its legs joining together in twos and become grasping tentacles, with the remains of the spider 
merging completely with the head. The head now looks more like that of an octopus or squid sitting atop a humanoid body 
than the spider it is based on. The head and tentacles are pale and ghastly-looking. The humanoid’s eyes are still present but 
the pupils are now star-shaped. The mouth has become a feeding maw. Only the rear spider’s eyes remain to betray its spider 
origins and are still useful for 360-degree vision. Their tentacles now secrete the paralysis poison of the old cranium spider 
They use these to paralyze their victims if they get too close. This new form gains strong mental abilities and an increasing 
appetite for brain matter and now spinal fluid. This form ages very slowly and can survive for over 200 years. These are 
referred to as Xar’Vell Mind Devourers. 
Finally, if the victim was especially mentally strong (average of 19+ Mental attributes) then after an indeterminate period 
of time, from 1 year to 100, the Mind Devourers body will atrophy away. The brain will grow in size and slowly be exposed, 
with only a thin layer of translucent flesh just covering the now massive brain. Four of the tentacles will grow in size to 
match the brain and four of them atrophy away. Eventually, the brain and the four tentacles detach from the useless body. It 
will move itself into some form of pool, where it must be bathed constantly in spinal fluid which it slowly sips to keep itself 
alive. These creatures become the mastermind of other mature Xar’Vell (Spidertaurs and Mind Devourers), and it creates a 
hive that then begins to steal humanoids to feed and sustain itself. This final form is ageless and can survive indefinitely. This 

===== PAGE 286 =====
280
form is referred to as a Xar’Vell Master Brain. 
Climate/Habitat: Created in Fae, though now spread to the many planes.

Ashman (Supernatural, Magical Humanoid, Level 12)
The Ashman is a dangerous and deceptive being. They have the ability to duplicate the form of any corpse that they have 
touched or killed themselves. If this form is destroyed, they revert to their ash form. They can also change to this form at 
any time. Ashmen can strike a being with an Ashen Touch which drains Will Force. They can also push their evanescent, 
ashen limbs into a being and then convert these to physical forms within a being’s body (unless they make a Magic 
Resistance) doing massive amounts of physical damage. It is said they are cursed beings destroyed in fire and reborn into 
an Ashman. Other’s claim they are an evil type of Formless. Both are possible. They hate physical beings and have their own 
evil agenda in infiltrating groups and escaping the Plane of Fire. 
Habits/Life Cycle: Their origins are a mystery. They reproduce only by converting others into Ashman. They do give off 
life force but the positive or negative aspect of their life force is shrouded, though they are not undead. They are essentially 
immortal unless destroyed. 
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Fire and sources of heat or fire linked to this plane.

Fire Wyrd, Emberfly (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 1)
This red and orange fly appears harmless and normally feeds on decaying plant and animal matter. However, after mating 
the female lays dozens (6d6) eggs on the hide, skin, and clothing of other creatures and humanoids. In 1-2 hours, the eggs 
begin a transformative process. They release a strong, magical acid (1d10 per 10 seconds if Magic Resistance fails) and melt 
their way into a being, pushing in with metallic-like egg hairs. Once inside, the eggs add heat to the acid release and begin 
doing 1d6 magical heat damage per 10 seconds if a second Magic Resistance fails. If the being becomes completely still the 
egg is triggered and breaks open. It releases the Emberfly larva that then begins to eat the flesh of the victim from the inside 
at 1-3 damage per minute. Initially, large amounts of water can neutralize the acid (and egg adhesion), and careful knifework 
can cut away the metallic-like egg hairs. Emberflies are found individually or in small groups of 3d4 when mating. 
Habits/Life Cycle: After females and males mate, the female 
lays small clutches of 6d6 sticky, fertilized eggs on a victim’s 
fur, hide, clothing, or armor. Soon both sexes grow lethargic 
and die. In 1-2 hours all eggs begin activating, releasing acid 
and the egg hairs begin pulling/pushing the egg into the 
victim. Once the being is still (assumed dead) the eggs hatch 
and the Emberfly larva consume the victim from within. In a 
week, they transform into Emberflies after wiggling their way 
to the surface of the victim. The entire Emberfly life cycle, 
from egg to death lasts 2 months.     
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Fire and sources of heat and 
fire linked to this plane.

Fire Wyrd, Fire Lion (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 12)
This creature’s skin is a deep-yellow with orange and red highlights, especially the mane of spikes around its head. It appears 
to be a huge, unusual lion. It has obsidian-like claws and spikes on its thrashing tail. The creature breathes fire and has a 
thunderous roar that is known to cause fear in those without strong will. Their bodies magically produce water, and so they 
do not need to drink. They are immune to fear and control. They can shake the ground with tremors once per day, and 
when three or more are gathered on an active volcano they can make it erupt by combining their tremor powers. It is said 
that they were once lions that were changed by an Ifrit wizard. Others claim that they were created by a magical mishap. 
Either way they are dangerous and powerful creatures. Who are also said to be as smart as apes with an affinity for those 
who revere nature: druids, shamans, rangers, and others. They have the ability to project and receive images of memories or 
desires as well as basic feelings. For these reasons, they are revered by many as nearly a spirit animal themselves. 
Habits/Life Cycle: The Fire Lions are found either as part of a pride or in a small family group. One male will have one or 
more mates and each pair produces 1-2 cubs every other year if they are healthy. Cubs are born 6 months after fertilization, 
and are cubs for a full year before reaching maturity. Male Fire Lions will push newly mature younger male Fire Lions to 
leave. They do this mentally and not through an act of aggression. When the females of a pride decide that the male lion 
is no longer fit, they will similarly drive him to leave the 
pride. Fire Lions can live up to 120 years.

Fire Whyll, Heat Moss (Supernatural, Magical Plant, Level 4)
This yellow-orange Fire Elemental plant usually grows on cooling magma. When the magma gets cold enough, the Heat 
Moss separates from the magma, with a small chemical reaction that flings it into the air where it uses capillary action to 
fold into a small, wing-like structure, wafting through the air with magical levitation. This continues until it senses warm 
spots below. Usually, this is magma, but sometimes it is a humanoid. It steers itself through the air toward the heat source 
with the same capillary action it used to form a wing. Right before it lands, it secretes a strong adhesive. It then attaches to 
the heat source,  drawing heat from it. If this is an unfortunate humanoid, they will generally freeze to death, even on the 
Plane of Fire as more and more heat is drawn from their body. When they drop to below the air temperature then the heat 
moss will again explode off of them doing even more damage. 
Habits/Life Cycle: Heat moss splits into two organisms whenever it gets too big to float (over a foot across). It is essentially 
immortal until killed. If it looses all heat for more than a year it dies.

magical in nature. When they speak there is a very mechanical nature to it as if the sound is being produced by the striking 
of various-sized metal tines. They are generally True Neutral in alignment, focused on the tasks they were created for. Those

Junk, Dybbuk, Lost Ghost (Supernatural, Level 10)
The Dybbuk is a dangerous, persistent, lost ghost without form. When the being who becomes a Dybbuk dies, it latches 
onto a small physical object from its life. The item would have had great value to the Dybbuk or be something that 
reminded it of someone it once loved. Many of these lost items end up on the Plane of Junk and so there are many Dybbuk 
there although they can be found anywhere humanoids live. They cannot be banished because they are focused on the 
special anchoring item. Banish does temporarily cast them back into their anchoring object if they are animating a figure. 
Most Dybbuk learn they can inhabit small statues, dolls, puppets and marionettes, and then tend to do this exclusively, 
usually hiding their anchoring item within their new figure host with the Mold power. They animate that figure, making it 
move even if it was formerly made of stone or wood. They are limited to small figures 3’6” (and under), but they can Size 
Change larger figures or smaller ones to be their ideal size of about 3 feet. They give supernatural Agility, Vitality, Strength, 
and speed to these figures, making them far more capable than they appear. If it is a statue that they have animated, it loses 
much of its hardness and physical properties to be become animated. They also tend to mold their chosen form to have 
teeth and claws not clearly visible but easy to use. Some of these hide their nature and appear to be a normal figure until 
they attack. Others make the figure look dangerous or menacing with a devil’s mask or skull face.
A few are never exposed to figures so end up haunting the area of their anchoring object in similar ways as a ghost, but one 
without form. They cannot both haunt and animate their chosen figures at the same time. Dybbuks are very difficult to 
eradicate. If they are animating a figure, then that figure must be destroyed, with no other figures nearby available for the 
Dybbuk to flee into. If the anchoring item is present and known, then that item must be destroyed. Only then can effects 
like Call of the Light be used. When the anchoring item is destroyed the Dybbuk converts into the appropriate-aged ghost,

Junk, Homunculus (Supernatural, Magical Humanoid, Level 4)
These small, humanoid constructs are made of wood, stone, clay, or even metal and are often the earliest creations of 
artificers, tinkers, or golem makers who go on to make stronger creatures. They are sometimes confused with puppets, 
dolls, or statuettes until they start moving. They are magically alive and aware though not the smartest beings. They make 
useful servants and are often found in such roles. They are retrievers, spies, messengers, and more to their masters. They 
see and hear magically. They have painted eyes that must be made with a magical dye or paint. They are usually True 
Neutral in alignment, unless they were enchanted by an involved creator. Some homunculi are formed with wings; these 
can fly through magical ability. Masterless homunculi are great tricksters. They have learned to recognize lost things and 
they will take these things and do weird and seemingly random acts with them. These include keeping items for a time 
and then placing them right back where they found it after an owner’s search so the owner finds it on a subsequent search 
and questions their own sanity. Another trick is the swapping of lost items between locations and owners. Someone might, 
for instance, reach into an old coat pocket they haven’t worn in ages and find someone else’s lost spy-glass instead of their 
missing key. 
Climate/Habitat: Any (Plane of Junk/Lost)
Body Type: Small (Humanoid)

Junk, Junk Skitter (Magical Animal, Level 6)
These pony-sized creatures are mecho-mechanical and have six legs, each ending in foldable spikes that can be locked for 
attack. They are driven by a magical series of propelled plates, gears, and rods in their torsos and controlled by a magical 
“brain” in their skulls. The copper rods in their necks passes this control into their torso engines. In this way, the Junk 
Skitter has the same vital areas of a normal animal. They do not require sustenance but have a metallic maw to damage 
opponents. Junk Skitters are extremely territorial. Generally, they serve Mechanos masters, but the masterless ones are 
the most dangerous because they will destroy anything that enters their territory, including other Junk Skitters. They vent 
mechanical heat generated from movement or combat out of fins on their back but cannot move quickly for more than an 
hour at a time without cooling down for 10 minutes. Once per night, they shutdown for 4 hours in a check and self-repair 
cycle that fixes damage portions of their body by magic.

Junk, Junkman (Supernatural, Magical Humanoid, Level 12)
The Junkman is an abomination, with the head of a living golem or Maginos being quickly separated from its body and 
placed on the torso of a Mechanos or automaton. It is then bathed in magical electricity, fusing the two together, creating 
a strange new creature. Some say this happens occasionally when these two forces are fighting hand-to-hand and the 

===== PAGE 319 =====
313
mechanical and magical bodies pile up. Others say it was an experiment gone horribly wrong. Either way, The Junkman is 
an amalgamated creature with the ability to graft any golem, Maginos, Mechanos, or automaton part to itself. It can also 
graft to machines like steam wagons, clockwork engines, combustion chambers, etc. It magically produces fuel and energy 
for any part which requires either. The Junkman repairs any grafted part of itself and is very difficult to kill. The head and 
torso(s) that were originally fused to create the creature have to be completely disintegrated, destroyed by acid, aura or 
plasma, or the largest section will repair itself and the rest of the attached parts. 
The Junkman is an insane creature. It hates everyone else just a little more than it hates itself and attacks nearly anything 
moving. It especially despises creatures of flesh and targets them first. Many Junkmen will remain still in a pile of refuse for 
hours, days, or longer and then burst forward to attack when they sense life around them, not satisfied until they no longer 
sense it. They also seek out parts to graft to themselves. It speaks only to mock others or curse its own existence.  
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Fire, and sources of heat and fire linked to this plane.

Junk, Monitor (Magical, Level 5)
When dormant these mecho-magical creatures appear as a magical brass sphere with eight irises: one large iris in the 
middle of one side, one smaller one below it, two smaller irises on the left and right sides (offset from the large iris) and 
two medium-sized ones slightly offset left and right beneath the orb just barely visible.  The underside has a large inverted 
hemi-spherical divot allowing the sphere to rest without rolling. There are various lines indicating hidden compartments 
on the opposite side of the large iris (back), two large ones higher up, and one small one below them. When the monitor 
is active, the large central iris opens and focuses a single, magical, crystal eye that can see normally or be focused to very 
far sight (100x normal human) or very close sight (100x microscopic). The small irises on either side for hearing. The 
smaller one below the main iris opens and fans outward to create a speaker/mouth. The medium lower irises open to 
reveal two articulated, telescoping, tentacle-like arms that end in four finger/thumb prongs that are offset with each other, 
allowing subtle manipulation. The two, larger, back compartments open up and two fan wings extend and unfurl. The last 
compartment is only opened by Junk Monitors with masters. An established master can request the third compartment be 
opened or it becomes sign of trust in a new master when the Junk Monitor voluntarily opens the last compartment for the 
first time. Within are revealed a tiny pair of articulated brass gauntlets. One is attached by chain to a monocle and the other 
to an ear piece. These are very small, no more than inches across while in the compartment, appearing that only a fairy or 
small creature could use them. They grow in size once removed to match their master. The gauntlets, monocle, and ear piece 
allow the master to directly control the monitor when it is not in autonomous mode. 
Physical contact with the sphere causes it to wake up. If it masterless, it will imprint on the first being to make physical 
contact with it. If it has a master, once awake it will rejoin its master. They are generally not aggressive creatures unless 
forced to be so by their masters. The monitor may not immediately understand the new master if it doesn’t understand the 
language, it will follow hand gestures and listen to the new master until it learns the language through Language Lore. If it 
already has a full set of languages,  it will discard the least used one (though never the Junk Monitor’s original language) to 
learn the new master’s language. These creatures can levitate, fly, and perform several magical scanning functions. The Junk 
Monitor is a curious being that tries to be useful and can perform many tasks. 
Climate/Habitat: Any (Plane of Junk/Lost)
Body Type: Medium Sphere (x2) with 2 arms (x1), 2 hands (x1/2) and wings (x1) (these 
appendages can be stored inside itself,)

Life Elemental, Alpha (Supernatural, Level 15)
The order (the Harisha) and chaos (the Arisha) Life Elementals are led by their alphas. They lead their lesser in most 
matters, only the Prime overrules them. They are extremely powerful Life Elementals that represent the best and strongest 
values of their beings. They are True Neutral with order or chaos tendencies.
Habits/Life Cycle: They can live indefinitely and do not age. Life Elementals do not breathe or have normal bodily 
functions. They are magical beings. They lose 1 Endurance per day if they are not in contact with a living thing or in a 
verdant area. They reproduce by joining and losing part of themselves to make 1-2 Enkindlers or small Life Elementals. 
They do this very infrequently unless they are in times of strife. Enkindlers grow based on need while in contact with any 
life-filled environment, growing to full size in a year.

Life, Incarnator (Supernatural, Magical Humanoid, Level 12)
An Incarnator is a spirit-form humanoid being. On the Plane of Life and Light they appear as luminous beings, glowing 
from within. Sometimes their lights are dimmer or intermittent, and sometimes they glow brightly. They spend most of 
their time in the Plane of Life tending to the unborn. When outside the plane they have either a shadow form for Evil 
Incarnators or a phaseable one for Good or Neutral. Each of them helps newly merged souls and spirits gain a sound 
pre-mind and pre-body to prepare them for what they will be in life. Mostly this involves coaching the spirit and soul into 
moving into an illusionary image of their body and mind as it will be. Most of the time this is a natural process. The spirit 
and soul are a good pairing and the pre-mind and pre-body images form correctly. Sometimes the pairing is strained and 
then the Incarnator has a difficult job. Spirits come in many forms, sizes, and intensities, but the soul they are paired with is 
an eternal manifestation of divine agency that changes slowly if it all. So, you may have a willful soul and a mercurial spirit 
or a somber soul and a joyful spirit. Such matches are rare and how an Incarnator deals with this depends on their outlook. 
An Evil Incarnator may just force them together and implant the knowledge in their pre-mind that life will be hard and 
that’s fate. A Good Incarnator will coax the spirit and soul to practice working together in their pre-mind and pre-soul by 
using their differences to be a strength. The Incarnator explains that challenges are a gift and the soul will grow stronger 
from having a difficult spirit pairing. A Neutral Incarnator may do some of both. Whatever work they do in the Plane of Life 
there are still issues, sometimes serious ones, after incarnation. 
When the pre-born makes the final leap into the light at the bottom of the Plane of Life (some say they were pushed by 
impatient and possibly Evil Incarnators) then their illusionary pre-mind and pre-body image will be stripped away and 
they will be born into a physical body. Rarely this loss of illusionary self doesn’t take well. Some think this is because the 
Incarnator failed to properly prepare the spirit-soul pairing to be born. In these cases, the Incarnator has to go repair the 
damaged pairing before something terrible happens. They go to whatever plane or place the being was born on, and they 
continue their efforts with the confused spirit-soul to get adjusted to their real body-mind. Some mortals claim this is why 
some babies are colicky and why some die inexplicably. The Incarnator stays with the being until either the meshing occurs 
and the new being begins to thrive or the pairing fails and the newborn dies in a way inexplicable to most mortals. Though 
tragic, this outcome is not as bad as the one where the Incarnator has failed so completely that the spirit-soul fusing breaks 
at the moment of incarnation and the soul rejects the whole endeavor, leaving a spirit to run the new body and mind. These 
rare births are incredibly dangerous.  Anything or nothing could replace the soul in the child. In the best case, a Formless 
might take up residence there and replace a badly matched spirit and mind. In the worst case, a demon could inhabit where 
the soul should be. A being without a soul is not supposed to occur. Incarnators that fail may find that themselves cast out of 
the Plane of Life, losing their powers and/or dying. 
Habits/Life Cycle: The origin of the first Incarnators is a mystery. Some claim they were failed angels or weakened devils 
waiting to be caretakers and influencers. It is now believed that new Incarnators are chosen from the recently dead. Some 

===== PAGE 329 =====
323
say it is those that have guided or led effectively in life. If they have done so to the benefit of many, they may become Good 
Incarnators. If they have done so to enrich themselves, then they become Evil-aligned Incarnators. Most are a little of 
both. Incarnators who can guide well benefit themselves as much as those they influence. Some Incarnators grow weary of 
guidance, they lose their way, and this is very dangerous to the unborn and newborn alike, as the failure of an Incarnator 
can precipitate a soulless child. One day they simply succumb and throw themselves into the incarnation light at the bottom 
of the Plane of Life. It is unknown if this kills them. Alternatively, it could strip off their spirit, mind, and spiritual body, 
returning the soul and spirit separately to the life pool at the top of the Plane of Life. Lastly, it is possible they are simply 
reborn. It is known that some pre- Incarnators come to watch the Incarnators work. Some say these are infusers that grew 
up and others think they come from outside the plane, as mortals, or devils, devas, or angels that gave up that life or possibly 
even never-born beings who choose instead to be an Incarnator. The Incarnators allow these others to watch until they sense 
they are ready to guide the pre-born. Eventually the watching spirits are allowed to work with the Incarnators on the pre-
born until the watchers are ready to work alone, finally becoming true Incarnators.

Life, Infuser (Supernatural, Magical Humanoid, Level 9)
An Infuser is a diminutive, spirit-form humanoid being. They inhabit and perform their duties in the Plane of Life and 
Light. They are short, appearing insubstantial and luminous, with no mouths but expressive eyes. The light coming from 
their hands outshines that coming from within the rest of their small, 3’6” on average, spirit bodies. Those hands have spirit 
adherence and can touch living things and spiritual ones alike. They are natural healers and no other has quite the empathy 
that these beings possess. Their job is to prepare animal spirits for the life they will lead by creating for them illusory bodies 
and showing them what it will be to inhabit them. They fix mystical problems these animal spirits have but accept that not 
all problems are treatable. They are shepherds for animal spirits and many have their specialties, choosing one animal type 
or another to care for and prepare. They are sentient but not overly bright, with their Wisdom being stronger than their 
Intelligence or Knowledge. They are generally Neutral preferring to side with the animals in matters of good and evil.  They 
sometimes venture out into other planes to correct spiritual problems with animals that are not adapting well to their new 
lives. When they are outside the Plane of Life, they can end up assisting more than just the animals they nurture. It is their 
nature to help and there are few greater healers than an infuser. 
Habits/Life Cycle: The origin of the Infusers is unknown. There are those that believe they were helpers who aided the 
creator in making the various original animals and settled in the Plane of Life and Light to guide them through the ages. 
Some claim they are failed Devas, who chose animals over sentients. They seem boundless in their empathy, but occasionally 
one tires and is seen to jump into the incarnation point at the bottom of the Plane of Life. What happens thereafter is one of 
the great mysteries. Perhaps they are reborn, or they release their soul and the spirit goes on to become one of the animals 
they have cared for, for so long. Either way, their numbers diminish and yet new Infusers appear, whether climbing from the 
pool of life or coming from one of the walls, as if they ported in. Those that come have no knowledge of what came before, 
only a desire to help, which they begin immediately doing. 
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Life and sometimes where new animals are born.

Life Wyrd, Psychoworm (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 5)
This translucent worm is about 3-feet long and has two eye-pits that it sees and senses life through. It can fly, though slowly, 
swimming through the air with Levitate and a weak, limited magical flight. They can make themselves invisible at need. It 
can Mind Dance and senses those in fear, terror, under the effects of any insanity, or mental instability. These worms are 
not harmful in the short-term but their use can be drug-like. They feed off of the negative mental problems of creatures, 

===== PAGE 332 =====
326
elevating but not curing their symptoms. They are warm to the touch, and anyone who makes contact with them finds 
their pleasure centers stimulated, feeling joy and even euphoria. Once in contact with a being, these creatures will drape 
themselves on the heads or necks of the beings and extend either end of their bodies to the ears. There they will begin mind 
dancing on their host, causing weird, phosphorous vapors to leave the ears of the being they are near. These vapors are a 
physical manifestation of the negative mental effects and the Psychoworm feeds directly off of these vapors, drawing them 
in through the ends of its body. The host creature will no longer feel the effects of these symptoms. If fearful or anxious, they 
will become calm. If angry, they will relax. Also, the effects of insanity abate completely. The worms are very useful in the 
short-term, but in most normal creatures, the worm eventually runs out of things to feed on and begins taking away normal 
pain. This can cause the being to further injure themselves, as they cannot feel anything harmful. They also become mentally 
numb or uncaring when facing emotional pain. Their use is addictive, and very drug-like, and if the being thinks about 
removing them, they induce joy and euphoria from their touch making it hard to do so. If the worm is placed on someone 
who is insane, it will only feed off the derangement, and thus is fully mutually beneficially for the parasite and its host. 
Habits/Life Cycle: These creatures are hermaphrodites. They can mate as often as once a year if they have fed well. They 
produce 1d12 eggs which they lay in a small place, generally in a corner or someplace likely to be unseen near where 
humanoids populate. They are most common on the Plane of Life, where they are used in short-term sessions by Incarnators 
and sometimes Infusers who are having a tough time dealing with unruly preborns. A Psychoworm lives 1d12 years outside 
of a host, but once they are with a host they will last as long as the host does. 
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Life.

Life Whyll, Sustasphere (Supernatural, Magical Plant, Level 2)
This elemental life plant looks like a small, glowing tennis ball in size and shape. It is warm to the touch and floats through 
levitation. It feeds off of stray bits of life culled away from Life Elementals, Infusers and Incarnators doing their work on 
the preborn spirits and spirit-souls. These plants are left alone as nearly all of the denizens of the Plane of Light and Life 
do not require sustenance. The interior of this floating, fruit-like fungi is sweet while the skin, minus the spores, tastes like 
bean curd. Most of those that eat these scrap off the hair-like spores which can be bitter tasting, thus improving the odds 
that this fungi reproduces. Most beings consider these a delicacy, and they are highly sought after for their taste and healing 
properties. 
Habits/Life Cycle: The translucent. furry outer skin is hairy because each of the hairs is a spore. When a Sustasphere is 
consumed or dies some of these spores are released. Some of these find a discarded source of life to latch on to and grow. In 
2 to 8 weeks a new Sustasphere grows from the spore. A Sustasphere can live for 10-20 years in a verdant area. Some of them 
escape the Plane of Life through portals or gateways, but they cannot reproduce outside of the plane. They can thrive for 
years in a rich environment such as a forest. After 1-2 weeks outside the Plane of Life, they stop glowing and the spores die. 
The Sustasphere then goes from translucence to a dull opaque gray. 
Climate/Habitat: The Plane of Life and verdant places connected to it. 
Body Type: Tiny (sphere x1 area, per plant)

Order, Borer (Supernatural, Magical Animal, Level 3)
Description: The Borer is a type of Crystorinn (crystal animal) and crystalvore that survives on crystal plants and natural

their body. They have a tongue that looks much like a drill bit and they can open their three-part maw flat against their face, 
revealing rasping crystal teeth. They also secrete a magical acid which dissolves non-crystalized matter. With their face, 
tongue, and secretions they are the fastest diggers around. When not digging, they can magically swim through earth and 
stone to get to the quartz they prize. They extract these digging around them and then scrapping away the last bit of material 
with their crystal claws.

the parents, each raises one.  If there is a third

surrounding crystals immediately and require 
no sustenance from the mother. Parents show 
teach offspring how to find the richest crystals 
and how to socialize with other Borers. They are 
fearful of predators, especially Crush Stalkers. 
Their favorite food is quartz and they can be

Order, Mender (Supernatural, Slime, Level 7)
The Mender is one of the few creatures of Order that doesn’t have a crystal body and isn’t a Crystorinn. They are very soft, 
translucent, blob-like beings that look like naked, sexless humanoids though their facial features are missing save for eyes 
that are twin sources of soft illumination with a colorful center. They also have two ears which are concave patches roughly 
ear shaped. Their skin glows slightly and is warm to the touch. The Mender has no bones and maintains it shape through 
its magical skin. Despite their appearance, they are actually slimes. They move by adhering to surfaces with their feet 
and pulling themselves along. They can also blink and teleport as needed. These creatures appear a little creepy, but their 
warmth, glow, and generally slow movement around living things alleviates this somewhat.  Their origins are a true mystery. 
Many scholars have studied them and their childlike intellect that is just below humanoid average. However, they came to 
be, they seek out those who have wounds or are suffering ailments which they mend, thus the name. They are sought after 
for healing but are immune to all forms of control and mental contact, even those that target slimes. A Mender appears, 
aids the stricken, and leaves without words. Their abilities and powers appear to be divinely given though by which deity or 
deities is unknown. 
Habits/Life Cycle: The Mender’s life cycle was a great mystery until some unscrupulous and cruel researcher kept one in 
captivity, in a magical cage from which it could not teleport away. Even after almost a hundred years it still healed every 
wounded or sick animal and being that was placed in its environment. Eventually, it was observed that Menders began to 
lose the ability to heal as they approach a hundred years. Then the entire body loses its shape, collapsing into a puddle. The 
internal light which seems to be its mind spreads to the opposite ends of the blob. The eyes and ears split, one going to each 
side of the blob. Slowly it divides into two creatures who appear to be full, adult Menders in hours, growing new parts (eyes, 
ears, etc.), and taking humanoid shape again. It is said that after the researcher died, that his daughter freed the two new 
Menders and before teleporting away one healed an undiagnosed disease that would have eventually led to the heir’s death.
